title: Help tells owners a payment link puts money in their account, but payment links are in test mode for every gym
what: The live help article on online payments tells every owner to paste their Razorpay or Cashfree keys, make a payment link, and that the money goes straight to their account. The payments switch in the repo is off, and while it is off every payment-company connection is test mode: no real money moves. The article mentions test mode only as a side note, not as the state of every gym today.
expected: The help says payment links take real money only when that is true, or the payment-link part of the article waits for the switch like the join-and-pay article does. The UPI QR part can stay.
who: owners who read the help or ask the AI help about online payments
how_often: every time, while payments stay in test mode
fix_line: Hold the payment-link half of the article behind the live-payments switch, or say plainly that payment links are in test mode for now

title: Help says member messages are deleted after 180 days, but they are only deleted when someone next opens the list
what: The help tells owners that member messages are deleted 180 days after the last one. No timed job does this. Old messages are removed only at the moment the member opens their messages or someone at the gym opens Member messages. If nobody opens either, the old messages stay.
expected: Messages older than 180 days are removed on a schedule, whoever opens the app, or the help says what really happens.
who: members and owners of a gym where nobody opens the messages for a while
how_often: only at gyms that stop opening messages
fix_line: Add the 180-day clean-up to a daily job (database change, needs his yes), or soften the help line

title: A help library is named in the notes but not found in code
what: The notes at the top of the help articles say the articles feed two things: the AI help answers and the help library. Only the AI answer and the no-AI help-page answer read the articles. No screen in the admin app, the member app or HQ lets a person browse the help pages.
expected: A help library people can browse exists, or the notes stop naming one.
fix_line: Decide: build a browse-the-help page, or remove the words from the notes

title: Staff help names a question and choices that are not on the Add a person form
what: The help says to pick Owner or Staff under a question called What can they do. The form really asks What is their job, with four choices: Owner, Staff (front desk), Trainer and Other. The help also says the sign-in code works for a few minutes; the screen says 30 minutes.
expected: The help uses the words on the form and names all four choices, including Trainer.
who: owners adding staff or a trainer
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Rewrite the step with the real question, the four choices and 30 minutes

title: Diet plan help names a button that does not exist
what: The help says to tap Start from a sample when making a diet plan. The button on the screen reads Start from a ready-made plan. The AI Assistant itself tells owners to start from a ready plan.
expected: The help names the button as it is written on the screen.
who: owners and trainers making a diet plan
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Change the help words to Start from a ready-made plan

title: Your growth help says old numbers can be typed in, but the button opens the Excel import
what: The help says to use Add old records to type your old numbers. The button opens the import page, which takes an Excel or CSV file of old members and fee records; nothing is typed. The button also shows only while the gym has no older records, which the help does not say.
expected: The help says Add old records brings in an Excel or CSV file, and that the button goes away once old records are in.
who: owners comparing with the time before MettleUp
how_often: every time they follow the help
fix_line: Reword the step: Add old records opens Import from Excel

title: No automatic check that the buttons named in help exist on the screens
what: The help file's own rule is never to name a button that is not in the code, checked by hand on 4 Nov 2026. The test file checks ids, length, banned words and that every screen has an article, but compares button names with the screens for the messaging articles only. Three articles have already drifted (staff, diet plans, Your growth).
expected: A test fails when a quoted button or label in a help article is not found in the screen code.
who: anyone reading help or an AI help answer after a screen's words change
how_often: each time a screen is reworded
fix_line: Add a test that searches the app code for every quoted label in the help articles

what: The backlog marks "Steps and water each day" as Live. The app shows today's steps from Health Connect. No water tap was found anywhere in the member app; the same backlog row admits the water tap is not built.

title: Backlog says Google Drive backup and automatic Drive backup are live, but both were stopped
what: The backlog marks "Google Drive backup and restore" and "Automatic workout backup" as Live, with a "Back up to Google Drive" row in Settings. Since 4 Nov the app no longer backs up to Google Drive: the upload code is still there but no screen calls it, and a phone with Drive linked is told that backups now go to the MettleUp account. Only bringing back an old Drive backup remains.
expected: The backlog says backups go to the MettleUp account and that Drive is restore-only, so no public text is written from the old rows.

The phone part is in the app, but it needs a database change that is marked not live and waits for the owner's yes. Until then members who joined before 23 Oct still share workouts only from the update day, so their trainers' charts stay short.
expected: The row says Waiting for you until the database change is live, or the change is applied.
fix_line: Say yes to the database change, or mark the row Waiting for you

title: Backlog says phone-number sign-in is switched off, but it is switched on in the app code

In the code the switch is on, with a note that the owner approved it on 15 Nov and that the server change and privacy line are live. The backlog row is out of date, so anyone reading it gets the wrong state.
expected: The backlog row says the switch is on from the next phone release and names the approval.
who: the owner and anyone planning from the backlog
fix_line: Update the backlog row to say the sign-in is on

title: Switched-off "Muscles ready today" and "Quick workout" screens are still in the app with no gate
what: The backlog says both were switched off on 5 Nov and only the code is kept. The card is gone from the Workout tab, but the two screens themselves have no check, unlike the Plus pages, which go straight back when Plus is off. A link to either screen may still open it (not driven, read in code only). The feature list also marks them live.
expected: A switched-off screen cannot be opened by any route, and the feature list marks it hidden.
who: members who open an old link

title: Notes say the admin app runs only its own scripts, but one outside script is allowed
what: The task list says the admin app "runs only its own scripts and talks only to the gym server". The security rule the admin app is served with also allows a Cloudflare analytics script and talks to Cloudflare's analytics address and to the app website.
expected: The note matches the rule, or the rule allows only what the note says.
fix_line: Correct the note, or drop the outside analytics script

title: The owner's inbox page and its feature backlog are missing from the feature list

expected: Every tool the owner uses has a row in the feature list, with its checks.
how_often: every time he opens the page

title: Teen accounts were decided for before the public launch, but none exist
what: On 24 Oct the owner decided: 18 and above for the trial, and teen accounts with a parent's OK built before the public launch. A later entry of 14 Nov says the app is live. A search of the member app, the admin app, the server and the database changes found no parent step and no teen flag. Today the app only asks every person to tick that they are 18 or older.
expected: Teen accounts exist before the app is public, or the decision is changed and written down.
who: gym members aged 13 to 17 and their gyms
how_often: every teen who wants to join
fix_line: Owner decides: build teen accounts now, or keep 18 and above and record that

title: The note says the small trial fee is built, but a trial can only be free
what: The owner picked a small trial fee (for example Rs 199 for 7 days), taken off the plan when the person joins, and the note says it was built with the free trial. In the code the trial fee is always zero and the owner's trial card offers only Off, 1, 3 or 7 free days. The fee waits for online joining payments, which are switched off. This is an inside note; no gym is told the fee exists.
expected: The owner can set a trial fee, or the note says the fee is not built yet.
who: gym owners who want a paid trial
fix_line: Correct the note to say the trial fee waits for online joining payments

title: The busy machines tip was promised with a one-tap move, but it only has Not now
what: The owner was told a member would see a line such as Leg day is quieter on Tuesday, with Move it, where one tap moves the routine to the quieter day. The card in the member app shows the line and one button, Not now, which hides it for 30 days. There is no button that moves the routine. This is an inside note; members were not promised the move.
expected: The tip has a Move it button, or the owner knows it is advice only.
who: members of a gym with busy machines on
fix_line: Add a Move it button to the tip, or tell the owner the tip is advice only

title: The backlog still says workouts never go to our server, but a copy does

The same row adds that this changes once the server copy is switched on, and other entries say that happened in late October. In the code, for a member signed in with Google, every saved workout, body weight, measurements and the profile are copied to the server. The row was never updated.
expected: The backlog says plainly that signed-in members' workouts are kept on the server, readable only by them.
who: the owner, and anyone he repeats the line to
how_often: every time the row is read
fix_line: Rewrite the backlog row to say what is copied to the server and for whom

The key is not in the public code, so that half is true; the word only is not.
expected: The row says the key is on the PC and also stored as a private build secret.
how_often: every time the row is read

title: Notes say register photos come later for the AI import; nothing reads a photo

expected: HQ can export one gym's data, or the plan says the gym downloads its own backup instead.

title: Website says our staff cannot open a member list unless the gym lets them in, but HQ can open it in an emergency

title: Desk still has Check workout code, but the member app no longer shows a code

title: Notes say Google Drive stays as an extra copy for people who want one; the app can no longer back up to Drive

who: members who want their own copy

title: Notes say the free limits can be switched on from HQ with no app update; the switch is built into the app

The paid-features switch is a fixed value inside the app, so turning it on needs a new app version. The limits also differ: no limit on the number of routines was found.
expected: The switch can be flipped from HQ, or the notes say a release is needed and list the real limits.

title: HQ plan says it shows app versions; the card says not connected yet

expected: The card shows which versions members run, or it is removed until it can.

title: Notes say nothing locks when a free trial ends; a staged lock is built behind a switch that is off
what: The free-trial decision says: when a trial ends, nothing locks. That is true today. The admin app also holds a built stop-paying path (7 extra days, then 30 days of basics only with no new members, then look and download only) that also covers a trial that ended. It is behind the plan switch, which is off. The trial banner's own notes still say nothing is ever locked.
expected: One rule for what happens after a trial ends, written the same in the notes, the banner and the lock.
how_often: once the plan switch goes on
fix_line: Decide the rule before the switch goes on and align the banner words with it

title: Notes say feedback can be typed or spoken in both apps; the admin app only takes typing
what: The feedback plan says a Send feedback button in the member app and the admin app, type or speak. The member app has speak. The admin app's Help and feedback page has a typing box only; speaking exists there only inside the AI Assistant.
expected: The admin app's feedback takes voice too, or the plan says typing only for owners.
fix_line: Add the speak button to the admin feedback box or drop it from the plan

title: The backlog calls a location check at the QR scan worth building, but nothing of it exists
what: The note of 29 Oct says a fixed QR poster lets a member check in from anywhere, and answers that a one-time location check (within about 150 m of a pin the owner drops) is worth it and takes 2 to 3 days. No pin, no location permission and no at-the-gym mark were found in the member app, the admin app or the gym server. So a photo of the poster still earns challenge days and workout-offer rewards from home.
expected: Either the location check is built, or the note says it is parked and why, and challenge rewards are known to rest on the plain QR.
who: gym owners who give rewards for visits
how_often: every check-in made away from the gym
fix_line: Decide: build the location check for reward check-ins, or park it in writing

title: Class booking is on the backlog as waiting for the gym visit, and is still not built
what: The backlog lists class booking (timetable, spaces left, book and cancel) as a gap against the gym's old software, waiting for the question "Do you run group classes?". Only one-to-one personal-training booking exists, and that sits behind a server part. No group class timetable or booking was found on any surface.
expected: The gym visit question is answered and class booking is either planned or dropped in writing.
how_often: every time such a gym compares us with its old software
fix_line: Ask the gym the group-class question, then plan or drop class booking

title: The price decision still lists a Pro + AI pack that the product has since retired

The shared pack list now says that pack was retired on 12 Nov and replaced by AI credits on every plan; nothing sells or shows it. The decision note was never corrected, so anyone reading it gets a price list that no longer exists.
expected: The price decision names only what is sold today: Starter, Pro, AI credits, the founding offer.
who: the owner and anyone pricing from the note
how_often: every time the note is read
fix_line: Add one line to the price decision saying Pro + AI became AI credits on 12 Nov

title: The switching offer in the price plan (pay nothing until the old software's year ends) is nowhere on the website
what: The price plan the owner picked includes an offer for gyms moving from their old software: free move of records, set-up in person, and no payment until their paid year ends, up to 6 months. The website's price section only says 3 free months for everyone and half price for extra branches. No switching offer, and no way in HQ to give a longer free period by offer, was found in the price list code.
expected: The offer is on the website and the sales material, or the note says it was dropped.
who: gym owners who already paid another software for the year
fix_line: Decide if the switching offer still stands; if yes, add it to the price section

title: Online acceptance of the terms is live, but its own server file still says it was never switched on
what: The backlog says owners accept the terms with a tick box at Create my gym, live on the server since 24 Oct. The live database does have the two functions that keep and read an acceptance (checked in the function list today). The server file that made them still opens with the words NOT APPLIED, needs the owner's yes, and the feature list carries it as unknown because of that line.
expected: The file's first line says when it went live, like the other live server parts.
who: anyone deciding what is live from the server files
how_often: every time the file is read
fix_line: Change the first line of the terms server file to say it is live since 24 Oct

title: The complaints contact was promised in both apps, but the member app shows no way to reach it after joining
what: The launch task says the named contact for data complaints goes into the privacy notice and both apps. In the member app the privacy notice is linked only inside the tick box shown once at sign-in or when joining a gym. Settings and About show credits and the version only: no privacy notice, no terms, no contact address. A member who wants to complain about their data later has nowhere in the app to find who to write to.
expected: Settings or About in the member app has a Privacy and terms row that shows the contact name and address.
how_often: every time a member looks for the privacy notice or the complaints contact
fix_line: Add a Privacy and terms row with the contact to the member app's About page

title: The data agreement says every look at a gym's records is recorded and shown in the admin app, but direct database looks are not shown and may not be recorded
what: The data agreement for gyms and the MettleUp access card both tell the owner that every look is recorded and listed in the admin app. The admin app lists only looks made through a support window. Looks made straight in the database with the owner login are sent by the server in a separate list that the admin app never reads or shows. The notes say this list is not built, that the recording stays off until a logs key is saved in HQ, and that a look made with the server key is never recorded at all.
expected: Every kind of look is recorded and the owner can see it in the admin app, or the agreement and the card say exactly which looks are listed.
who: every gym owner who accepted the data agreement
how_often: every direct look at gym data

title: The admin app says a member gets the automatic birthday wish when the member's phone may never show it
what: With the automatic birthday wish on, the AI Assistant and Today stop asking the owner to wish a member whose mobile number and first name match an app member, and say that member gets the wish at 9:30 am. The wish is a notification the member's own phone sets for itself. It does not show when the member turned off reminders from the gym, has notifications off, or has not opened the app lately. The notes also name an older case: a number that was typed but never proven counts as wished in the admin app while the server refuses it. In all these cases nobody wishes the member.
expected: The admin app counts a member as wished only when the wish will really reach them, or the words say the wish is set on the member's phone and may be switched off there.
who: members with a birthday whose phone has gym reminders or notifications off, and their gym owner
how_often: each birthday of such a member
fix_line: Soften the admin app words to say the wish is set on the member's phone, or have the phone tell the server whether gym reminders are on

title: What's new tells members silent gym messages and Rest is over now make a sound, but this was never proven on a real phone of that kind
what: The 0.79.0 What's new line says that on some phones gym messages and Rest is over made no sound and now they do. The notes say the ring was not proven on the owner's OPPO, the only phone known to have the fault; the cloud test phone keeps its sounds, so it proves only that nothing rings twice. The notes also say the buzz and the pop-up banner are still missing on those phones. The line is live in open testing.
expected: The line is shown only after the ring is heard on a real phone that had the fault, and it does not suggest the buzz or the pop-up came back.
who: members on OPPO and OnePlus phones
how_often: every gym message and every rest end on those phones, if the fix does not work there
fix_line: Test a gym reply and a locked-screen rest end on the owner's OPPO with 0.79.0 before production; drop the line if it stays silent

title: Dragging an exercise up in a live workout sometimes drops it at the bottom of the list
what: In the release test rounds for 0.79.0, on the owner-size test phone, an exercise held and dragged up above another one landed at the bottom of the list in 2 of 5 runs. The notes call it an open app question with no cause found and say it looks new in 0.79.0. The suspected part is the rule that moves the held card by the gap between where the list is scrolled and where it should be. 0.79.0 went to open testing with this open.
expected: A dragged exercise lands where the finger lets go, every time.
who: members who reorder exercises during a workout
how_often: about 2 in 5 drags on the owner-size test phone; unknown on real phones
fix_line: Reproduce on a phone of the owner's size, log the scroll and the held card's shift at the drop, then fix the drop place

title: Two server change files still say they are not live although the notes say both went live on 16 Nov
what: The first line of the direct-read record change and of the bell done-and-read change still says not applied live. The notes record both as applied on the live server on 16 Nov 2026. The feature map read those first lines and marks both server features as hidden, while the admin app side of the bell is marked live. Anyone who trusts the file line gets the wrong state.
expected: Each server change file says its true live state and date, as the two before them do.
who: anyone reading the code to learn what is live, and this audit's feature map

title: The phone offers to install the watch app on old Wear OS watches that cannot install it

expected: The demo turns away a second entry for the same day, as the real gym does, so the prospect sees the real rule.
how_often: every time a second entry is added for one day
fix_line: Refuse a second entry for the same member and day in the demo, as the real gym does

title: Demo gym: an approved renewal or pause says only "Approved", without the new dates
what: In the demo gym, approving a member's renew or pause request on Today shows only "Approved by Vikram Rathore." The real gym shows the new plan dates and "Collect the fee at the desk.", which is the point of the demo.
expected: After Approve, the demo shows "Renewed by ...: <start> - <end>. Collect the fee at the desk." or "Paused by .... Plan now ends <date>.", as the real gym does.
fix_line: Fill in the new start and end dates from the plan when the demo approves a request

title: A payment taken with no internet from the Dues list only says "Payment saved."
what: From a member's page, a payment taken with no internet says it is saved on this device, gives its receipt number and says it goes online later. The same payment taken from the Dues list in Money says only "Payment saved.", with no receipt number and no word that it is still only on this device.
expected: The Dues list gives the same message as the member page: saved on this device, the receipt number, and that it goes online when the internet is back.
how_often: every payment taken from the Dues list while the internet is off
fix_line: Use the member page's message, with the receipt number, on the Dues list too

title: The desk sees an empty "Pay online" box when the gym has no UPI ID
what: In a gym with no UPI ID and no payment company, a desk login that opens Collect payment or Sell membership sees a box headed "Pay online" with nothing in it. The owner sees a line telling them to add the UPI ID; the desk gets no words and no button.
expected: The box is hidden for the desk when there is nothing to offer, or says in one line that the owner can switch this on in Settings.
who: desk staff of gyms with no UPI ID saved
how_often: every time such a desk opens a money sheet for ₹1 or more
fix_line: Hide the box for the desk when there is no UPI ID and no payment company

title: The owner is told "The owner gives the extra days." when the member has no plan to add days to
what: After checking a workout code, the owner should get a "Give extra days" button. When the member has no gym plan that can take days (only a personal-training pack, or every plan cancelled), the owner instead reads "The owner gives the extra days.", the line meant for the desk, and has no button and no reason.
expected: The owner is told why no days can be given (the member has no plan to add them to) and what to do, such as sell or restore a plan first.
how_often: each time a workout code is checked for a member with check-ins but no gym plan that is not cancelled
fix_line: Give the owner their own line that says the member needs a plan first

title: With "Comes with a pass" ticked and no company picked, "Add member" can look as if it does nothing
what: When the pass box is ticked and no company chip is picked, pressing Add member (or Save changes) saves nothing and writes "Pick or type the pass company." under the chips. Every other wrong box is scrolled into view, but this message is not, because the chips are not marked as a wrong box. The pass part sits near the top of a long form and the button is at the bottom, so on a phone the message is off the screen and the button seems dead.
expected: The pass company message is brought into view like every other wrong box, so the desk sees why nothing was saved.
who: owners and front-desk staff adding a pass member
how_often: each time the pass box is ticked, no company is picked and the form is scrolled down
fix_line: Scroll to the pass company message when it is the reason nothing was saved

title: The "price is more than the plan price" question stays on screen after another plan is picked
what: On the sell sheet, after the question about a high price or fee appears, picking another plan empties the price boxes but leaves the old question and the "Yes, save" button. The next tap saves the other plan at its normal price while the screen still talks about the old amount.
expected: Picking another plan removes the question and puts the button back to "Confirm", the same as editing the price does.
how_often: only when the plan is changed after the question shows
fix_line: Clear the question whenever the plan is changed

title: Today's member news depends on the clock of the phone or laptop
what: Today lists member news of the last 24 hours and writes how long ago each came, by comparing the server's time with the clock of the device. On a device whose clock runs a day ahead, messages and requests that still need someone drop off Today; on a device that runs behind, old lines stay and say 'Just now'. The server's own clock comes with the list but is not used here.
expected: Today uses the server's clock for the 24 hour cut and for the age words, so a wrong device clock never hides a line that still needs someone.
who: owners, front desk and trainers on a device with a wrong clock
how_often: only on a device whose clock is wrong by hours
fix_line: Use the server's clock that comes with the list for the cut and the age words

title: The WhatsApp follow-up to a web-page enquiry carries the system note
what: For a person who asked on the gym web page or joined online, the ready WhatsApp message reads "you asked about <gym> (Asked on your web page: …)" or "(Joined online: …)". The enquiry card hides that note, the message does not.
expected: The message leaves out the system note, or uses only the words the person typed.
who: owners and front desk, and the people they message
how_often: every WhatsApp tap on an enquiry that came from the web page or online join
fix_line: Strip the system prefixes before the interest goes into the message

title: The growth Excel file shows a renewal rate the page hides
what: For a month whose 15 renewal days are not over, the page shows "–" for renewal rate and members lost, but the downloaded file gives a rate (often 100%) and a lost count made from the few plans decided so far.
expected: The file leaves the renewal rate and members lost empty for such a month, like the page.
how_often: every download, for the latest one or two months
fix_line: Write the file from the same shown value as the page

title: Workout code check calls entry-machine check-ins "imported"
what: In the summary line of "Check workout code", every matched day that was not at the desk or in the app is counted as "imported". A check-in at the entry machine falls in that group, while the row below it says "Checked in at the entry machine".
expected: The summary names entry-machine check-ins as such, and "imported" only for imported ones.
who: owners and front desk at gyms with an entry machine
how_often: every code check for a member who enters by the machine
fix_line: Count machine check-ins on their own in the summary

title: 'Download all your gym's data' leaves out much of the gym's data
what: The button and the help page say the file holds all the gym's data. The Excel file has eight sheets: about, members, plans, memberships, payments, check-ins, enquiries and expenses. Shop products and orders, diet plans, trainers and their bookings, staff, body measurements, member messages and photos are in neither file. Workout plans are only in the second, technical file.
expected: The download holds every kind of record the gym keeps in MettleUp, or the button and the help page name exactly what is inside and what is not.
fix_line: Add the missing kinds of record to the download, or change the words to say what it covers

title: Times in the gym's data download are 5 and a half hours behind India time
what: The check-in time, the day the gym was set up, the download time and the time an enquiry was added are written in world time, not India time, and nothing in the file says so. A 6:00 am check-in reads 00:30, and one before 5:30 am shows the day before next to the right date. The file's name carries the world date too, so a download before 5:30 am is named for yesterday.
expected: Every time and the file name use India time, the same as the panel's own screens.
fix_line: Write the times and the file date in India time

title: 'Your questions' in Help shows one person's questions to the next person on the same computer
what: The list of questions, AI answers and replies from MettleUp is kept in the browser, not per person or per gym, and signing out does not clear it. On a shared desk computer the staff see what the owner asked and what MettleUp replied. The owner's 'delete our gym' request, with the gym's name, code and phone, lands in the same list. A different gym signing in on that browser sees it too.
expected: Each person sees only the questions they sent; the list is tied to the gym and the signed-in person and is cleared or hidden at sign-out.
who: owners and staff on a shared computer
how_often: every time two people share a browser
fix_line: Keep the list per gym and person and hide it at sign-out

title: Import button says 'Update 1 members'
what: When exactly one member already in the gym gets blank details filled in and nobody new is added, the import button reads 'Update 1 members'.
expected: 'Update 1 member', the same way the button says 'Add 1 member'.
how_often: each import that updates exactly one member
fix_line: Use the singular for one, as the add label does

title: A special day with a past date vanishes without a word
what: On Gym timings, a special day whose date is already over (for example a wrong year) is dropped before the check and before the comparison with the saved timings. If it is the only change, Save stays greyed as 'Saved ✓' and the page says the timings are saved; with another change, Save works and the special day silently disappears.
expected: The owner is told the date is over, or the date box refuses a past day.
how_often: when a special day is typed with a past date
fix_line: Say 'This day is already over' on the special day instead of dropping it

title: An imported plan named like '3 days a week' becomes a 3-day plan
what: When another software's sheet names a plan by how often the member comes, such as '3 Days a Week Monthly' or '5 days/week 3 months', the import reads the first number and word as the plan's length. The new plan is saved as 3 (or 5) days long, and a row with a start date but no end date gets a membership that ends after 3 days and shows as expired.
expected: A number followed by 'days a week', 'days/week' or 'per week' is not a length; the month or year word in the name (or the row's own dates) decides it.
how_often: every import with such plan names
fix_line: Skip a number that counts days per week when reading a plan's length from its name

title: Past pass visits change when a pass member is edited
what: A check-in the member made by scanning the gym's QR carries no pass company of its own; the panel works it out from the member as they are today. Untick the pass box and every past QR visit of that member leaves the monthly count; tick it again and the first day becomes today, so the old visits stay lost; change the company and the old QR visits move to the new company. The gym then claims too little (or from the wrong company) for a month it has not been paid for yet.
expected: A visit that counted for a pass company on the day it happened keeps counting for that company, whatever is changed on the member later.
who: owners and staff of gyms with pass members whose members check in by QR
how_often: each time a pass member stops, restarts or changes company before the month is matched
fix_line: Write the pass company on the visit when the QR check-in is saved, or keep the member's pass history with its dates

title: A second friend with the same name gets the member a "Free days added" message but no days
what: When a member brings two friends who have exactly the same name, the thank-you for the second friend adds nothing to the member's plan. The screen still says the free days were added and gives a new last day, and the friend is marked as rewarded, so the offer never comes back.
expected: Each friend who joins counts on its own: the second thank-you adds the days, or the screen says plainly that this friend was already rewarded.
who: owners and the member who invited
how_often: rare: one member brings two friends with the same name
fix_line: Tell friends apart by their enquiry, not by their name

title: The owner's quick buttons are kept on one device only, though the sheet reads as if staff get them
what: The owner picks and orders the buttons, and the sheet says staff see only the ones they may use. The choice is kept in that one browser. On the front desk's own phone, and on the owner's second device, the four starting buttons show and nobody but the owner can change them there.
expected: The owner's choice reaches every device of the gym, or the sheet says that it is for this device only.
how_often: every gym with more than one device
fix_line: Keep the choice with the gym's settings, or say "on this device" in the sheet

title: In the quick buttons sheet the up and down arrows move nothing the owner can see in the list
what: The sheet always lists the eight buttons in one fixed order. Tapping an arrow changes the order on Today, but the rows in the sheet stay where they are and show no position number, so on a phone, where the sheet covers Today, the tap looks as if it did nothing.
expected: The chosen buttons are listed first, in their order, and a row moves when its arrow is tapped.
how_often: every time the order is changed
fix_line: List the chosen buttons first in their own order

title: A workout offer with a 1-day reward says "Give 1 days" and "1 days added"
what: The owner may set the reward of a workout offer to 1 day (the form allows 1 to 7). The give button then reads "Give 1 days", the note after giving reads "1 days added for <name>", and the take-back question reads "Take back the 1 reward days". The offer name members see and the "Rewarded" line use the right word ("1 extra day", "1 day").
expected: With a reward of 1 day the button, the note and the question say "1 day".
how_often: every time an offer has a 1-day reward
fix_line: Use the same one-day wording the offer name already uses

title: A second friend with the same name earns the member no free days, yet the screen says they were added
what: When a member brings two friends who have the same name, the owner’s tap for the second friend adds no days to the member’s plan. The screen still says the free days were added and shows a new end date, and the offer is closed for good.
expected: Each friend who joins gives the member the free days once; the already-given check should look at this friend’s own enquiry, not at the friend’s name.
who: owners and the members who invite friends
how_often: whenever one member brings two friends with the same name (also across old plans)
fix_line: Tie the already-given check to the friend’s enquiry, not the name

title: Gym timings says 'Right now members see' for times that are not saved yet
what: While the owner is still changing the gym timings, the top line reads 'Right now members see: Open now…' from what is typed on the screen. Members still see the last saved timings, or nothing at all the first time, until the owner taps Save.
expected: Before saving, the line says it is a preview of what members will see after Save. Only saved timings are called what members see right now.
how_often: every time the owner edits the timings before saving, and always on first set-up
fix_line: Word the line as a preview until the timings on screen are the saved ones

title: An owner checking a workout code is told "The owner gives the extra days." when the member has no gym plan to add days to
what: After a good workout code, the owner normally gets a "Give extra days" button. If the member has no gym plan that is not cancelled (for example only a personal training pack, or a cancelled plan), the button is left out and the owner reads "The owner gives the extra days.", the line meant for front desk staff. The owner is the owner, so the line sends them nowhere and does not say that a plan is missing.
expected: An owner sees the real reason, such as that this member has no plan to add days to and one must be sold first.
how_often: each time a workout code is checked for a member with no gym plan that can take days
fix_line: Give the owner their own line that says there is no plan to add the days to

title: A MettleUp receipt that fails to load says "Receipt not found"
what: When the owner opens a receipt for a payment to MettleUp and the internet is off or the server does not answer, the page says "Receipt not found. Open it again from Settings, Pay MettleUp, Your receipts." There is no "Try again" and nothing says the problem is the connection. An owner who needs the receipt for their accounts is told a paid receipt does not exist.
expected: A failed load says the receipt could not be loaded and offers to try again; "Receipt not found" shows only when the server says there is no such receipt for this gym.
how_often: every time a receipt is opened with no internet or while the server is failing
fix_line: Show a could-not-load message with a Try again button, apart from the not-found words

title: The desk can never see whether the MettleUp Plus lock is on
what: The lock card has a read-only version for the desk, with its own words. But the card is drawn only on the owner's Member app tab, and a desk person always gets the short Settings page, which leaves the card out. So the desk cannot tell a member whether the paid extras will lock.
expected: A desk person sees the lock card in read-only form, or the unused desk words are removed.
fix_line: Show the read-only lock card on the desk Settings page

title: A receipt number that is not sure yet can still be sent to the member on WhatsApp
what: When a payment was saved while the internet dropped, the receipt page greys out Print and says the receipt number is sure only once it is sent. The Send on WhatsApp button has no such check: once the internet is back it shows, and its message carries the receipt number.
expected: Send on WhatsApp is held back, like Print, until the payment is confirmed.
how_often: after a save with no internet
fix_line: Hide the WhatsApp button while the payment is not confirmed

title: On a trainer's page showing a past week, the booking sheet offers only a day that is already over
what: On a trainer's page, after pressing 'Last week', the button 'Book with <name>' opens a booking sheet whose Day list holds one day only, the Monday of that past week. Every try ends with 'This time has already passed', and the day cannot be changed. The same button under the main calendar handles this and offers today.
expected: The sheet opens on today (or the next day that can be booked), as it does from the main calendar.
who: owners and desk staff of gyms with trainer pages switched on
how_often: each time a booking is started while an earlier week is shown on a trainer's page
fix_line: Open the sheet on today when the shown week is already over

title: 'Copy link' on the web page says nothing when the copy fails
what: On Your web page, the owner taps 'Copy link'. When the browser refuses to copy (permission off, an in-app browser, an old browser), nothing happens on screen: no toast, no words. The owner may paste something old to a customer.
expected: A failed copy says so in plain words and shows the link so it can be copied by hand.
how_often: each time the browser blocks copying
fix_line: Show a short line with the link when copying fails

title: Web page editor says '1 plans from Plans'
what: In the card 'Also on your page, from your other screens', the Fees row always writes the count with the word 'plans'. A gym with one active plan reads '1 plans from Plans'; a gym with none reads '0 plans from Plans' with no hint that the page will show no fees.
expected: '1 plan from Plans' for one plan, and for none a line that says no fees will show until a plan is added.
how_often: every time for a gym with one or no active plan
fix_line: Use the singular for one plan and a clear line for none

title: Empty Shop page points members to a tab that no longer exists
what: When a gym has no orders yet, the Shop page says members order from the Shop tab in the MettleUp app. That tab is called Gym in the member app now.
expected: The line names the tab members really see: Gym.
who: owners and staff of gyms with no orders yet
how_often: every time the empty list shows
fix_line: Say Gym tab in the empty-orders line

title: Join link cards say people pay at the desk even when paying online is on
what: The gym-code card and the Invite members page always say people who join online pay at the desk. The WhatsApp message they send drops that sentence when the gym has turned on paying online on joining, so the screen and the message disagree.
expected: The cards follow the same switch as the message: no 'pay at the desk' while paying online on joining is on.
who: owners and staff of gyms that take payment online on joining
fix_line: Use the paying-online switch for the card words too

title: The heading 'Turn on the member app first' is never shown
what: Invite members gives its 'not turned on' card the heading 'Turn on the member app first', but the card only draws a heading once the member app is on. So the heading never appears, and the page only talks about turning on the shop.
expected: A gym without the member app sees the heading on the Invite members page, so it is clear why there is no link yet.
who: owners of gyms that have not turned on the member app
fix_line: Draw the heading on the not-turned-on card as well

title: A real gym owner is told their demo gym is gone
what: When the sign-in on a real gym has ended, saving the gym look or uploading a product photo or logo shows: This demo gym is no longer available. Start a new demo gym. On the Branding page the owner stays on the page with that message and is not taken back to sign in.
expected: A signed-in owner is told the sign-in ended and is taken to sign in again; the demo words show only in a demo gym.
how_often: each time a sign-in ends while the owner is on Branding or adding a photo
fix_line: Send these failures through the same sign-in-ended path every other shop call uses

title: "Open" on All branches switches branch while this branch's entries still wait to be sent
what: The branch list at the top refuses to open another branch while entries saved on this device are still waiting to be sent, because the other branch's panel would not send them. The "Open" buttons on the All branches page and the "Open <new branch>" button after adding a branch switch at once with no such check, so those entries stay unsent until the owner comes back to the first branch.
expected: Every way of opening another branch waits until this branch's entries are sent, and says so with the same words as the top list.
how_often: whenever an owner opens another branch from these buttons with entries waiting
fix_line: Check for waiting entries before every branch switch, not only in the top list

title: All branches tells an owner who cannot open other branches that the gym has one branch
what: The page shows "One branch" and "Your gym has one branch. Add another in Settings → Branches." whenever the person may not open other branches, even when the gym has two or more. An owner whose key cannot open the others (or a desk person who types the address) is told something untrue and sent to add a branch that already exists.
expected: When the gym has more than one branch but this person cannot open them, the page says that, in plain words, instead of saying there is one branch.
how_often: rare: only when the person cannot open the other branches
fix_line: Show different words when there are branches but no right to open them

title: Member search on All branches stops at 50 results without saying so
what: "Find a member in any branch" returns at most 50 members and then stops, with no line saying there are more. The lists above it say "And N more", the search does not, so for a common name the owner can miss a member of a later branch and think they are not a member.
expected: The search says when there are more matches than shown, or shows them all.
how_often: when 50 or more members match the typed letters
fix_line: Add an "and N more, type more letters" line under the search

title: Front desk can freeze a plan by approving a pause request
what: Freezing a plan is the owner's alone: the member page hides 'Freeze / extra days' from the front desk and the staff-rights words say staff cannot freeze plans. But on Today, 'Requests from the app', a front-desk login can tap Approve on a member's pause request and the plan gets up to 365 extra days, with no role check on the way.
expected: Either only the owner can approve a pause request (the desk sees it and is told to ask the owner), or the staff-rights words and the freeze rule say plainly that the desk may approve pauses members ask for.
how_often: every pause request a front-desk login approves
fix_line: Check the freeze permission before Approve on a pause request, or change the rule and its words

title: Quick buttons the owner picks stay on his own device
what: The owner picks and orders Today's quick buttons, and the sheet says staff see only the ones they may use. The choice is saved only in the browser where he made it, so the front desk's device and his own second device keep showing the standard buttons.
expected: The owner's choice of quick buttons shows on every device of the gym, with staff seeing the ones they may use.
how_often: every time the owner changes the buttons
fix_line: Save the button choice with the gym, not in the browser

title: "Download my data" says the file is saved even when the member closed the share sheet without saving it
what: After the backup file is made, the app opens the phone's share sheet. Whatever happens there, including closing it without picking Files, Drive or WhatsApp, the screen then says 'Saved mettleup-backup-....zip'. The file is only in the app's own temporary folder and is deleted at the next save, so a member can believe they have a backup that does not exist outside the app.
expected: The words say the file is ready to be saved and where to look, or 'Saved' appears only when the member chose a place.
how_often: every time the share sheet is closed without a choice
fix_line: Change the line after the share sheet to say the file was handed over, not saved

title: Drive sign-in message names two buttons that do not exist
what: When Google Drive asks the member to sign in again, the message says to tap 'Unlink Google' and then 'Link Google Drive'. The card has 'Unlink Google Drive' and 'Find my Drive backup'; there is no 'Link Google Drive' button.
expected: The message names the real buttons: tap 'Unlink Google Drive', then 'Find my Drive backup'.
who: members restoring an old Drive backup
how_often: every time Drive's permission has expired
fix_line: Change the message to name 'Unlink Google Drive' and 'Find my Drive backup'

title: Backup line blames the internet for an item the server refused
what: An item the server refuses stays in the waiting list and is tried every 6 hours. Settings then shows '1 change is waiting for the internet' even when the phone is online, and the 'Last saved' time is never shown again while it waits.
expected: A refused or not-yet-ready item is told apart from changes waiting for the internet, and the 'Last saved' time still shows.
who: signed-in members with an item the server will not take
fix_line: Count only items waiting for the internet in the line, and say plainly when one could not be saved

title: The body map says nothing was trained when the 30 or 90 day read fails
what: If reading the longer range fails, the body map treats it as no sets and shows 'Nothing trained in the last 30 days', though the member did train.
expected: A plain error with a way to try again, as the muscle sheet already does.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's own data read fails
fix_line: Show a try-again error instead of the empty message when the read fails

title: The privacy notice's list of what Help and feedback sends leaves out the phone's push address and the gym member key
what: Each help message sends the phone's push address (kept with the question so the team's reply can pop up) and, for a gym member, the member's gym key, besides what the privacy notice lists. The notice also says the install number is used only to stop misuse, but the phone uses it to fetch its answers and replies.
expected: The notice names every item a help message carries and every use of the install number, or the phone stops sending what the notice does not name.
fix_line: Add the push address, the gym key and the reply use to the notice's Help and feedback line

title: Erase says nothing was deleted after the account was deleted
what: A signed-in member who picks 'erase this phone and delete my account' has the account deleted first. If the phone erase then fails, the message says nothing was deleted, though the account and its saved copy are already gone.
expected: The message says the account was deleted and the phone erase failed, and offers to try the phone erase again.
who: signed-in members who erase their phone and account
how_often: rarely: only when the phone erase fails after the account delete
fix_line: Say what already went when the phone part fails after the account delete

title: Two notices still say 'OK' though the app's rule is never 'OK'
what: The app's one-button notice is meant to name what the button does ('Close', never 'OK'). Two notices skip that and show 'OK': the stop message when leaving a gym with open orders, and 'Could not remove the demo'.
expected: Every notice uses the same 'Close' button word.
fix_line: Use the shared notice helper in both places

title: The new-version check can stop for a long time after the phone clock goes back
what: The app asks GitHub for a new version only when the last answer is more than 6 hours old. If the phone clock was ahead and is then set back, the last answer looks to be from the future, so the app does not ask again until the clock passes that time. The What's new check next to it already handles this case.
expected: A saved answer dated in the future is treated as old, and the app asks again.
who: members who installed from GitHub and whose phone clock was wrong
fix_line: Ask again when the saved answer's time is later than now

title: Help and feedback sends more than the privacy notice says
what: With each help question the phone also sends its push address (kept so the team's reply can pop up), the gym's member key, and how its gym pop-up channel is set. The privacy notice's list for Help and feedback names the message, app version, phone model, screen, gym code, install number and coded internet address, but not these.
expected: The notice names everything the help box receives, or the phone stops sending what the notice does not name.
who: every member who sends a help question
fix_line: Add the push address and gym key to the privacy notice's help list

title: The watch screen log says it holds only screen times and settings, but it also sends when a workout was open and the watch app version
what: The caption under 'Add my watch's screen log' says it holds only the times the watch screen turned on, off or dim and the Battery Saver and screen settings. The log that is sent also marks, line by line with times, whether a workout was open, and names the watch app version and the last update pop-up decision.
expected: The caption names everything the log carries, or the log leaves out what the caption does not name.
who: members with the watch app who send feedback
how_often: every time the log is sent
fix_line: Add 'when a workout was open and the watch app version' to the caption

title: Gym messages may stay silent on OPPO and OnePlus phones
what: The rescue ring for gym messages tells the check the channel was made at normal importance, but it was made at high. When the phone strips the sound and marks it as set, the check takes it for the member's own choice and does not ring. The rest-over alert passes high and rings.
expected: The gym-message ring passes the importance the channel was really made with (high), like the rest-over ring.
who: members on OPPO and OnePlus phones
how_often: every gym message, on phones that mark the stripped sound as set
fix_line: Tell the check that the gym-message channel was made at high importance

title: The watch screen log sends more than its switch says
what: The switch says the log holds only screen on, off and dim times and the watch's Battery Saver and screen settings. The log that is sent also carries the watch app's version, the last choice on the watch update pop-up, the phone model and the sender's id.
expected: The switch's words list everything that is sent, or only the listed things are sent.
how_often: every time the watch log is sent
fix_line: Add the version, phone model and update note to the switch's words

title: With workout sounds off, the alert check-up asks the member to turn a sound back on
what: With Workout sounds off, Rest is over only buzzes. If Android stops that buzz, the check-up row says Android muted Rest is over and asks the member to turn its sound back on. That alert has no sound on purpose; what is missing is the buzz.
expected: With Workout sounds off, the row asks the member to turn the buzz (vibration) back on.
how_often: only with Workout sounds off and the buzz turned off in Android
fix_line: Say 'turn its vibration back on' when Workout sounds are off

title: Erase can leave reminders and Health Connect on
what: After 'Erase all data', the phone-side clean-up (reminders off, Health Connect sending off, widgets blank, shortcuts gone) runs only after three unrelated screen refreshes. If any of them fails, the clean-up is skipped silently: 'Time to train' keeps arriving, new workouts can still go to Health Connect, and old workout names can stay on the widget.
expected: The phone-side clean-up runs on every erase, whatever happens to the screen refreshes before it.
how_often: only when a refresh before it fails (rare)
fix_line: Run the phone clean-up in its own guard, first or always

title: The start-up error screen tells members to send their whole data file to their gym
what: When the app cannot start, 'Save my data file' shares the full phone data (workouts, body weight, notes, profile and mobile number). The line under it says to send the file to the gym, who passes it on to MettleUp. Elsewhere the app promises the gym never gets body weight, photos or notes.
expected: The help line sends the file straight to MettleUp support, and says the file holds private data.
how_often: every time a member follows the help line on that screen
fix_line: Point the line to MettleUp support directly and say the file is private

title: A workout delete that fails half-way leaves the workout without its records
what: Deleting a workout first removes its records, then the workout, as two separate steps. If the second step fails, the member is told the workout is still there, but its records are already gone and nothing rebuilds them.
expected: Both steps happen together or not at all, so a failed delete changes nothing.
how_often: rare: only when the database refuses the second step
fix_line: Run both deletes in one transaction

title: Loading the demo from the welcome screen can delete a member's own routines and body records without saying so
what: After 'Remove demo data' a member's own routines, body weight, measurements and photos stay on the phone. If they then tap 'Load demo data instead' with no workout of their own, the sheet says only 'You can remove it any time.' and the load erases all of it. With workouts kept, it names only the workouts.
expected: The welcome sheet names everything that will be deleted (as the Settings demo switch already does) and is shown as a warning whenever anything of the member's is on the phone.
who: members who removed the demo and then load it again
how_often: rare: only after a demo was removed
fix_line: Use the Settings demo wording on the welcome sheet and warn whenever own data exists

title: The home summary has no screen: its numbers and its 'Couldn't load' line are never shown
what: The app still works out the home summary after every save, an import, a sign-in and a bring-back, but no screen in the app shows those numbers or the failure line. The work is done for nothing, and the feature list says it is live.
expected: Either a screen shows the summary and its 'Couldn't load your summary, Try again' line, or the summary work is removed and the feature marked gone.
how_often: every save that refreshes the summary
fix_line: Decide whether a screen should show the summary; otherwise remove the work and mark the feature gone

title: In Calendar, a day with workouts can say 'No workout that day' when reading it fails
what: Tapping a marked day reads that day's workouts. If the read fails for a moment, the failure is swallowed and the sheet says 'No workout that day.' on a day the calendar itself marks as trained. Two fast taps on different days can also show the first day's workouts under the second day's date.
expected: A failed read says it could not load and offers to try again; a slow read for an older tap never fills the sheet of a newer tap.
how_often: rare: only when a day's read fails or two days are tapped fast
fix_line: Show a load error with Try again, and drop answers for a day no longer open

title: If 'Your profile' cannot be read, the page stays empty with no way to try again
what: When the profile cannot be read on opening Edit profile, a pop-up says to try again, but the page under it stays blank: no boxes, no Try again button. The member can only leave and come back.
expected: The page shows a load error with a Try again button, as the Profile tab does.
how_often: rare: only when the phone database read fails
fix_line: Show a load error with Try again on the page

title: Join screen says workouts stay on the phone, then says the gym sees them
what: When the gym has trainers set up, the join card says 'Your workouts stay on this phone.' and, two lines later, 'Your gym and your trainer see your workouts'. Joining then switches trainer sharing on.
expected: One true line about what the gym and trainer will see, without 'stay on this phone' when sharing starts at join.
how_often: every join at a gym with trainers
fix_line: Drop 'Your workouts stay on this phone' when the trainer line shows

title: Save stays spinning after the free exercise limit message
what: When the free plan's own-exercise limit is reached, Save shows the limit message and stops, but its busy state is never cleared, so Save keeps spinning and cannot be tapped again on that screen.
expected: After the limit message, Save is usable again (or the screen closes).
who: free members at the limit (only if the switch is turned on)
how_often: every time the limit is hit
fix_line: Clear the busy state before returning at the limit

title: A diet plan sent late at night shows the day before
what: The date under a diet plan is taken from the world clock day, not the India day. A plan a trainer sends or changes between midnight and 5:30 am shows yesterday's date to the member.
expected: The date is the India day the trainer sent or changed the plan.
how_often: every plan sent or changed between midnight and 5:30 am India time
fix_line: Turn the time into the phone's own day before showing it

title: Privacy notice says progress photos never leave the phone, but a setting sends them to Google backup
what: With 'Include photos in my backup' on, the newest progress photos are copied into the folder Android backs up to the member's Google account. The privacy notice says the photos never leave the phone.
expected: The privacy notice says photos stay on the phone unless the member turns on the photo backup, which copies them to their own Google account backup.
who: members who turn on photo backup
fix_line: Add one line to the privacy notice about the opt-in photo backup

title: Add measures says a picture stays on the phone even when photo backup is on
what: The Add measures page always says 'It stays on your phone.' under Add picture, even when the member has turned on the photo backup that copies photos to their Google backup. The photos page changes its words for this; Add measures does not.
expected: Add measures uses the same words as the photos page: stays on this phone when the backup is off, also in the phone's backup when it is on.
who: members who turn on photo backup
fix_line: Read the backup switch on Add measures and pick the words from it

title: A routine reorder that fails to save is undone with no word
what: In Edit routine, tapping Move up or Move down shows the new order at once. If the save fails, the screen quietly reloads the old order: no message and no Try again, so the member thinks it was saved or sees the order jump back for no reason.
expected: A failed reorder says so like every other save on this screen ('Couldn't save your last change. It is still shown here.' with Try again), as the file's own header promises (RP-15).
fix_line: Send the reorder through the screen's save helper so a failure shows Try again

title: A routine rename saved on leaving can fail with no word
what: When the member types a new routine name and leaves Edit routine by the back gesture or a tab switch, the name is saved on the way out. If that save fails the error is thrown away, so the routine keeps its old name and the member is never told.
expected: A rename that could not be saved is told to the member (or kept and retried), as the header says every save is awaited and a failed one says so.
fix_line: Report or retry a failed rename on leaving instead of swallowing it

title: Gym timings blames the gym when the phone is only offline
what: The first time a member opens Gym timings without internet, the page says the gym has not added its opening times and to ask at the desk, even when the gym has set them. No word says the phone is offline.
expected: The page says the hours could not be fetched and to try again when online, and keeps "No timings yet" for a gym that really has none.
how_often: first open of the page without internet
fix_line: Tell offline apart from no hours and say so

title: Taking back a plan request with weak signal makes the whole pause and renew area vanish with no word
what: A member taps 'Take back my request'. When the line is down, the take-back fails silently, the re-read fails too, and the panel hides itself: the waiting line, 'Pause my plan' and 'Renew my plan' all disappear. The member thinks the request was taken back while it still waits at the desk.
expected: A failed take-back says it could not be sent and keeps the waiting line on screen; the button shows it is busy.
how_often: when the signal drops during a take-back
fix_line: On a failed take-back or re-read, keep the last answer and show the 'Couldn't send it' words

title: My membership says 'No internet' while it is still loading
what: Every time the Gym tab opens, the card first shows the plan kept on the phone with its 'kept' time, so the line 'No internet. As of 6:42 pm today.' shows until the gym answers, even with good internet (up to 15 seconds on a slow line).
expected: The kept plan shows without the 'No internet' line while the fresh answer is on its way; the line shows only after a call really failed for lack of internet.
fix_line: Show the kept plan with keptAt null until the call fails offline

title: The sample shop is listed as live but no screen can open it
what: The list of app features says the sample shop and its pretend orders are live, but every shop page now sends a person without a gym back to the join screen. The sample shop's words and its saved bag are still in the app and still loaded on every start, but nobody can reach them.
expected: Either the sample shop opens before joining a gym, or it is marked removed and its leftover parts are taken out.
who: nobody sees it; the feature list is wrong
fix_line: Mark the sample shop removed and take out its leftover parts

title: Swapping the two photos puts the newer one as Before
what: In Share before and after, tapping the Before box and then the photo already in After swaps them, so the newer photo is labelled Before and the older After.
expected: The older photo is always Before, as the sheet itself says.
how_often: every time this swap is tapped
fix_line: Keep the older photo first after a swap, or drop the swap

title: The exercise chart can open on a year or on all time without the free-plan check
what: When a member's last workout of an exercise is older than 3 months, the chart opens on the 1-year or all-time range by itself, and the free-plan 3-month check only runs when the range is tapped, so a free member sees older charts without being asked to upgrade.
expected: The opening range is checked the same way as a tapped range, and falls back to 3 months (or the limit pop-up) when the plan does not allow more.
who: free members, only while the 3-month chart limit is switched on
how_often: every time such an exercise page opens
fix_line: Run the same plan check on the opening range

title: 'Skip for now' on the first-routine card hides it for good
what: The button reads 'Skip for now' (and a screen reader hears 'Skip making a routine now'), but one tap hides the card forever, even if the member later has no routines.
expected: The words say the card will not come back (for example 'Skip, don't show again'), or the card comes back later as 'for now' suggests.
how_often: every time the card is skipped
fix_line: Change the button words, or bring the card back later

title: A treadmill speed above the top is shown but not saved
what: Typing a speed above 40 (or a level above 100, or a second decimal point) leaves the number in the box, but the set's stored value is quietly cleared, so History shows no speed and the member is never told.
expected: The box says the number is too high (or refuses it), so what is on screen is what is saved.
who: members logging treadmill or bike sets
how_often: when a number above the machine's top is typed
fix_line: Show a short message under the box, or keep the box at the last saved value

title: The "Muscles ready today" card is listed as live but nothing in the app shows it
what: The feature list says the resting-muscles card on the Workout tab is live. The Workout tab no longer draws it: it was switched off on 5 Nov 2026 and only a note is left where it was. The body map and quick workout pages behind it have no way in from it.
expected: The feature list marks the card as switched off (hidden), so tests and reports do not count it as a live screen.
who: the team reading the feature list
how_often: every audit and report that counts live features
fix_line: Mark the card as hidden in the feature list

title: Routine rest picker names the wrong default
what: In the routine editor the rest picker always offers 'Default · 1:30', even when the member set a different default rest in Settings, so the chip names a length the exercise will not use.
expected: The Default chip shows the member's own default rest, as the workout screen does.
how_often: every time a member with a changed default edits a routine rest
fix_line: Pass the member's saved default rest to the routine picker

title: Strength level comparison choice can fail to save without a word
what: In the strength level sheet, tapping Everyone, Men or Women marks the chip at once and redraws the level. If saving the choice fails, only a log line is written: the member is not told, and the next time the page opens the old choice and the old level come back.
expected: The choice is shown as kept only once it is saved, or the member is told it could not be saved and can try again.
who: members who change who they are compared with
how_often: rarely, only when the phone's storage write fails
fix_line: Wait for the save before keeping the choice, and say so calmly when it fails

title: Save stays stuck after the own-exercise limit pop-up
what: On 'New exercise', when the free plan's own-exercise limit is reached, Save shows the limit pop-up and returns without clearing its busy state, so the Save button stays disabled on that screen.
expected: After the limit pop-up the Save button is usable again, as it is after the 'Already in your library' pop-up.
who: members on the free plan when the limit switch is on
how_often: every time the limit is hit (the limit is switched off at launch)
fix_line: Clear savingRef and saving before the limit return

title: Undo on the Body screen can fail without a word
what: When the member taps Undo after deleting or replacing a weigh-in or measurement, the bar closes first. If putting the entry back then fails, the error is dropped and nothing tells the member; the entry simply stays gone.
expected: A plain line says the entry could not be put back, and Undo can be tried again.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's database write fails
fix_line: Keep the Undo bar until the undo has worked, and say so when it fails

title: Fixing a wrong weigh-in for today asks 'Keep it?' against the wrong number
what: When today's weigh-in was saved wrong (say 765 kg) and the member types the right number on Add measures, the typo question compares the new number with the wrong one that is about to be replaced, and asks '76.5 kg — that's far below your last (765 kg). Keep it?'. The edit screen leaves the entry being edited out; Add measures does not.
expected: The weigh-in that the save will replace is left out of the comparison, as on the edit screen.
who: members who correct today's weigh-in on Add measures
how_often: each time a wrong weigh-in of the same day is fixed
fix_line: Leave the same day's weigh-in out of the comparison on Add measures

title: Body map says 'Nothing trained' when the 30 or 90 days could not be read
what: When the member picks 30 or 90 days and reading the sets fails, the map treats it as no sets and shows 'Nothing trained in the last 30 days', which tells a member who did train that they did not.
expected: A read failure says the sets could not be loaded, with a way to try again.
who: members who switch the body map to 30 or 90 days
fix_line: Show a could-not-load line instead of the empty state on a failed read

title: A treadmill box keeps showing a number it did not save
what: Typing a number over the top (incline or speed over 40, level over 100) leaves the number in the box, but the set is saved with nothing for that field, and no message says so. The member sees 45 while logging and nothing in History.
expected: The box says the number is too high, or holds the top value, so what the box shows is what is saved.
who: members logging treadmill, bike or rower details
how_often: only when a number over the top is typed
fix_line: Show a short too-high line under the box or refuse the extra digit

title: Body fat can be saved above 100 percent
what: The body measurement form accepts any number above 0 for every box, body fat included, so 150 % or a typo like 182 % is saved and drawn on the Body chart. Fixing an entry has the same rule.
expected: Body fat is refused above 100 % with a plain message (lengths may keep no upper limit).
fix_line: Refuse body fat above 100 percent in the add and fix forms

title: Long-rest marks are lost when workouts come back from the cloud copy
what: The account cloud copy of a workout leaves out the rest taken before each set and the rest planned. A workout brought back on a new phone, or written back from the server copy, loses its long-rest marks, so a set done after a long rest raises the next Target again.
expected: The cloud copy carries the rest taken and the rest planned for each set, as the Drive backup does.
who: members who use the cloud copy on a second or new phone
how_often: every workout brought back from the cloud copy
fix_line: Add the two rest values to the packed workout sets and to the insert

title: Muscle map says 'Nothing trained' when the 30 or 90 day read fails
what: On Progress, picking '30 days' or '90 days' reads that range's sets. If the read fails, the error is only logged and the range is treated as empty, so the member sees 'Nothing trained in the last 90 days' and 'Do a workout...' even when they trained.
expected: A failed read says it could not load the map and offers to try again, never an empty-training message.
how_often: rare: only when the phone's database read fails
fix_line: Keep a failed state and show a load error with Try again

title: Weekly goal line counts days but says workouts
what: The Up next card says 'This week: 2 of 4 workouts', but the number counts days trained since Monday. Two workouts on one day show as one workout.
expected: The line counts workouts as it says, or says days.
how_often: every week a member trains twice on one day
fix_line: Count workouts, or change the words to days

title: Before and after can be swapped so the newer photo says Before
what: In the before/after picture, picking the photo that is already in the other place swaps the two without putting them back in time order, so the newer photo is tagged Before while the sheet says the older photo is Before.
expected: After any pick the older photo is Before, as every other pick does and as the sheet's own words say.
how_often: when they pick the other slot's photo
fix_line: Put the pair in time order after a swap too, or say the swap on screen

title: The workout picture's 'more than previous' line can count body weight
what: The share picture leaves body weight out of its kg lifted box, but its 'Workout complete · +N kg more than previous' line is worked out from the full workout total, which counts body weight on pull-ups and dips. When only body-weight reps changed, that number is reps times the member's body weight, on a public picture that says it never shows body weight.
expected: The line on the picture compares the same body-weight-free kilos the picture's own box shows, or is left off when body-weight moves are in the workout.
who: members who share workouts with pull-ups or dips
how_often: every shared workout that beat last time with body-weight moves in it
fix_line: Work the picture's line out from the picture's own kilos, without body weight

title: Before and after can be swapped so the newer photo is Before
what: In the before/after sheet, picking for one slot the photo already in the other slot swaps the two, so the newer photo becomes 'Before', while the sheet says 'The older photo is Before.'
expected: The older photo stays Before (or the sheet stops saying it always is).
how_often: when the member picks the other slot's photo
fix_line: Keep inOrder on a swap, or drop the 'older is Before' line

title: Home numbers are worked out after every save but no screen shows them
what: The Home loader (about 40 database reads: today's Targets, weekly kg, recovery, lifts that beat a best) runs on every save, edit, import and failed write, but no screen reads its result; the only reader is the chat coach's snapshot tool, and the coach is switched off.
expected: Either a screen shows these numbers, or the loader runs only when the coach asks for them.
fix_line: Stop the background refresh while no screen reads it, or remove the feature row

title: A hold timer left open but never started stops the forgotten workout from pausing
what: The idle check skips any workout while the hold timer panel is on screen, even when its clock was never started. A member who opens a plank timer, does not press Start and walks away keeps a workout that never pauses itself, so its length keeps growing.
expected: Only a hold timer whose clock is running or paused part-way blocks the forgotten-workout pause.
how_often: when a member opens a hold timer and leaves without starting it
fix_line: Mark the hold timer as in use only once its clock has started

title: A set logged from the watch while the app is closed can be dropped without a word
what: When the phone queued 'Done' taps while MettleUp was closed and one of them lacks a number, the app takes the tap off the queue but, if it is not on screen at that moment, neither saves it nor leaves the 'Open MettleUp to log' note the other Done path leaves. The member believes the set was logged.
expected: A queued tap that cannot be saved stays queued, or leaves the same note as a live Done tap.
how_often: rarely: a watch Done with a missing number, read while the app is in the background
fix_line: Leave the same note as a live Done, or keep the tap queued

title: Help still tells members to tap a card that was removed
what: The member help article 'See which muscles are ready today, and build a quick workout' says to tap the 'Muscles ready today' card on the Workout tab, but that card and Quick workout were switched off on 5 Nov 2026 and nothing opens them. The article has no not-released mark, so it still shows.
expected: The article is hidden (marked not released) while the card is off.
how_often: every member who opens that help article
fix_line: Mark the article not released while the card is off
