what: The tests of Bring a friend cover new numbers, known enquiries, members, the member's own number and the daily cap, but never a gym that MettleUp has paused. A change could let a paused gym still get friend alerts and notes, and no test would fail.
expected: A test sends a friend invite to a paused gym and checks that no alert, note or enquiry is made.
fix_line: Add a paused-gym case to the friend invite test

title: Nothing tests that old shared workouts are cleared or that non-sharing members stay off Training progress
what: The year-of-workouts test checks the share, its limits, who may read it, and that turning sharing off or leaving deletes it. No test checks that a member who shares nothing new for 90 days drops off, that a member who never shared is not listed, or that sharing again after turning it off sends the year afresh.
expected: A test ages a share past 90 days and checks it is gone, and checks that a never-sharing member is not listed.
fix_line: Add an aged-share case and a never-shared case to the progress tests

title: Nothing tests that a removed trainer loses their member questions and alerts
what: The message tests take the Trainer tick off a person and sign a desk person out, but never remove a trainer from the gym. No test checks that a removed trainer can no longer read their questions, gets no more alerts, or that a member can no longer send a question to them.
expected: A test removes a trainer and checks they list nothing, get no browser alert, and that a new question to them is refused.
fix_line: Add a removed-trainer case to the message recipient test

title: The browser alert run is never checked for phone numbers or for the 8-day summary limit
what: The browser alert test checks who gets each alert, the summary count and the 6-hour limit for urgent alerts. It never checks that a push body carries no member phone number, and never ages a waiting summary alert past 8 days to see it marked late. Single alert kinds check their own words elsewhere, but the push run as a whole has no such guard.
expected: The push test asserts no 10-digit number in any push body, and that a summary alert older than 8 days is marked late and never sent.
fix_line: Add a no-phone-number check and an 8-day summary case to the browser alert test

title: Phone sign-in is never tested after a change to the person's plan, pass or Trainer tick
what: The phone sign-in tests use people whose state is fixed at the start. None renews an ended plan, removes a pass, or ticks or unticks a trainer and searches again, so a stale answer after such a change would not be caught.
expected: A test changes the plan, pass or tick and checks the next search shows the new state.
fix_line: Add before-and-after cases to the phone sign-in test

title: Changing a lead or a feedback message in HQ is never tested
what: No test saves a lead status or note, or a feedback status, through HQ. Nothing checks that a lead moves to Demo with its old note kept when HQ makes a gym from it, that a Won lead is never pushed back, or that the Needs you count drops after the save.
expected: A test saves a status and note on one lead and one message, reads them back, checks the other rows are untouched and the count drops, and makes a gym from a lead.
how_often: every lead and message HQ handles
fix_line: Add a server test that saves lead and feedback statuses and makes a gym from a lead

title: The 12-month promise to demo leads is tested without a Demo lead
what: The website form promises the details are deleted within 12 months. The clean-up tests use only lost, won and new leads, never one marked Demo, and no test reads the promise on the form. The Leads page also reads only the newest 300 leads and nothing tests what happens past that.
expected: The clean-up test includes an old Demo lead and checks it goes; a test reads the privacy line on the form; a test covers more than 300 leads.
fix_line: Add a Demo lead to the clean-up test and check the form privacy line

title: Nothing checks that gym owners see a changed UPI ID
what: Tests check the owner sees the UPI ID once. No test changes the details while Pay MettleUp is open or after, so an owner paying to an old UPI ID, or the trial line showing other details, would pass.
expected: A test changes the UPI ID, then checks the owner sees the new ID and QR on reopening, from Settings and from the trial line.
how_often: each time HQ changes the details
fix_line: Add a step that changes the UPI ID and reopens Pay MettleUp from both paths

title: Nothing checks that a pause, a sign-out, a new owner code or a new gym writes its log line
what: The database tests check log lines for approving, restoring and trial changes. They never look for the log line of a pause with its reason, a sign-out everywhere, a new owner code, or a new gym with only the last 4 mobile digits.
expected: Each of these actions is checked to leave one log line with its reason, and the new gym's line keeps only the last 4 digits of the mobile.
fix_line: Add a log-line check after each of the four actions in the database test

title: Making a gym for a lead is never tested through HQ
what: No test sends a Make a gym through the HQ server. That the lead moves to demo with the gym code in its note, and that a lead already past called is left alone, is never checked.
expected: A server test makes a gym for a new lead and for a won lead and checks each lead's status and note.
how_often: every gym made for a lead
fix_line: Add a server test for making a gym with and without a lead

title: The limit of 5 owner codes an hour and the old browser key note are never tested
what: HQ refuses a sixth owner code in an hour and adds a note when a gym still has an old browser key. No test makes a sixth code or a gym with such a key.
expected: A test makes six codes and checks the sixth is refused with its words, and a test checks the old key note.
fix_line: Add the sixth-code and old-key cases to the database test

title: The sign-out-everywhere test accepts any count of 3 or more
what: The test only checks at least 3 devices were signed out. A count that also counts devices already signed out, or a second press that does not say 0, would pass.
expected: The test checks the exact count, and that a second press says 0 devices.
fix_line: Check the exact device count and a second press

title: Cancelling a delete request is never tested
what: No test cancels a delete request. That a cancel needs a reason, that the gym keeps working, and that a cancelled request does not block a new one are never checked.
expected: A database test cancels a request with and without a reason, then adds a new request for the same gym.
how_often: each owner who changes their mind
fix_line: Add a cancel case to the delete request test

title: The phone test expects a second pop-up for a corrected reply, while the journey says none
what: HQ sends one push per question only. The phone's own reply check is tested to show one more pop-up when a correction arrives, which is what the journey says must not happen.
expected: The journey and the test agree: either a correction pops up once more, or it only shows in Help and feedback.
fix_line: Pick one rule for a second reply and fix the journey or the test

title: Nothing checks that HQ's log keeps only the length of a reply
what: The reply test lets the log call answer but never reads what it was sent, so the reply words or the question landing in the HQ log would pass.
expected: The test reads the log line and checks it has the length and no words.
fix_line: Read the logged line in the reply test

title: The gym delete request is never tested when it fails to send or for a gym not online
what: The only test of the admin app's delete request has the message reach MettleUp. A failed send, and the button staying hidden for a gym not online, are never checked.
expected: Tests check no success line when the send fails, and no delete button for a gym that is not online.
fix_line: Add a failed-send case and an offline-gym case to the browser test

title: No test checks that taking back free AI credits never takes credits the gym paid for
what: The take-back test starts from a gym that holds only free credits, so it proves the balance never goes below zero but never tries a gym that also bought a pack. Bought credits being taken back or expired is never tried either.
expected: A test gives a gym a bought pack and some free credits, takes back more than the free part, and checks the bought credits stay; and checks a month change never expires bought credits.
fix_line: Add a database check with bought and free credits mixed, then a take-back and a month change.

title: The nightly run is never tested with its backup or its first clean-up failing
what: The 03:00 test lets every step succeed. Nothing checks that the clean-up still runs when the backup fails, or that the gym server clean-up still runs when the Cloudflare clean-up fails. The log lines of the night are silenced in every test.
expected: Two tests: a failed backup night still runs every clean-up; a failed Cloudflare clean-up still runs the gym server one and reports failed; the logged words are checked.
fix_line: Add two night tests where an early step fails, and check the later steps still ran.

title: Signing out of HQ and the 30-day sign-in end are never tested
what: The HQ door tests cover signing in and refusals by status code only. No test signs out (Google or Cloudflare Access mode), checks the old session stops working, lets a session pass 30 days, or checks the words on the refused, server-down and not-set-up pages, or that the log says whether a sign-in was fresh.
expected: Tests sign out and then retry the old cookie, move the clock past 30 days, check each refusal page's words, and check the sign-in log row carries the fresh flag.
fix_line: Add sign-out, 30-day expiry and refusal-page word checks to the HQ door tests.

title: No test checks a fee pop-up skips members not on the app, members who left, or another gym
what: The fee note test uses list members of one gym who are linked to the app. Nothing tries a list member with no app account, a member who left the gym, or an id from a second gym, so a please-pay pop-up reaching the wrong person or a gym they left is never ruled out, and the desk is never checked for telling staff the member was notified.
expected: The database test adds an unlinked member, a member who left, and a second gym, and checks no note is made for any of them.
fix_line: Add unlinked, left and other-gym members to the fee note database test.

title: The backup's real part size and its public status door are only half tested
what: The split test cuts copies into 40-byte parts, so the real part size is never checked against the store's 25 MiB limit, and the parts count in the meta is never read. No test tries a POST or other call to the public backup status to show it cannot change anything or read a copy.
expected: A test checks the real part size stays under the limit and the meta names the parts; another tries a POST and other paths under the backup door and gets sign-in or a refusal.
fix_line: Check the real part size and meta, and try a write call on the public backup status.

title: No test checks that an unknown /api address answers "Not found"
what: The server answers any /api address it does not know with a plain "Not found". No test asks for such an address on any host, so a change that served the admin app page or crashed there would pass every check.
expected: A test asks for a made-up /api address on each host and sees a 404 "Not found", never the app page or a 500.
fix_line: Add one test that asks for a made-up /api address on each host and checks the 404 answer

title: No test checks that the demo form saves nothing while the landing page is hidden
what: When the landing page switch is off, the demo form address should answer "Not found" and save no lead. Every lead test runs with the switch on, so a lead saved while the page is hidden would not be caught.
expected: A test with the landing switch off posts a lead and sees a 404 with nothing saved.
fix_line: Add a lead test with the landing switch off that checks the 404 and that nothing was saved

title: No test sends a zero, tiny or huge amount to a payment request
what: The server refuses a payment request whose amount is under Rs 1 or above the cap, for desk dues and shop orders. No test ever sends such an amount, so a change that let a zero or wrong amount make a payment link would pass.
expected: A test sends a zero, a negative, a tiny and a too-large amount and sees BAD_AMOUNT with no request saved and no company link made.
fix_line: Add a payment test that sends bad amounts and checks the refusal, no saved request and no link

title: No test checks that a payment held by a closed desk frees up after 5 minutes
what: When a desk taps Approve on a paid-online payment it holds it for 5 minutes. If that desk closes the app, the hold should run out so another desk can make the receipt. No test moves the clock past the hold, so a payment stuck as taken for ever would pass.
expected: A test holds a payment, moves the clock past 5 minutes, and sees the payment back in the list and taken by a second desk.
how_often: when a desk closes during Approve
fix_line: Add a payment test that holds, waits past 5 minutes, and holds again from another desk

title: No test checks what a member sees when the gym turns off paying in the app
what: With "Take payments in the member app" off, the member should still see the amount and label but no payment page, QR or UPI link. One test makes such a request for another member but never reads what that member is shown, and no test covers a link looked at again after it expired.
expected: A test makes a request with in-app payment off and checks the member sees amount and label with no link or UPI; another checks a fresh link replaces an expired one.
fix_line: Add a member payment test with the switch off that reads what the member is sent

title: No test checks that the move keeps a sign-in the new address already has
what: The move page skips the hand-over when the new address already has a sign-in, so keys of two gyms never mix. The move test only starts from an empty new address, so a change that wrote the old sign-in over a newer one would pass.
expected: A test signs the desk in on the new address first, then moves from the old address, and sees the new address keep its own sign-in.
fix_line: Add a move test where the new address is already signed in to another gym

title: No test checks the safety lines on answers passed through our gym server address
what: Every answer passed on from the gym server gets two lines that stop the browser running it as a page, so it can never read the desk sign-in. No test checks those two lines, so removing them by mistake would pass every check.
expected: The pass-through test checks every passed-on answer carries the no-sniffing and sandbox lines.
fix_line: Add two checks to the pass-through test for the two safety lines

title: No test sends a live-update connection through our gym server address
what: Live-update connections take their own path through our address. No test sends one, so a change that broke them would pass.
expected: A test sends a connection upgrade through our address and sees it passed on unchanged.
fix_line: Add a test for a connection upgrade request through our address

title: No test checks the owner key stays out of the AI Assistant request and logs
what: The member help box test checks the member key is never sent to the AI or saved. The owner AI Assistant has no such check, so a change that put the owner sign-in key into the AI request or a log would pass.
expected: An AI Assistant test checks the owner key is not in the AI request, the saved rows or the log lines.
fix_line: Add the same key-not-sent checks the member help test has to the AI Assistant test

title: The address that hands Play Console each release bundle has no test at all
what: Play Console pulls each new release bundle and its store pictures through our own address. No test asks it for a bundle, a missing version, a picture, a wrong method or the browser first-ask, so a break would only show on release day.
expected: A small test asks the address for a bundle, a missing one, a picture, a POST and an OPTIONS ask, and checks the answer, the size, no caching and the Play-only browser rule.
fix_line: Add a test for the release bundle address with a fake GitHub

title: The download link for phones without Google Play has no test
what: The link that gives the newest MettleUp app file to a phone without Google Play is never asked for in a test: not the newest file, not the fallback page when GitHub cannot be reached, not the 10-minute wait after a release.
expected: A test asks the link with a fake GitHub and checks it points at the newest file, falls back to the release page, and keeps the answer for no more than 10 minutes.
fix_line: Add a test for the phone app download link

title: The public page a check-in poster opens is never tested
what: Scanning the check-in poster without the app opens a public page. No test opens it on Android, on an iPhone, with an old poster, or when the gym server is down, so none of its words or its no-check-in-from-home rule is checked.
expected: A screen test opens the poster page for each of those cases and checks the words and that nothing is recorded by the page.
fix_line: Add a screen test for the check-in poster page

title: The limit of 30 friend enquiries a day for one gym is never tested
what: The friend page has three daily limits. Two are tested (one address, one link). The third, 30 a day for one whole gym, is never reached in any test.
expected: The friend database test fills a gym with 30 friend enquiries and checks the next one is refused with nothing half-made.
fix_line: Add the 30-a-day gym check to the friend database test

title: Nothing checks a new gym name or logo reaches the invite link within 5 minutes
what: The invite link page keeps each gym's name and logo for 5 minutes. No test checks that time, so a change could stick for much longer without anyone noticing.
expected: A test checks the kept copy lasts 5 minutes and that a changed name and logo show after it.
how_often: after a name or logo change
fix_line: Test the 5-minute keep time of the invite preview

title: What's new: the keep times, the 5-line limit and the broken-file rule are never tested
what: The What's new feed keeps a fresh copy 10 minutes and a last good copy a week, shows at most 5 lines, and must never keep or pass on a broken file. None of these is tested; only the two ways to GitHub and the 503 are.
expected: Tests check 6 lines become 5, a broken file is not kept, and the 10-minute and one-week times.
fix_line: Add the keep-time and broken-file cases to the What's new test

title: The one-year delete of feedback messages is never tested
what: The privacy notice promises feedback is deleted after a year. The run that deletes it, and the run that sorts messages, have no test, so nothing proves old messages really go.
expected: A test puts in a message older than a year and one newer, runs the delete, and checks only the old one is gone.
fix_line: Add a test for the feedback delete and sort runs

title: The invite and get-app pages' own words are mostly never checked
what: Tests check which part of each page shows, but not most of its words: the WhatsApp preview 'Join <gym> on MettleUp', 'First, get the MettleUp app' with its steps, 'Get it on Google Play', the code box, 'Open this link on your phone', and the iPhone and computer headlines of the get-app page.
expected: The screen tests assert these words for each kind of phone and the preview title set by the server.
fix_line: Add the missing words to the link page screen tests

title: Admin app feedback: the journey expects the gym code, the test says none is sent
what: The journey says the owner's and desk's feedback is kept with the gym code. The admin app's test checks the opposite: the message carries nothing about the gym.
expected: The map and the code agree: either the journey drops the gym code, or the admin app sends it and the test checks it.
fix_line: Decide whether admin feedback carries the gym code and fix the journey or the test

title: A retry after a failed save, and the daily feedback limit lifting, are never tested
what: No test saves a message after a failed try and checks there is one copy and the failure did not count, and no test checks the 20-a-day limit lifts after 24 hours.
expected: Tests send after a failure and after the 24 hours pass, and check one copy and a working send.
fix_line: Add the retry and next-day cases to the feedback test

title: The app server's nightly clean-up run is never tested as a whole
what: Each delete step is tested alone, but no test runs the nightly job itself. Nothing checks that the 10-minute payment check skips the clean-up, that a missing database stops the job with a clear line instead of crashing, or that one missing table leaves the other steps running.
expected: A test runs the nightly job and the 10-minute job and checks which steps ran, the log line for each, and that one failing step does not stop the others.
who: everyone whose data the clean-up promises to delete
fix_line: Add one test that calls the scheduled job with each timer and with no database

title: No test shows what owners and staff see when alerts cannot be switched on
what: When the alerts key is not set up or the HQ server is down, the admin app should say alerts cannot be switched on now. No test drives this; every alerts test hands the browser a working key. The browser is also asked for permission before the key is checked, so a person can allow alerts and then be told they cannot have them.
expected: A test with the key address failing shows the plain 'not ready' line and no success.
how_often: whenever the HQ link is down
fix_line: Add an alerts test where the key address answers not set up

title: The WhatsApp delivery log lines HQ relies on are barely tested
what: HQ reads these log lines to find out why a sign-in code never arrived. Tests check the answer codes, but not the 'bad signature' and 'webhook check refused' lines, the title and details of a failure, that a failure is logged as an error, one line per status in order, or the 'Too large' refusal.
expected: Tests check each log line HQ reads, and that an over-size post is refused unread.
who: HQ, and owners waiting for a code
fix_line: Assert the log lines and add an over-size post test

title: The Help box's daily limit and length limit are never tested on the Help address
what: The daily message limit, the 'Keep it under 2000 letters.' wording and the daily free question lines for owners and staff are tested only on the plain feedback address, or not at all. Nothing proves a refused Help message never calls the AI.
expected: A Help test sends one message past the limit and checks the refusal words and that no AI call was made.
fix_line: Add Help address tests for the daily limit and the length limit

title: No test proves a crash report drops the gym code and install id
what: The crash test checks that the saved row has an empty gym and sender, but the report it sends never contains a gym code or install id. So the promise that these are never kept is not tested. It also never sends a member-app crash.
expected: A test sends a member crash with a gym code and an install id and checks neither is saved.
fix_line: Send a gym code and install id in the crash test and assert they are gone

title: A demo request from a member's shared link is never tested on the page
what: The landing page should mark a demo request as a member referral when opened from a member's shared link. Tests send that label to the server directly. No page test opens the link and checks the label reaches HQ.
expected: A landing page test opens the member link, sends a demo request and sees it saved as a member referral.
fix_line: Add a landing page test opened with the member link

title: The alerts key address has no time limit when HQ is slow, and no test of it
what: When the admin app asks for the alerts key, the server waits for the HQ server with no time limit. A slow HQ means the switch spins until the platform gives up. No test covers a slow HQ, and the 'GET_ONLY' answer words are not checked.
expected: The key request gives up after a few seconds with 'UNREACHABLE', and a test proves it.
who: owners and front desk turning on alerts
fix_line: Add a short time limit to the HQ key request and a test

title: Getting a running rest back after a watch restart or app update is never tested
what: When the watch restarts, the app updates or Alarms & reminders is switched on, the watch rebuilds a saved rest: alarm, countdown card, copy settings, version for the phone. No test runs this. No watch test touches the restart or the rest restore at all.
expected: A test restarts with a rest saved, with none, with one already ended and with one skipped, and checks one buzz at the right time and no buzz for a lost rest.
fix_line: Add watch tests that run the restart path with a saved rest

title: How the watch takes in what the phone sends is never tested
what: The watch's handling of each phone item (save a rest, set its alarm, show the card, drop an old or unreadable item, clear on skip or discard, keep the gym colour) has no test. Watch tests only check small helpers, like the 5-second buzz rule.
expected: Tests feed the watch phone items, including late, repeated and broken ones, and check the saved rest, the alarm and the buzz.
fix_line: Add watch tests that feed phone items into the watch's state and check the result

title: The Done, +15 s and Skip buttons on the watch's rest card are never tested
what: No test presses Done, +15 s or Skip on the watch's rest card, or checks that the phone ends or lengthens the rest or ticks the right set. 'Phone not reachable' is never checked either. One test only reads the code to see that the phone's refusal reaches the watch.
expected: A test presses each button and checks what the phone receives, and checks the words when the phone cannot be reached.
fix_line: Add tests for the three rest card buttons and the no-phone words

title: The watch's own rest notifications and buzz pattern are never tested
what: No test checks the watch's countdown card, its Rest is over card (words, no button, going away by itself, only one at a time), the long-pause-short buzz, or that Ring through Do Not Disturb really gets through. One test only reads the code to see that the buzz is always called.
expected: Tests check each card's words and lifetime and the buzz pattern; Do Not Disturb is checked once on a real watch before release.
fix_line: Add watch tests for both cards and the buzz, plus a Do Not Disturb check on a real watch

title: The watch's memory of its copy settings is never tested
what: The watch remembers the copy settings it applied, so it only sets them again when they change, after a refusal, or after an update from the older name. No test runs this. Tests only check which tags are chosen.
expected: A test applies the settings twice, makes the watch refuse once, and starts from the older name, and checks when they are set again.
fix_line: Add a watch test for when the copy settings are set again

title: HQ's view of a member's watch screen log is never tested
what: Tests check how the phone builds and sends the watch log. Nothing checks how HQ shows it: the log under its message, no empty block when there is none, each message keeping its own log, or that a gym's owner and staff can never read it.
expected: A test sends two messages with a log and one without, then checks what HQ shows and that the gym's side cannot see them.
fix_line: Add an HQ test that shows feedback messages with and without the watch log

title: The heart sensor starting and stopping on the watch is never tested
what: Tests check the heart line's words (dash, number, hidden). Nothing checks that the sensor stops when the screen dims or the workout ends, that the question is not asked again, or that the logging screen shows the same number as the rest timer.
expected: Tests check the sensor turns on and off with the workout and the dim, and that both screens show one reading.
fix_line: Add watch tests for when the heart sensor starts and stops

title: The "one line when the numbers match" test checks a helper no watch screen uses
what: A test proves that when today's target equals last time's numbers only one line shows, but it tests an old helper that no screen calls. The real screens always draw both a Previous and a Next line, so the same numbers show twice.
expected: The test should check the screen's own card, and the screen should show one line when the numbers match (or the journey should say two lines are wanted).
fix_line: Test the card the screens draw, decide one line or two, and remove the unused helper

title: The -15, +15 and Skip buttons on the watch rest timer have no test
what: No test changes a running rest by 15 seconds or skips it. The rule that a rest can never be cut below one second, and that a skipped rest does not come back or buzz, is unchecked.
expected: A test moves the rest by +15 and -15, checks the new end time and its floor, and checks Skip ends the rest with no later buzz.
fix_line: Add a small test of the rest step and skip rules

title: Only the bright countdown is size-checked at the largest text; weight, reps, the dim countdown and the smallest text are not
what: The text-size promise covers the countdown and the weight and reps numbers, bright and dim. Only the bright countdown is compared between normal and largest text. The weight and reps numbers, the dim countdown, the smallest text size and a live change of text size are never compared.
expected: Each big number is measured at normal, smallest and largest text, bright and dim, and must stay the same size.
fix_line: Extend the size comparison to the logging numbers, the dim screen and the smallest text

title: The watch's workout notice is never checked: its words, that it is silent, that only one shows
what: The notice that keeps MettleUp up during a workout is never posted in a test. Its two lines, its silent channel, that only one notice shows, and that it carries no exercise, weight or heart rate are unchecked. Tests only check when the app wants the notice.
expected: A test posts the notice and checks its words, that it makes no sound, that a second post replaces it, and that it holds nothing private.
fix_line: Add a small test that posts the notice and reads it back

title: Nothing tests that the watch asks for permissions only once; a test even pins the ask over a running rest
what: A test makes sure the heart-rate ask is chosen over a running rest timer when the ask flag is on. No test checks that the flag is cleared after the first answer, so a later open could cover a rest with the ask again.
expected: A test answers both asks, reopens the app and checks no ask screen comes back, during a rest or not.
fix_line: Add a test of the stored "already asked" mark

title: The "Phone not connected" screen's wait for two empty checks is never tested
what: Tests only check which screen shows once the phone is known to be gone. The rule that one empty check is not enough, and the return of the current set after the link is back, are unchecked, so a one-moment drop could flash the screen.
expected: A test feeds one empty check (no change) and then two (Phone not connected), then a link back with a new set.
fix_line: Add a test of the connection check count

title: When the watch writes its version for the phone is never tested
what: Tests check only which version values are kept. Writing once per change, writing again after an update or when the phone asks, and trying again after a failed write are unchecked.
expected: A test checks one write per process, a rewrite after an update or an ask, and no crash without Play services.
fix_line: Add a small test of when the version is written

title: No test taps the watch screen: the waking tap, the no-workout screen, the dim Open on phone button
what: No test checks that the first tap on a dimmed screen only wakes it and does not press Skip or -15, that the no-workout screen has no button and starts nothing, or that a dim Open on phone tap sends no second request. Only the crown's waking turn is tested.
expected: A screen test taps each of these and checks nothing else happens.
fix_line: Add screen tests for these three taps

title: No test opens the check-in poster page
what: The web page a member reaches by scanning the gym's check-in poster has no automated test. Nothing checks its words for Android with the app, without the app, an iPhone, a wrong poster or no internet, or that it never shows a member's name.
expected: A test opens the poster page as each kind of phone and checks what it says, like the invite page test already does.
fix_line: Add a page test for the check-in poster like the invite-link one

title: The invite link page's key words and its WhatsApp preview are never checked
what: Tests check the invite page's heading and buttons, but not 'invites you to the MettleUp app', the 'First, get the MettleUp app' card, the older-app try, the 'Gym not found' and 'Couldn't reach the gym' states, or the preview title and line WhatsApp shows. The preview test replaces the part that writes the title with one that does nothing, so a wrong or leaking preview would pass.
expected: Tests read the page's words in each state and the preview title and description the server writes.
fix_line: Check the invite page states and the preview text in the existing invite tests

title: No test checks the gym-server relay's no-run safety headers
what: The relay adds two safety headers so a gym-server answer can never run as a page on the admin app address, where the desks' saved keys live. No test checks either header, so removing them would pass every test.
expected: The relay test asserts both safety headers on every answer.
fix_line: Assert the two safety headers in the relay test

title: No test checks the admin app moves to a new version and drops the old files
what: The offline keeper is meant to show the newest version when online and remove old files after a deploy. No test runs a second deploy against it, so a desk stuck on yesterday's buttons, or a blank page from a dropped file, would pass. The skip-list test also never checks the check-in page is kept out of the device copy.
expected: A test installs one version, deploys another, and checks the new one shows online and offline with no old file left; the skip test includes the check-in page.
fix_line: Add a two-version test of the offline keeper

title: No test checks a shared desk computer keeps no gym copy after sign-out
what: Tests sign out of a device and see the Sign in button, but none then goes offline or reloads to check the previous person's members and payments cannot be read.
expected: After sign-out, a test reloads offline and finds no gym data on screen or in the device copy.
fix_line: Extend the sign-out test to reload offline and check nothing is left

title: The desk's payment-link messages are never checked on screen
what: The collect sheet's 'Making the link...', the camera line, the WhatsApp payment message, 'Sent. They see it under My membership...', the missing-mobile message, 'No internet. Try again.' and the 'paid online but the receipt could not be made' card have no test on screen. The server refusal of a Rs 0 or tiny amount also has no test.
expected: The payment screen test checks each of these lines, and a server test sends a zero amount and gets the refusal.
fix_line: Add these lines and a zero-amount call to the payment tests

title: The member's pay card words are never checked
what: The member test checks the amount, failed and run-out lines, but not 'Pay your gym', the UPI scan line, the 'Pay by UPI app' button, 'Paid. The gym can see it.', 'Online payment is not set up at this gym yet. Pay at the desk.' or the test-mode line.
expected: The member pay test checks every line the card and the order payment show.
fix_line: Assert the remaining pay card words in the member pay test

title: No test keeps the delete-account page's backup promise in step with the privacy notice
what: The delete-account page promises backup copies go within 7 days, and the privacy notice says the same in its own words. No test reads either line, so one could change and the two pages would disagree.
expected: A test checks the backup line on the delete-account page matches the privacy notice.
fix_line: Add a line check to the legal pages test

title: No test checks an unknown /api address answers 'Not found'
what: The server answers 404 'Not found' for an /api address it does not know, so the admin app page is never served there. No test asks for such an address.
expected: The address test asks for a made-up /api address and gets 404 'Not found'.
fix_line: Add one made-up /api address to the address test

title: The friend invite page is never tested for a member with no first name
what: Every invite-page test uses an inviter called Asha. Nothing checks the 'A friend invited you' and 'Your friend does not' wording, or that the word 'undefined' never shows.
expected: A test opens an invite from a member with no first name and checks the friendly wording and that the send still works.
fix_line: Add one invite-page test with an empty inviter name

title: The join page keeps the person's name and checked number in the browser tab, and the test expects it to
what: The join-online test reloads the page half-way and after sending, and checks the name and checked number come back. The journey says the number must not be kept by the page itself.
expected: Either the journey allows tab-only keeping until the tab closes, or the page forgets the number after sending; the test then checks whichever is decided.
who: people joining online on a shared phone
fix_line: Decide the rule, then make the page and its test match

title: The join page's refusal and change messages are never seen by a test
what: No screen test checks 'Too many sign-ups were sent today...', 'Use another number', 'Change number', 'Step 1 of 3', or what happens when the gym's plan or price changes while the page is open.
expected: A screen test covers each of these messages and the plan-changed path, and checks 'Sent to <gym>' stays hidden after a refusal.
fix_line: Add screen tests for the daily limit, plan changed and the two buttons

title: How long the update notes are kept is never tested
what: The update-notes address tests check the status codes only. Nothing checks the 10-minute keep time, the 1-minute time on a kept copy, that a failure is never kept, or that a second request skips GitHub.
expected: Tests check the keep times on each answer and that a kept copy is used without asking GitHub again.
fix_line: Assert the cache headers and a cache hit in the existing test file

title: The update screen promises up to 5 new lines, but the app keeps only 3
what: The journey says the full-screen update shows up to 5 What's new lines. The app's own test checks it reads at most 3 lines and drops the rest.
expected: The journey and the app agree on one number, and the test checks that number.
fix_line: Pick 3 or 5 and fix the journey or the app to match

title: When saving feedback fails, people see the offline words, not 'Could not save. Try again.'
what: The tests check that a failed save shows the app's offline words ("Couldn't send"), while the journey expects 'Could not save. Try again.'.
expected: One wording for a failed save, written into both the journey and the tests.
fix_line: Choose the words and update the journey or the apps

title: The get-the-app page on a computer is checked only for its blocks, not its words or QR
what: The test checks the computer page has a QR block and the two store names. It never checks the headline, the 'Scan this QR code' line, 'Coming soon', or that the QR points at the app link.
expected: A test checks the words and decodes or reads the QR's address.
who: people getting the app from a computer
fix_line: Check the page words and the QR target in the existing test

title: The help box's daily message limit is never tested
what: Feedback's daily limit is tested, but the help box (which answers questions) has no test that the limit refuses a question and gives no AI answer.
expected: A test sends questions past the daily limit and checks 'Too many messages today' with no AI call.
who: owners, staff and members asking for help
fix_line: Add a limit test to the help tests

title: The cap of 2,000 crash reports a day for everyone together is never tested
what: Crash reports are capped at 30 a day from one network address and 2,000 a day for all reports together, to keep the free database from filling. A test checks the 30 cap; nothing checks the 2,000 cap, so a change that broke it would pass.
expected: A test fills the day with 2,000 reports from many addresses and sees the next one refused with 429 and no row saved.
fix_line: Add one test that pre-fills 2,000 reports and checks the next is refused

title: MettleUp's messages in the bell are never tested for staff, for two gyms, or at the 120-day edge
what: The bell test opens 'From MettleUp' only as an owner. No test opens it as staff or checks two gyms see the same messages and nothing of each other. The age test only asks that the limit is at least 90 days and uses a 6-month-old message, so a limit anywhere from 90 to 180 days would pass though the promise is 120.
expected: Tests open the bell as staff, compare two gyms, and check a 119-day message shows while a 121-day one does not.
fix_line: Add a staff bell check and pin the 120-day edge in the server test

title: AI column matching for staff, an ended sign-in and a used-up day is checked only as a status code
what: The server tests check that a staff login gets 403 and an ended key 401, but not that no AI call is made or no read counted for them. No screen test shows the import with the daily limit used up, the demo gym, a staff login, or a person just made owner; the words the owner reads in those cases are never checked.
expected: Server tests check no AI call and no count for staff and an ended key; one screen test per refusal checks the import falls back to matching by hand with its plain line.
fix_line: Assert no AI call and no count on each refusal, and add screen checks for the refusal lines

title: Most of the AI Assistant's refusal words are never checked
what: Only the daily-limit, no-credit and paused words are checked exactly. The words for an empty ask, the demo gym, a too-long voice clip, the trial money cap, a diet-plan ask, too few exercises and too few usable days are checked only by a status or a short piece, and only the no-credit line is checked on a screen. A wording or wiring change in the others would pass.
expected: Each refusal's exact words are checked once on the server, and the cap, demo and too-long lines once on the screen.
fix_line: Assert the exact refusal words in the server tests and add screen checks for three of them

title: Browser alerts are tested only for an owner on the path where everything works
what: The screen test turns alerts on and off for an owner with a working key. Nothing on a screen checks what a person sees when MettleUp has not set up alerts, that a failed browser sign-up never says alerts are on, or a staff member turning alerts on and off.
expected: Screen tests for the not-set-up answer (a plain line, no 'on'), a refused browser sign-up, and a staff login turning alerts on and off.
fix_line: Add three screen checks: not set up, refused sign-up, staff on and off

title: HQ's menu icons are copied from a free icon set without the credit line its licence asks for
what: The menu and bottom-bar icons in HQ (bell, phone, speech bubble, pulse line, bin and others) are the same drawings as the free Feather and Lucide icon sets, path for path. Those sets are free to use, but their licences (MIT and ISC) ask that their short copyright notice travels with every copy. HQ ships no such notice anywhere.
expected: Either a one-line credit for the icon set kept with HQ (for example a licences note in the HQ folder or a comment beside the icons), or icons drawn by MettleUp.
who: MettleUp (legal tidiness only; nobody outside sees HQ)
fix_line: Add the icon set's one-line licence notice next to the icons

title: The assistant hands every member without the app to WhatsApp for offers, with no way to leave out someone who asked not to be messaged
what: When the owner asks for a come-back offer, a 'we miss you' message or a festival wish, the assistant lists every member in that group who lacks the app and offers to send it to each of them on WhatsApp. There is no 'does not want messages' mark on a member anywhere, so a member who told the gym to stop still lands on the list, and the assistant's own ideas keep suggesting win-back offers to lapsed members. WhatsApp's rules ask senders to message only people who agreed and to honour a request to stop; members who report the owner's number can get it limited or blocked.
expected: A member can be marked 'no offers on WhatsApp' and the assistant leaves them out of offer and win-back lists (and says how many it left out); greetings and gym-closed notices can still go.
who: owners and members who asked to stop
how_often: every offer or win-back sent to members without the app
fix_line: Add a no-offers mark on a member and drop marked members from offer lists

title: The AI that writes offers to members is not told to avoid promising body results
what: The rules given to the AI that drafts and rewrites member messages forbid inventing phone numbers, links, prices and dates, but say nothing about health or body-result promises. An offer draft can come back saying things like 'lose 5 kg in a month' or 'guaranteed results', which India's advertising code (ASCI) treats as claims that need proof. The owner can edit the draft, but nothing warns him.
expected: The writing rules also say: never promise weight loss, body changes, health cures or guaranteed results.
how_often: sometimes, when the AI adds a claim
fix_line: Add one line to both writing rules banning result and health promises

title: Owners upload a logo that goes out to all their members without being asked if they may use it
what: The branding screen lets an owner upload any picture as the gym logo, and we then store it publicly and show it in every member's app and on the home-screen shortcut. Nowhere on the screen does it say the owner must own or have permission to use that logo, so we could end up shipping someone else's trademark in our app with no record that the gym took responsibility.
expected: A short line next to the upload button (or a tick box the first time) saying the owner confirms the logo is theirs or they have permission to use it, backed by a matching line in the terms.
fix_line: Add one line by the upload button saying the owner confirms they may use this logo, and the same in the terms

title: Gym web page photos can show members' faces with no check that those people agreed
what: The owner adds up to a set number of gym photos to a public page that Google may list. The only tick says the fees, photos and words are the gym's own. Nothing asks whether people seen in the photos agreed to be shown, and the tick is asked only once, at first publish, so photos added later are never covered.
expected: Before publishing photos, the owner is told to use photos where any person shown has agreed (or shows no faces), and the promise covers photos added later.
how_often: every gym that publishes a page with people in its photos
fix_line: Add one line under Photos and in the tick: only photos where anyone shown has agreed to be on the page

title: Owners can upload any picture as a shop product photo with no word that they must have the right to use it
what: The product form takes any photo the owner drops in, uploads it at once and shows it to every member in the app shop. Owners often save a supplement brand's picture from a shopping website. Nothing on the form says the photo must be their own or one they may use, so we can end up showing someone else's copyrighted picture in our app with no record that the gym took responsibility.
expected: One short line under the photo box says to use your own photo or one you have permission to use, and the terms say the gym answers for pictures it uploads.
fix_line: Add a one-line rights reminder under the photo box

title: If the AI coach comes back, it has no health safety rules and no way to report a bad reply, which Google Play asks of AI apps
what: The coach is switched off today. Its instructions to the AI tell it to coach training and estimate meal calories, but say nothing about pain, injury, medical conditions, eating problems or young members, and never ask it to say a calorie number is a rough guess. The chat also has no way for a member to report a harmful or wrong AI reply.
expected: Before the coach is switched on: the AI is told to stay out of medical advice and point to a doctor for pain or illness, to say photo calories are estimates, and each AI reply has a report button, as Google Play asks of apps that make AI content.
how_often: only if the coach is switched on
fix_line: Add safety rules to the coach instructions and a report button on AI replies before switching the coach on

title: The copy uploaded to Google Play still carries the 'download the new version file from GitHub' update path
what: Google Play gets the same build as the GitHub file, and that build is marked 'GitHub copy' by default. On Play copies the app normally asks the phone who installed it and uses Play's own update. When the phone cannot say, it falls back to the GitHub default and shows 'Tap Update now to download the file, then open it to install', sending the member to download an app file outside Play. Play's rules say an app from Play may not update itself by any way other than Play.
expected: The build sent to Google Play is marked as a Play copy, so it can never offer an app file from outside Play.
how_often: only when the phone cannot say who installed the app
fix_line: Build the Play copy with the Play mark set, so the outside-Play update can never show

title: On an iPhone the update screen would tell members to download an Android app file
what: The update check decides between Google Play and GitHub only. An iPhone cannot say who installed the app, so it falls to the GitHub default and would show 'A new MettleUp is here' with 'download the file, then open it to install', pointing at the Android file. Apple rejects apps that point to other ways of installing or updating, and the member cannot use the file anyway.
expected: On an iPhone the update screen sends members to the App Store, or does not show.
how_often: every update, once the iPhone app ships
fix_line: Add an App Store path to the update check before the iPhone app ships

title: The AI coach's replies have no way to report a bad or offensive answer
what: Coach chat shows the AI's replies as bubbles and cards, but a reply cannot be pressed, flagged or reported. Google Play asks apps that show AI-made content to let users report offensive answers inside the app. The chat is hidden today, so this bites the day it is switched on.
expected: Each coach reply has a way to report it, and the reports reach MettleUp.
how_often: every coach reply, once the chat is shown
fix_line: Add a report choice on each coach reply before the chat is switched on

title: On iPhone the permission questions talk about the hidden AI coach, not what the app really uses
what: When the iPhone app asks for the camera, photos or microphone, the reason it shows was written for the AI coach: snap a meal for nutrition, talk to your AI coach, log meals by voice. The coach is switched off. The real uses are scanning the gym poster, progress and profile photos, and speaking a feedback message. The poster scanner has no reason line of its own, and two parts of the app give two different microphone reasons, so which one shows is down to build order. Apple turns apps away when the reason does not match what the app does with the permission.
expected: Before the iPhone app is sent to Apple, each permission reason says what the app really does today: scan your gym's poster, add progress and profile photos, speak a feedback message.
who: members on iPhone, and MettleUp at App Store review
how_often: once the iPhone app is sent for review
fix_line: Rewrite the camera, photos, microphone and speech reasons to match today's uses and give the poster scanner its own camera reason

title: The Credits page leaves out the app's icon set and the free code it is built on
what: The Credits page lists the exercise pictures, the body map and the fonts, but nothing else. The app's icons are drawn in the style of the free Lucide icon set, and at least one (the flame) is Lucide's drawing exactly. The app is also built from many free code packages whose licences ask that their short copyright notice comes with every copy. Neither the icon set nor the code packages are named anywhere in the app.
expected: The Credits page (or a 'free software used' page linked from it) names the icon set and lists the code packages with their licence notices.
fix_line: Add the icon set to the Credits list and a generated list of free code packages with their notices

title: Once MettleUp Plus is switched on, an iPhone member would lose the paid features with no way to buy them, and be told to pay through Google Play
what: The free-month rules and the locks on paid features are the same on Android and iPhone. On an iPhone there is no store to buy from yet, so a Buy tap answers 'Buying opens soon' or 'Google Play is not available right now', while the page says 'You pay through Google Play'. After the free month an iPhone member who is not at a MettleUp gym loses the watch, older charts, suggested weights and calculators and cannot get them back. Apple rejects apps that mention another phone platform's store and apps that sell digital features without Apple's own payment.
expected: Before the iPhone app ships with Plus switched on: either iPhone members keep every feature free until Apple payment is built, or the Plus page buys through Apple and names the App Store, never Google Play.
how_often: every iPhone member after the free month, once the iPhone app ships with Plus on
fix_line: Keep every feature open on iPhone until Apple payment exists, and show App Store words there instead of Google Play

title: The member app ships dozens of open-source packages but shows none of their licence notices
what: The Credits page lists four things: the RepDB pictures, the Everkinetic drawings, the body map and the fonts. The app is built from about fifty outside packages (React Native, Expo and others), most under licences such as MIT or Apache that ask for their copyright notice to travel with every copy. No screen, file or build step in the member app gathers those notices.
expected: Settings has an 'Open-source licences' list (made at build time from the packages) or the Credits page links to one.
fix_line: Add a build step that collects every package's licence and show it from the Credits page

title: The record of where exercise pictures come from leaves out the main picture source, and the Credits page undersells what was changed
what: The exercise library's 'where everything comes from' record lists only the Everkinetic drawings, yet the start and end pictures most members see come from RepDB, and 238 pictures are MettleUp's own. RepDB's terms (credit line, no reuse as a dataset, no AI restyling) are written nowhere in that record. The Credits page says the RepDB pictures were only 'resized', while the picture list says they were resized and recoloured.
expected: The rights record names every picture source with its terms (RepDB, Everkinetic, our own pictures and clips), and the Credits page says truthfully what was changed.
fix_line: Add RepDB and our own pictures to the rights record and make the Credits change note say recoloured

title: The Play app asks for "display over other apps" though nothing in it uses that
what: The release app lists the permission to draw over other apps. It came from the starter template, which keeps it only for test builds; no screen or native part of MettleUp ever uses it. Google Play and the phone's app info show it to members.
expected: Every permission in the Play app has a reason the member can see; an unused one is left out of the release build.
fix_line: Remove the draw-over-other-apps permission from the release app and from the approved permission list

title: The app ships many open-source parts but never shows their licence notices
what: The Credits page lists only the exercise pictures, the body map and the fonts. The app also ships open-source code (the app framework, Google's Android libraries, Health Connect and Play billing libraries) whose licences ask that their copyright and licence notice go with the app. No screen or file in the app shows them.
expected: An open-source licences page (or file) in the app lists every shipped library with its licence notice.
fix_line: Add an open-source licences list made from the build's library list and open it from Credits

title: Nobody wrote down where the main rest-over chime came from
what: The bell, beep and whistle sounds are made by our own script from plain maths, so they are ours. The default chime they copy their loudness from is not made by that script, and no file says who made it or under what licence. It plays on every rest and is copied into the notification sounds.
expected: Every sound the app ships has a recorded maker and licence, like the pictures and fonts on the Credits page.
fix_line: Record where the chime came from; if unknown, remake it with the same script as the other sounds

title: On an iPhone the welcome would offer Continue with Google but no Sign in with Apple
what: The welcome screen shows Continue with Google whenever this build can sign in or look in Google Drive. Nothing checks for an iPhone, and the app has no Sign in with Apple at all. Apple's review rules ask an app that offers a sign-in through another company to also offer one that keeps the email private, so an iPhone build would be refused as it stands.
expected: When the iPhone app ships, the welcome offers Sign in with Apple (or an equal private way) next to Google, or hides Google sign-in on iPhone.
fix_line: Add Sign in with Apple to the welcome and account screens before the iPhone release, or hide Google sign-in there

title: Importing routines from a Hevy link copies Hevy's pages through a hidden browser without Hevy's permission
what: A member pastes a Hevy share link and the app opens Hevy's web page out of sight, listens in on the data Hevy's page loads for itself, and copies the routines out of it. The link is often someone else's shared folder. Hevy's terms say nothing from their app may be copied or reused without written permission, and Hevy offers an official way in that needs their approval. Hevy could block it at any time or complain to us or to Google Play.
expected: Routines come in only from the member's own export file, or through Hevy's official way in with Hevy's approval, or the owner decides in writing that he accepts this risk.
fix_line: Owner decides: ask Hevy for approval, switch to their official way in, or drop the link import and keep the file import

title: Google Play asks for the app's top and bottom bar colours to be updated for Android 15, and the app has not done it
what: Play Console shows a recommended action on the live version: the app still uses old ways of colouring the phone's top and bottom bars that Android 15 has retired. The app frame sets the top bar style on every start. On newer phones the bars may look wrong, and Google may turn this into a requirement.
expected: The app draws behind the bars in the way Android 15 expects, and the Play Console recommendation is gone.
fix_line: Move the bar colouring to the Android 15 way and check the Play recommendation clears

title: Google Play wants MettleUp's EU trader status declared by 1 February 2027
what: The Play Console dashboard shows a banner asking the account to declare whether it is a trader in the EU by 1 February 2027. If it is not done, Google may stop showing the app to people in the EU.
expected: The owner fills in the trader declaration in Play Console before the date.
who: the owner; members in the EU
fix_line: Owner declares trader status in Play Console

title: A plain feedback message marked Question waits for a reply HQ cannot send
what: When a feedback message that did not come through the help box is marked Question, Needs you counts it as a help question waiting for your reply, but its card in HQ has no reply box. It can never be answered from HQ and stays on the list until it is marked done.
expected: Every message Needs you calls waiting for a reply can be answered from HQ, or HQ says plainly that this one cannot be answered and how to reach the person instead.
who: members and gyms who sent feedback, and the owner
how_often: every plain feedback message marked Question
fix_line: Leave plain feedback out of the waiting-for-reply count, or show a clear line on the card saying it cannot be answered in the app

title: HQ tells you the wrong place for the gym’s own support switch
what: The support access card says the gym opens access from Settings, Your data. The admin app moved that card to Help and feedback, and its own What’s new says so. On a call you would send the owner to the wrong screen.
expected: HQ names the screen where the switch really is: Help and feedback.
who: owner, gym owners on a support call
how_often: every time support is asked for
fix_line: Change the words to say Help and feedback

title: The welcome message to a new gym owner gives no address for the admin app
what: The message HQ makes for a new or locked-out owner says to open the MettleUp admin app and type the code, but has no link or web address. A new owner does not know where that app is, and the code stops working after 30 minutes.
expected: The message carries the admin app’s address so the owner can tap it and sign in before the code runs out.
how_often: every new gym and every sign-in reset
fix_line: Add the admin app address to the message

title: HQ warns only about the logs key; every other key can stop working without a word
what: HQ shows a warning when the Supabase logs key fails or is near its end. When the phone pop-up key, the admin app alert key or the Cloudflare usage key is missing or refused, the server only writes a hidden log line, and the System page says errors and outages are not connected yet. Member reply pop-ups or gym alerts could stop for weeks without you knowing.
expected: Each key HQ relies on shows on the System page as working, missing or refused, and a refused key shows in Needs you.
who: owner, members waiting for replies, gyms waiting for alerts
how_often: whenever a key ends or is revoked
fix_line: Record each key’s last result and show it on the System page and in Needs you

title: Some HQ steps end in tell Claude, with no written steps for anyone else
what: Signing a gym out everywhere can say the gym has an old browser key and to tell Claude. Renewing the logs key ends with tell Claude its end date. Nothing in HQ says what Claude then does, so if Claude is not at hand the job cannot be finished.
expected: Each step HQ asks for is something you can finish yourself in HQ, or links to written steps.
how_often: rare: an old browser key, or once a year for the logs key
fix_line: Give the key end date a box in HQ and the old browser key its own remove button

title: Needs you says nothing when the payments to confirm cannot be counted
what: If the count of payments waiting to be confirmed, or of online payments to check, cannot be read, Needs you simply leaves the line out. The could-not-count warning looks only at leads, feedback, help questions and new gyms. You may think no gym is waiting for its plan while one is.
expected: A payment count that could not be read shows the same could-not-count warning.
fix_line: Tell a failed payment read apart from switched off and show the warning for it

title: Complaints and refund requests by email or phone have no place in HQ
what: The contact page promises to confirm a complaint within 48 hours and settle it within a month, and asks people to write about payments and refunds. HQ can write down only delete requests that came by email or phone. Complaints, refund asks and plan changes by email have no list and no clock, so a missed one is not noticed.
expected: HQ has one place to write down a request that came by email or phone, with its promised deadline counted in Needs you.
who: gym owners and members who email or call
how_often: every complaint or refund ask by email or phone
fix_line: Let the delete request list also take complaints, refunds and plan changes, each with its deadline

title: Nothing reaches you about a new lead or help question unless HQ is open
what: HQ beeps and pops up only while it is open in a tab, and says so: when HQ is closed, no alert comes to your phone. The website tells a gym we will call you soon and the apps say we reply as soon as we can, so a lead or a question can wait days unseen.
expected: A new lead or a help question waiting for a reply reaches your phone even when HQ is closed, for example a daily summary or a phone pop-up.
who: owner, gyms asking for a demo, people asking for help
how_often: every day HQ is not opened
fix_line: Send a phone pop-up or a daily summary for new leads and waiting questions

title: An owner with no credits who asks MettleUp for more is sent back to the AI Assistant
what: The AI credits sheet tells the owner to write to MettleUp in Help and feedback. When the gym has no credits left, the message sent there gets a help-page answer saying the gym has no credits and to get more from the AI Assistant, with an Open AI Assistant button. The owner goes round in a circle; only a small last line says the team reads every message.
expected: A credit request written in Help and feedback says plainly that MettleUp got it and will add the credits, with no button back to where the owner started.
how_often: every time an owner with no credits asks for more
fix_line: When the help box has no credits to answer, say the request reached MettleUp and drop the button back to the AI Assistant

title: The week summary's main button promises to send it to the owner's WhatsApp, but nothing can
what: The week summary answer card has one big button, Send this to my WhatsApp. It only asks the AI that sentence again. The AI's list of tasks has no way to send anything to the owner's own WhatsApp, so at best the owner gets a 'cannot do' card, and the tap may use one of the day's questions.
expected: Only buttons that work are shown: either the summary really goes to the owner's WhatsApp, or the button is not there.
how_often: every time the week summary is asked
fix_line: Remove the Send this to my WhatsApp button until sending to the owner is built

title: A how-to question is sent to Help and feedback empty, where asking again may cost credits
what: When the owner asks the AI Assistant how to do something, or asks for something it cannot do, the card offers Open Help and feedback. The owner's question is not carried over, so he must type it again. In Help and feedback a question is paid from the gym's AI credits, while the owner's own questions in the AI Assistant are free.
expected: The question goes with the owner to Help and feedback already filled in, and moving it there costs nothing extra.
fix_line: Open Help and feedback with the owner's question already in the box

title: If the AI key goes missing, or one usage table cannot be read, the AI Assistant quietly disappears for every owner
what: The server answers 'switched off' when the AI key is not set, and also when a usage table cannot be read. The admin app then hides the AI Assistant with no word to the owner. A missing key is not even logged, so nobody at MettleUp is told. The assistant also borrows the help box's key when its own is missing, so one lost key can stop both.
expected: A missing or expired key, or a database problem, raises an alert to MettleUp, and the owner sees a short 'not working right now' line instead of the feature vanishing.
how_often: whenever a key is removed, expires or the table read fails
fix_line: Keep 'switched off' for the planned switch only; log and alert on a missing key or table error and show the owner a calm problem line

title: Every AI credit top-up is a hand job hidden among ordinary help messages
what: Buying credits in the admin app is not built. The owner writes a free-text message in Help and feedback and MettleUp must spot it among all other help messages and add credits by hand on the HQ page. The message carries no mark that it is a credit request, and nothing reminds MettleUp it is waiting.
expected: A credit request reaches MettleUp marked as one, with the amount asked, so it cannot be missed on a busy day.
fix_line: Send credit requests as their own marked kind of message, with the number of credits

title: The AI Assistant help page leaves out the daily question limit and how to get credits
what: The help page says questions are free and the credits show at the top. It never says there is a daily number of questions after which the ask box locks until tomorrow, and never says how to get more credits (write to MettleUp). An owner who hits either has no help page that explains it.
expected: The help page names the daily question limit and says how to get more credits.
how_often: when an owner hits the limit or runs out
fix_line: Add two lines to the AI Assistant help page: the daily limit and how to get credits

title: When the gym is paused or its plan runs out, desk staff are told to download the data, which only an owner can do
what: The paused-gym message and the plan-ran-out message are shown to everyone at the desk. Both say you can still download your data (from Settings). Front desk staff never see the download card, because only an owner may use it.
expected: Staff are told to ask the owner; only the owner is told about downloading the data.
how_often: every time a gym is paused or read-only
fix_line: Give staff their own line: ask your gym owner

title: A locked-out owner's last way back in is an email that only one person can act on, with no record in HQ
what: An owner with no other signed-in device and no second owner is told to email MettleUp with gym name and mobile, and is promised a call and a code. That email lands in the general contact mailbox. HQ has no place to note the request or its state, nothing alerts anyone, and only MettleUp HQ can make the code. If that one person is away, the gym cannot open its desk.
expected: A locked-out request is logged and tracked like other support work, with a promised reply time and a second person able to make the code.
who: owners with one owner and one device
how_often: rare, but blocks the whole desk
fix_line: Track locked-out requests in HQ and give a second person HQ access

title: The data agreement tells the owner to open support access in Settings, but it is now in Help and feedback
what: The data agreement says MettleUp looks only in a window the owner opens in Settings. The MettleUp access card was moved to Help and feedback, so an owner who follows the agreement will not find it.
expected: The agreement names the screen where the card really is.
fix_line: Change the agreement line to Help and feedback

title: Help has no page on working without internet, and its forgot-PIN line names only one way back in
what: The offline front desk (look up members, take payments, then send them later) is live but no help page explains it. The staff and sign-in help page says only: where you are still signed in, make yourself a code. It leaves out the WhatsApp way, asking another owner, and emailing MettleUp, which the sign-in screen offers.
expected: Help covers the offline desk and lists every way back in that the sign-in screen offers.
fix_line: Add an offline desk help page and the full ways back in

title: The admin app tells owners to message MettleUp on WhatsApp but never gives a number or a button
what: When Branding cannot save because the server step is missing, the owner reads 'Message MettleUp on WhatsApp to switch it on'. Branches, entry machines and trainer pages say the same. Nowhere in the admin app is MettleUp's WhatsApp number or a WhatsApp button, so the owner has no way to follow the line. Other screens send owners to Help and feedback instead, so the paths do not agree. The Branding case is also a fault for every gym (a missing server step), not a per-gym switch, and nobody at MettleUp is told it happened.
expected: Every 'contact MettleUp' line leads somewhere the owner can tap: Help and feedback, or a WhatsApp button with the real number. A missing server step is reported to MettleUp, not left to the owner.
fix_line: Change these lines to point at Help and feedback (or add a real WhatsApp button), and report the missing server step

title: When saving the gym look fails for an unknown reason, nobody at MettleUp ever hears of it
what: A failed Branding save or 'Use MettleUp's look' shows 'That didn't save. Please try again.' The real error is not written to the log and is not sent as a crash report, because the error is caught on the screen. If saves start failing for many gyms, MettleUp only learns when an owner complains.
expected: An unexpected save failure is logged and sent to MettleUp's crash reports (without personal data), so support can see and fix it.
fix_line: Log the real error and send it as a crash report before showing the calm message

title: A replaced or removed gym logo stays public on our server for ever
what: Every logo upload is saved as a new picture with a new name. Changing the logo, removing it, or going back to MettleUp's look only drops the link; the old picture stays public at its old address with a one-year cache. The confirm box says it 'removes your logo'. Only deleting the whole gym from HQ cleans logos up.
expected: An old logo is deleted from our server when the gym replaces or removes it, or the words say it is only taken off the app.
fix_line: Delete the previous logo file when a new look is saved or cleared

title: Every saved gym logo link names one database project, so moving to a new one breaks all logos
what: Logos and product photos are saved with the database company's own project address written into the link, and the server accepts only that address. If MettleUp ever has to move to a new project (account lost, project closed, region move), every gym's saved logo link points at the old place and there is no written way to rewrite them.
expected: Saved picture links use MettleUp's own address (or a path only), so a project move does not break them; or a written move plan says how links are rewritten.
fix_line: Save picture paths, not full project links, or write the move plan

title: The admin app still relies on the founder's personal web address
what: The admin app treats two addresses as its own: the MettleUp one and an old address on the founder's personal domain, which the code says 'stays for good'. Desks that saved the old address keep using it. If that personal domain lapses or is lost, those desks stop working, and the code gives no end date or plan to move them.
expected: Only MettleUp-owned addresses carry the admin app; the old personal address forwards to the new one with a set end date.
fix_line: Forward the old address to the MettleUp one and set a date to drop it

title: The Branding help article skips half the screen
what: The help article walks through upload logo, brand colour, headings and save. It never mentions the colour suggested from the logo, 'Use my own background tone', the 'Easy to read?' check, 'Remove logo' or the free tip for logos with a photo behind them, so an owner asking about those gets no help article.
expected: The help article names every part of the Branding screen in the order the owner sees it.
fix_line: Add the missing parts to the Branding help article

title: When a payment, sale or new member fails to save, MettleUp never hears of it
what: Every desk form (collect payment, sell or renew, add or edit member, freeze, change start date, cancel receipt) catches a failed save and shows the desk a message such as Please try again. The failure is never sent anywhere. The crash reports only cover errors nobody caught. So a gym whose payments keep failing is invisible to you until the owner complains, and then there is no record of what went wrong. The message also gives the desk no way to reach help.
expected: A failed money or member save is reported to MettleUp (no personal data), and the message tells the desk where to get help if trying again does not work.
fix_line: Send each failed desk save to the existing crash report, and add a help line to the failure message

title: Several desk tasks have no help answer, and the help check never looks at these forms
what: The help library has no answer for changing a future start date, taking part payment at a sale, selling a personal training pack with the plan, the front desk money limits (10% off, payment date 31 days back) or taking payments with no internet. The help check only looks at full screens, never at these pop-up forms, so a new or changed form never asks for help words.
expected: Each desk form task has a help answer, and the help check covers the forms too.
fix_line: Write the missing help answers and make the help check include the forms folder

title: Help says a cancelled receipt always goes back onto the member's dues
what: The help answer says the amount of a cancelled receipt goes back into the member's dues. The form itself knows that when the plan was cancelled, nothing goes back onto the dues. An owner following the help waits for a due that never shows.
expected: Help says the amount goes back onto the dues unless the plan was cancelled.
how_often: each receipt cancelled on a cancelled plan
fix_line: Add the cancelled-plan exception to the help answer

title: A reply from the MettleUp team reaches only the browser the question was sent from
what: Questions sent from Help and feedback carry no name or mobile number, and the team's reply can be fetched only by the same browser that sent it. An owner who asks from the desk computer and later looks on a phone, a new computer, or after clearing the browser never sees the reply, and nothing else tells the gym a reply came. After 30 newer questions an old one is dropped and its reply is lost too. A 'delete our gym' request sent the same way gets its answer the same way.
expected: A reply from MettleUp reaches the gym wherever the owner signs in, for example tied to the gym and the person who asked, or also shown in the gym's notification bell.
who: owners and desk staff who ask MettleUp for help
how_often: every time the person who asked looks from another device or browser
fix_line: Keep each question with the gym and the person who asked, so the reply shows wherever they sign in

title: A gym that pays MettleUp by UPI gets no warning before its plan ends
