what: The 'your MettleUp plan ends in N days' reminder on Today shows only while online paying is switched on. The plan-ended banner and its limits follow a different switch. With limits on and online paying off (the page then says to pay by UPI or bank transfer), the owner hears nothing until the plan has already ended and the 7 extra days have started, and MettleUp has to chase each gym by hand.
expected: Every owner whose plan is near its end sees the reminder, with the way to pay that is open at the time.
who: owners who pay MettleUp by UPI or bank transfer
how_often: every plan end while online paying is off
fix_line: Show the plan-end reminder whenever the plan has an end date, pointing to whichever way of paying is open

title: Several screens say 'Message MettleUp' but give no way to do it
what: When paying MettleUp is not ready or has no payment details, when a gym has more than one branch, when a payment is not confirmed, and when trainer pages are not switched on, the panel tells the owner to message MettleUp (once 'on WhatsApp'). None of these lines has a button, a number or a link, and the panel holds no MettleUp WhatsApp number at all. The owner who wants to pay is left to find a way himself.
expected: Every 'message MettleUp' line carries one tap that reaches MettleUp: Help and feedback, or the support email or WhatsApp number.
how_often: every time one of these states shows
fix_line: Add an Open Help and feedback button (or the support contact) under each 'message MettleUp' line, and drop 'on WhatsApp' unless a number is shown

title: 'Needs you' on Today leaves out people who asked to join online
what: The 'Needs you' count, badge, list and sound cover plan requests, check-in numbers, shop orders, member questions and member messages. A person who asked to join (or paid online and waits for approval) is not one of them, even though the closed-app alerts treat a joining request as urgent. An owner who works from the 'Needs you' list can leave a paid joiner waiting.
expected: A waiting online join request counts in 'Needs you' and takes the owner to it, the same as the alerts do.
fix_line: Add waiting online join requests as one more kind in 'Needs you'

title: The Pay MettleUp code still says its server part is not live, though it is
what: The top note of the Pay MettleUp rules says the server change is not applied, while a note further down and the live database both show it is. Whoever picks up billing next, without the owner to ask, reads two answers.
expected: One true line about whether paying MettleUp is live.
evidence: data:live database function list holds owner_pay_mettleup and owner_report_mettleup_payment (catalog read 2026-11-21)
fix_line: Change the top note to say the payment server part is live

title: Owners are told to 'Message MettleUp on WhatsApp' with no number or button to do it
what: When branches or entry machines are not ready, or a limit is reached, the admin app says 'Message MettleUp on WhatsApp' but gives no number, link or button. MettleUp's number is only on the website's contact page. The Pro card says something else again: write in Help and feedback. The entry machine guide says 'tell us' with no way to reach anyone.
expected: Every 'contact MettleUp' line opens the same place in one tap: a WhatsApp button to MettleUp's number, or Help and feedback.
how_often: each time one of these messages shows
fix_line: Give every contact line one button that opens MettleUp's WhatsApp or Help and feedback

title: The app promises MettleUp will raise a limit or sort out a machine clash, but MettleUp has no way to do either
what: 'You already have 10 branches... message us if you need more' and 'You can add up to 10 machines... message us' point the owner to MettleUp, but both limits are fixed in the server for every gym; MettleUp cannot raise them for one gym. 'This machine is already added to a gym... we will check it' promises a check, but the HQ app has nothing about entry machines, so the founder would have to dig in the database by hand.
expected: Either MettleUp has a way to raise a limit or free a machine for one gym, or the words do not promise it.
who: owners with many branches or machines, and the founder
fix_line: Add a per-gym limit and a machine look-up to HQ, or change the words

title: A branch can be added but never closed, and leaving MettleUp says nothing about branches
what: An owner can add a branch, open it and rename the business, but there is no way to close or remove one branch, in the app or on the server. The delete request speaks of 'this gym', and the written delete steps for MettleUp never mention branches, so an owner with several branches does not know if one request covers all of them.
expected: An owner can close a branch they no longer run, and the delete request and its steps say what happens to every branch.
who: owners with more than one branch
how_often: when a branch shuts or the owner leaves
fix_line: Add Close a branch, and say in the delete request and its steps which branches it covers

title: Branches are live but have no help article, and the help check cannot see them
what: The All branches page, the branch switcher, adding a branch and checking in a visitor from another branch are live, but no help article covers them, so the help and the AI help cannot answer branch questions. The check that every screen has help only looks at one folder and at files named like screens, so it never noticed.
expected: A help article on branches, and the help check covers the branch pages.
who: owners with more than one branch
fix_line: Write a branches help article and widen the help check to the branch pages

title: Someone trying the demo gym has no way to ask MettleUp a question
what: In the demo gym, Help and feedback is switched off ('This works in your own gym'), and the only link in the demo bar is 'Leave the demo'. A gym owner who is curious has no WhatsApp, phone or form to reach MettleUp from inside the demo.
expected: The demo shows a one-tap way to talk to MettleUp, like a WhatsApp button.
fix_line: Add a Talk to MettleUp WhatsApp button to the demo bar and the switched-off Help page

title: One secret key locks every gym's payment company keys, with no second key and no written way back
what: Each gym's Razorpay or Cashfree keys are locked with one MettleUp secret key kept on the server. There is no second key and no way to change it, and no written record of where a copy is kept. Cloudflare does not show a saved secret again. If that key is lost or replaced, every gym's payment connection stops working and each owner must connect again.
expected: A written, safe copy of the key outside the laptop, and a way to change it without breaking every gym.
how_often: once, if the key is lost
fix_line: Write down where the key's copy lives, and let the server accept an old and a new key

title: The old address on the founder's personal domain must work for good, but nothing records when the domains run out
what: The old admin address sits on the founder's personal domain and is kept for good, for old phones and printed posters. The new address and the entry machine address are on mettleup.fit. Nothing written says when either domain must be renewed or who renews it; if the personal domain lapses, old phones and posters stop reaching the gym server. The entry machine address is still 'to be agreed'.
expected: A written list of both domains with their renewal dates, auto-renew on, and the entry machine address fixed.
fix_line: Write both domains, their renewal dates and auto-renew into the setup notes

title: The entry machine guide says 'the address MettleUp gives you', but the screen writes the address in
what: The written machine set-up guide tells the owner to wait for MettleUp to give them a server address. The app's own set-up steps already show the address. An owner reading the guide waits for a message that never comes.
expected: The guide names the address, or says it is shown on the Entry machines page.
fix_line: Say in the guide that the address is on the Entry machines page

title: Help and feedback gives no other way to reach MettleUp when sending fails
what: The Help and feedback page has only a message box. When sending fails, the owner is told to check the internet and try again, even if the help service itself is down. The page shows no email address, phone or WhatsApp number. The MettleUp support email is shown only on the sign-in welcome screen, which an owner who is already signed in never sees.
expected: The Help and feedback page also shows the MettleUp support email (or another working contact) so an owner can still reach a person when the message box fails.
who: owners and desk staff who need help
how_often: whenever the help service cannot be reached
fix_line: Show the support email line under the message box on Help and feedback

title: Door machines are set up with one fixed web address typed in by hand
what: The setup steps tell the gym to type one MettleUp web address and port into each finger or face machine. If that address ever has to change (domain lost, host moved), every machine at every gym stops sending entries until someone at the gym types the new address on each machine. Nothing written says how that move would be done. The feature is not switched on yet.
expected: A written way to move machines to a new address, and the address kept on a domain whose renewal and ownership are recorded, before the feature goes live.
how_often: once, if the address ever changes
fix_line: Write the move-to-a-new-address steps and record who holds the gate domain before launch

title: Paying MettleUp has no help answer, because the help list still calls it not live
what: Every online owner sees a Your MettleUp plan card in Settings that opens Pay MettleUp, and the live server already answers it. The help library has no answer for picking a plan, paying by UPI or bank transfer, sending the reference number, a payment that is not confirmed, or the MettleUp receipt. The help check lets both screens off with a note saying they are not live yet, so nothing flags the gap. An owner stuck on paying asks in Help and feedback, which is the owner's own inbox to answer by hand.
expected: A help answer for paying MettleUp and its receipt, written now that the page is live, and the not live yet notes removed so the help check covers both screens.
fix_line: Write the help answer for paying MettleUp and drop the not live notes

title: After a gym disconnects its shop, members can still place orders that nobody will ever see
what: Disconnect the shop only makes this browser forget the gym's key. The gym, its code and its products stay switched on on our server, so members who joined can keep ordering (and, where paying online is on, paying). The owner no longer has any screen that shows those orders, and the screen says only that members and payments are still here.
expected: Disconnecting closes the shop on the server too (members are told the shop is closed and cannot order), or the owner is warned the shop stays open for members.
who: members of a browser-only gym that turned the shop off, and that gym
how_often: every order placed after a disconnect
fix_line: Make Disconnect close the shop on the server, or block new orders for a gym whose shop is off

title: A gym kept in the browser that turns on the shop can lose its shop for good with one cleared browser
what: For a gym not signed in with a mobile number, the only key to its shop, orders and app members is kept in this browser. A lost laptop, a cleared browser or a new computer means the shop can never be opened again; there is no recovery and no written way back. When the key stops working the panel quietly drops it with no message for a real gym, while members keep the old gym code.
expected: Turning on the shop needs a sign-in (or offers one first), so the gym can get back in from any device; a lost key shows a plain message and a way to recover.
who: owners of browser-only gyms that turned the shop on, and their app members
how_often: each time such a browser is lost, cleared or replaced
fix_line: Ask the owner to sign in before turning on the shop, and say plainly when the key is gone

title: A gym delete request is sent through the AI help box, with the gym's name, code, phone and the asker's name
what: Tapping Send delete request posts the request as an ordinary help question. The help box saves it and then asks the AI for an answer, so the gym name, gym code, gym phone and the person's name go to the AI company, although the help box promises it never sends the gym code. The request and the AI's reply also land in the owner's Your questions list like any how-to question, and it shares the 20-a-day message limit.
expected: A delete request goes straight to MettleUp's delete list without an AI answer, sends nothing to the AI company, and is not mixed into the help questions.
fix_line: Send delete requests to their own box that skips the AI answer and the question history

title: Help says gym alerts work only while the admin app is open, but they now come with it closed
what: The Needs you help article ends with: alerts work while the admin app is open in a tab. The admin app now sends alerts to the phone or computer with the app closed, and the owner can pick Instantly, Once a day or Once a week in Settings. Help never mentions the closed-app alerts or the timing choice, so an owner may keep a tab open all day for nothing, or not know why alerts come once a day.
expected: The help article says alerts also come with the app closed and explains where to pick when they come.
fix_line: Rewrite the alerts help to cover closed-app alerts and the timing choice

title: When a plan ends and the gym goes read-only, the line on Today gives no way to reach MettleUp
what: The stopped-paying line (hidden for now) says nothing can be changed and offers only Pay now to the owner; desk staff are told to ask the owner. Unlike the paused-gym message, it gives no MettleUp email. The support line meant for every such place is used only on the first sign-in screen.
expected: The read-only and basic-mode lines show the MettleUp support email, like the paused-gym message does.
who: owners and desk staff of a lapsed gym
how_often: once the plan gate is switched on
fix_line: Add the support email line under the read-only and basic-mode messages

title: Help never explains checking a member's workout code, and says the desk gives the reward days
what: The workout offer help article covers starting an offer and says the front desk gives the days members earned. It never mentions Check workout code, the step where the desk types the member's code and sees how many workouts match a check-in. On that screen only the owner can give the days; the desk is told to ask the owner.
expected: Help explains the workout code check and says who can give the reward.
fix_line: Add the workout code check to the workout offer help and fix who gives the days

title: A damaged or full Drive backup tells the member to tap Back up now, a button that no longer exists
what: When a Google Drive backup cannot be read, the member reads 'Make a new backup with Back up now'. When Drive is full, 'Free some space, then tap Back up now'. Uploading to Drive was taken off every screen, so there is no such button and the member is left with no next step.
expected: Each message names a button that is really on the screen, for example Download my data, or says the old Drive backup cannot be used and what to do instead.
who: members restoring an old Drive backup
how_often: each time a Drive backup is damaged or Drive is full
fix_line: Change the two lines to point at Download my data, or say the old backup cannot be used

title: When Drive backup is broken in a build, the member is told to tell their gym, who cannot fix it
what: If the build's Google setup is missing, the Drive restore message ends 'and tell your gym'. The gym owner cannot fix Google setup, and members with no gym have nobody to tell. Help and feedback, which reaches MettleUp, is not mentioned.
expected: The message points to Settings, Help and feedback so the report reaches MettleUp.
who: members restoring from Drive, most of all members with no gym
how_often: every time the build's Google setup is wrong
fix_line: Say 'tell us in Settings, Help and feedback' instead of 'tell your gym'

title: If Google sign-in breaks for a new app build, every member silently loses their only backup and MettleUp is never told
what: The MettleUp account is the one backup, and it works only while Google Cloud has this build's signing fingerprint registered. If that is missing (a new signing key, a lost laptop, a new sideload key), every member reads 'Google sign-in is not ready in this version' and nothing is saved. The real reason is written only to the phone's own log. Nothing reaches MettleUp, so the owner finds out only if a member writes in.
expected: A sign-in failure of this kind is reported to MettleUp automatically, or a release check proves Google sign-in works on the signed build before it ships, and a written note says which fingerprints must be registered.
who: every member of a build whose signing key is not registered
how_often: rare, but all at once when it happens
fix_line: Send this one failure to MettleUp and add a signed-build sign-in check to the release steps

title: The coach's model names are fixed in the app and will stop working when the AI companies retire them
what: The coach (now switched off) offers fixed model names for Claude, OpenAI and Groq. AI companies retire model names without warning; Groq already did this once to another of our apps. The code itself says to update it if one stops working, but nothing tells MettleUp when that happens.
expected: Before the coach is switched on, model names are checked automatically or a retired model falls back to a working one and is reported.
who: members using the coach with their own key, once it is switched on
how_often: each time a provider retires a model
fix_line: Fall back to a working model and report it, before the coach goes live

title: The crash screen and the Couldn't save line give no way to ask for help
what: When a screen crashes, the member sees only Try again, Go back and Go to Workout. When saving keeps failing, the line over every screen says to free some space and has no button at all. Neither offers Help and feedback or any way to tell MettleUp what happened, so a member stuck on a screen that crashes every time, or whose saves keep failing after freeing space, has to find the help box in Settings on their own. The crash itself is reported to MettleUp automatically, but without the member's words.
expected: The crash screen, and the Couldn't save line once it has stayed a while, offer a Get help or Tell us what happened button that opens Help and feedback.
fix_line: Add a Get help button to the crash screen and to a long-standing save problem that opens Help and feedback

title: Member help says nothing about the update screen, save problems, the crash screen or the Charts page's newer parts
what: The AI help answers only from the help articles. No member article mentions the full-screen 'A new MettleUp is here' with Update now, the watch app update pop-up, the 'Couldn't save' line, or the crash screen. The progress article says Charts shows 'your last 7 days, sets for each muscle group, and your main exercises', but the Charts page also has the body map with a 7, 30 or 90 day switch, the Balance check card and the Strength score with Add body weight. A member who asks about any of these gets no answer, or a partial one.
expected: The member help explains updating the app (phone and watch), what to do when saving fails or a screen crashes, and each card on the Charts page.
how_often: every member who asks help about these
fix_line: Add member help lines for app updates, save problems, the crash screen and the Charts page cards

title: A reply from the MettleUp team reaches only the phone that asked, and only for 30 days
what: Help and feedback asks for no email or number. The team's reply is fetched only by the phone that sent the question, using an id made on that install, and only for questions sent in the last 30 days. A member who erases the app, moves to a new phone, or gets a late reply never sees it, and the team has no other way to reach them.
expected: A member can leave an optional way to be reached, or the team can see that a reply will never arrive and close the question some other way.
how_often: every reply sent after 30 days, or after the member changes or resets the phone
fix_line: Offer an optional email or WhatsApp number in the help box, and show the team when a reply cannot reach the phone

title: Gym sync sign-in has no way back for a forgotten password
what: Connecting to the gym with email, password and gym code, and signing in again after the session ends, asks only for email and password. There is no forgotten password link and no line saying who to ask, so a member who forgot the password cannot reconnect. This card is behind a switch today.
expected: A forgotten password link, or a line naming who helps, beside the password box.
who: members using gym sync, once it is switched on
how_often: every time a member forgets the password
fix_line: Add a forgotten password link before this card is switched on

title: A reply from the MettleUp team reaches only the phone the question was sent from
what: A member's help question carries no name or mobile number. The team's reply can be fetched only by the same phone install, using an id and a secret kept on that phone. A backup does not carry them, so after a new phone, a reinstall or a restore the member never sees replies to earlier questions, and nothing else tells them a reply came. After 30 newer questions an old one is dropped and its reply is lost too.
expected: A reply from MettleUp reaches the member wherever they use the app, for example tied to their MettleUp account when they have one, or carried in their backup.
who: members who ask for help and later change or reset their phone
how_often: every time a member changes phone or reinstalls before reading a reply
fix_line: Tie help questions to the member's account when signed in, or carry the question secrets in the backup

title: When a help message cannot be sent, the member app gives no other way to reach MettleUp
what: Help and feedback is the only way a member can reach MettleUp from the app. When both help addresses fail, the member is told to check the internet and try again, even when the help service itself is down. The app holds no MettleUp email address, phone or WhatsApp number to fall back on.
expected: When sending fails, the member is shown a working MettleUp contact (for example the support email) so a person can still be reached.
how_often: whenever the help service is down or unreachable
fix_line: Show the MettleUp support email beside the 'Couldn't send' line

title: Failures the member app catches itself never reach MettleUp
what: Crash reports cover only two cases: an error nothing caught, and a screen that crashed and showed Try again. Everything the app catches and handles quietly is only written to the phone's own log: a help message that could not be sent, a Google Play purchase that failed, a screen that shows Couldn't load, a background task that failed. MettleUp learns of these only if a member writes in, so a fault hitting many phones can stay unseen.
expected: Caught failures that stop a member's task are counted and sent to MettleUp (without personal data), so you see them before members complain.
who: you, and members hit by a silent fault
fix_line: Send a short, no-personal-data report for caught failures on key tasks, limited per run

title: The MettleUp Plus help page says gym members always get every feature free, but they lose them after their plan ends
what: The member help page says members of a gym that uses MettleUp get every feature free. The app's rule gives them the paid features only while their gym plan is open; when the owner's lock is on (the start setting), the features lock 7 days after the plan ends. A member whose plan ended is told by help that it should be free. MettleUp Plus is still switched off, so nobody sees this yet.
expected: The member help page says the features are free while the gym plan is active, and may lock some days after it ends, as the owner's help page says.
how_often: every time, once MettleUp Plus is switched on
fix_line: Change the member help page to say free while the gym plan is active

title: The member app is hard-wired to the founder's personal GitHub account and personal web address
what: Phones that installed the app from GitHub learn about new versions only by asking one GitHub account's release page, and What's new falls back to the same place. The help box and crash reports keep a backup address on the founder's personal domain, written to stay for good. These are fixed inside every installed copy: if that GitHub account is renamed, locked or lost, or the personal domain lapses, older phones silently stop hearing of updates and lose their backup help address, and only a new app version can change it. Nothing in this part of the app says who holds these accounts or how to get back in.
expected: The app's update, help and crash addresses sit on MettleUp-owned names only, with a written note of who holds each account and how to recover it.
how_often: only if the account or domain is lost, but then for every older phone
fix_line: Move update and backup addresses to MettleUp-owned names and write down who holds each account

title: When the rest alert, the watch link, Health Connect or a Plus payment fails on a member's phone, MettleUp never hears of it
what: The phone's notification, watch, widget, Health Connect and payment parts catch their own failures and write them only to the phone's own log (well over 100 such lines in this area): a rest-over sound that is missing, an alert ring that did not play, a watch message not passed on, a workout not sent to Health Connect, a Play payment answer. The crash reports that do reach MettleUp only carry errors nothing caught and screens that crashed. So a rest alert that stays silent on one phone model, or Health Connect sending that stops for everyone, shows up only if a member writes in.
expected: The failures that break a promise to the member (rest alert, watch link, Health Connect sending, payment) are counted and sent to MettleUp the same way crash reports are, without personal data, so the owner sees them in his daily check.
who: every member; the owner, who cannot see the fault
how_often: whenever one of these parts fails
fix_line: Send a short, data-free note to MettleUp's crash inbox when a promised alert, watch link, Health Connect send or payment fails

title: A member on the GitHub copy of the app gets a watch app from Google Play that can never talk to their phone
what: The phone and the watch only talk when both apps carry the same signing key. The app's own notes say the GitHub copy of the phone app is signed with a different key from the Play copy, and the phone sends members to the watch's Play Store to install or update the watch app. So a member on the GitHub copy installs a Play watch app that never shows the workout and whose buttons never log. Nothing on screen says why, and the owner has no written note of which key goes with which copy.
expected: On the GitHub copy, the phone either offers a watch app signed with the same key or says plainly that the watch needs the Play Store copy of the phone app. Which key signs which copy is written down where the owner can find it.
who: members who installed the phone app from GitHub and own a watch
fix_line: Tell GitHub-copy members the watch needs the Play copy, and write down which key signs which copy

title: Android's notification settings say workout reminders are set in Profile, but they are set in Settings, Reminders
what: In the phone's own notification settings, the 'Workout reminders' kind reads 'On the days and at the time you chose in Profile'. The days and time are now on the Reminders page inside Settings (reached from Profile's gear), so a member looking on Profile does not find them.
expected: The line names the real place, for example 'chosen in MettleUp, Settings, Reminders'.
who: members who look up reminders in the phone's settings
fix_line: Change the line to name Settings, Reminders

title: A MettleUp Plus subscriber is told they can cancel in Google Play but the app gives no way to get there
what: The Plus page says 'You can cancel a monthly or yearly plan there any time' (in Google Play). The app's Play payment part can only show prices, buy and check what is owned; there is no button that opens the member's Google Play subscriptions page. Plus buying is still switched off.
expected: Before payments go live, the Plus page has a 'Manage or cancel in Google Play' button that opens the member's Play subscriptions page for MettleUp.
who: Plus subscribers, once payments go live
how_often: every time one wants to cancel
fix_line: Add a button that opens Google Play's subscriptions page for MettleUp

title: Member help still describes the old first screen and the old erase, and says nothing about phone number sign-in
what: The help article for joining a gym tells a new member to tap Join my gym on the first screen. The first screen now shows only Continue with your phone number and a Try another way link, and no member article explains signing in with your phone number at all. The erase article says only that Erase all data deletes everything on this phone, though a signed-in member now chooses between this phone only and deleting the MettleUp account too. No article covers the screen shown when the app cannot start. The AI help answers only from these articles, so it gives the old steps.
expected: Member help explains the phone number sign-in and Try another way, the two erase choices, and what to do on the start-up error screen.
how_often: every time a member asks help about getting in or erasing
fix_line: Update the join and erase articles and add one for phone number sign-in and the start-up error screen

title: When the app cannot open a member's data, MettleUp is never told
what: If the app fails at start-up (its data will not open, update or read), the member sees the start-up error screen. That failure is only written to the phone's own log. The crash reports that reach MettleUp are sent only for a full crash or a screen that crashed, so a member locked out of their workouts this way is invisible to MettleUp unless they find someone to tell.
expected: A start-up failure sends one crash report (without workout data) so MettleUp sees it the same day, as it does for screen crashes.
who: members whose app will not open
how_often: rare, but each one is a locked-out member
fix_line: Send a crash report when the start-up error screen is shown

title: If MettleUp's WhatsApp check line stops working, every new member is stuck in a Start again loop and MettleUp is not told
what: The main way into the app is now Continue with your phone number, which depends on one MettleUp WhatsApp number receiving the member's message. If that line stops receiving (account blocked, token expired, number lost with the laptop or phone), the waiting screen only offers Open WhatsApp and Start again, and ends with 'The check ran out of time. Tap Start again.' It never suggests Try another way or the gym code, and nothing tells MettleUp that checks are failing.
expected: After a check runs out of time, the screen offers the gym code and Try another way, and repeated failed checks alert MettleUp.
who: every new member using phone sign-in
how_often: whenever the WhatsApp line is down
fix_line: Offer the other ways in after a timed-out check and alert MettleUp when checks keep timing out

title: When bringing in Hevy or Strong workouts fails, or undoing it fails, nothing records why and the member has nowhere to turn
what: If saving the imported workouts fails, the member reads 'The import failed. Nothing was changed. Please try again.' If Undo fails, they read 'Couldn't undo the import... Please try again.' In both cases the app throws the real error away without writing it anywhere, and the page offers no Help or 'tell us' button. A member whose file fails every time keeps trying again, and MettleUp cannot find out what went wrong even if the member does reach the help box in Settings.
expected: Both failures write the real error to the app's log, and after a second failure the page offers a way to send the problem (and the file name) to MettleUp.
fix_line: Log the real error on both failures and add a Get help button after a repeat failure

title: A gym name typed on Find my gym is lost without a word when it cannot be sent
what: When no gym is found, the member can type their gym's name and city and tap Tell my gym; the page says the MettleUp team may contact that gym. The name is sent once in the background. If the phone is offline or the server refuses it, the only trace is a line in the phone's own log: the member is not told, it is never sent again, and MettleUp never sees the lead.
expected: An unsent gym name is kept and sent again later, or the member is told it did not go.
fix_line: Keep the lead and retry it when the phone is back online

title: A member who paid for MettleUp Plus but is told 'this Google account has no Plus' is given no next step
what: On the MettleUp Plus page, I already paid checks Google Play. When nothing is found, the member reads only 'This Google account has no MettleUp Plus.' A member who did pay (on another Google account, or while Google Play was slow) is left with paid features locked and no word on what to do or who to ask. The page names no help path; the member must think of the round help button or Settings, Help and feedback on their own. The same is true when a payment stays 'waiting' and never opens. Plus is still switched off, so nobody meets this yet.
expected: When I already paid finds nothing, or a payment stays waiting, the message says to check the Google account used to pay and offers a Get help button that opens Help and feedback with the case filled in.
how_often: each time a paid member's purchase is not found
fix_line: Give the not-found and still-waiting messages a check-your-Google-account line and a Get help button

title: A gym link or code that finds no gym leaves the member with nobody to ask
what: When a join or check-in link, or a typed gym code, matches no gym, the page offers only Scan the poster and Type a gym code (or Close). If the gym has left MettleUp or its code changed, the poster and old WhatsApp links will always land here, and the member has no way to tell MettleUp or anyone else.
expected: The page also gives one way to reach someone, for example a Tell MettleUp button or the gym's own contact, so a dead poster gets noticed and fixed.
how_often: every time a link or code finds no gym
fix_line: Add one contact button to the gym not found page

title: A member's Tell my gym lead reaches MettleUp with only a gym name and city
what: When no gym lists the member's number, the app says the MettleUp team may contact your gym if the member types its name and city. Only those two words are sent: no phone number, area or member count. Someone at MettleUp must find the gym by hand each time, and nothing alerts them a lead came in unless HQ is open.
expected: The lead carries enough to act on (for example the gym's area or phone, typed by the member if they wish), and the owner's daily list shows new member leads.
fix_line: Ask for one more optional detail and list member leads in HQ's daily work

title: A member who pays the gym straight by UPI cannot tell the gym, and the fee keeps showing as owed
what: Pay your gym shows the gym's UPI QR and a Pay by UPI app button. When the member pays that way, the app only says the gym saves the receipt after they pay. There is no I have paid button and no place for the payment reference, and the app re-checks only payments made through a payment company. So the fee stays on screen as open with the pay buttons until someone at the desk spots the money in the bank and records it. The member may pay again or have to go to the desk to prove it.
expected: After a UPI payment the member can tap I have paid (optionally with the reference), the fee shows as waiting for the gym, and the desk is told to check it.
who: members who pay fees by UPI in the app, and the front desk
how_often: every direct UPI payment from the app
fix_line: Add an I have paid step that marks the fee as waiting and alerts the desk to check the bank

title: The member help says renewals are paid at the desk, while the app can show Pay your gym
what: The member help answer for membership says you pay at the desk after asking to renew. The app's membership page can show a Pay your gym box with a UPI QR and a UPI app button for fees the desk asked for. No member help answer explains paying the gym from the app.
expected: The member help says that fees can also be paid from the app when the gym allows it, and what happens after paying.
how_often: whenever a member reads help about renewing at a gym that takes app payments
fix_line: Add a member help answer for Pay your gym and change the renew line to match

title: Bringing routines in from a Hevy link depends on Hevy's web page, and nobody is told when Hevy changes it
what: The Hevy link import works by opening Hevy's public share page in a hidden browser and reading the routines off the screen. If Hevy changes how that page looks, every member who pastes a link is told 'We found no routines on that page. Check that it is a Hevy folder or routine link', which blames the member's link. No scheduled check opens a real Hevy link, and a failed read is only noted on the member's own phone, so the owner first hears of it from members, if at all.
expected: A small scheduled cloud check that reads one known Hevy share link and warns the owner when it finds no routines, and a member message that says the reader may be out of date rather than that the link is wrong.
who: members moving from Hevy, and the owner
how_often: every time Hevy changes its share page
fix_line: Add a daily cloud check on one real Hevy link that alerts the owner, and soften the member message

title: When bringing routines in from Hevy or Strong fails, nothing records why and the member has nowhere to turn
what: After a Hevy or Strong import, or from a Hevy share link, the routine steps end with Save. If saving fails the member reads 'Nothing was changed. Please try again.' (or that some new exercises were already added). The real error is thrown away without being written anywhere, and the screen offers no Help and feedback. Several earlier steps also swallow their errors: if the app cannot read which plan the member follows, it does not ask before switching their Up next to the new routines; if it cannot read the folders, the folder list is simply empty.
expected: The real error is kept (in the crash reports MettleUp reads), a repeat failure offers Help and feedback, and a failed read of the followed plan stops and says so rather than skipping the question.
who: members moving from Hevy or Strong
how_often: each time a routine save or a read fails
fix_line: Log the real error, add a Get help button after a repeat failure, and stop rather than skip the follow question when it cannot be read

title: Member help says nothing about swapping an exercise, demo data, easy weeks, strength level or trainer videos, and stops the Hevy import before the routine steps
what: The AI help answers only from the help articles. No member article mentions Swap an exercise, the Demo data strip and its Remove, Easy weeks, the strength level line, Watch your trainer videos, or set types beyond warm-up sets. The Hevy or Strong article ends at Merge or Replace, says nothing about the step-by-step routines that follow, the Up next switch or the 'From Hevy' folder, and says the file is not uploaded without saying a signed-in member's workouts are then copied to their MettleUp account. The help check only looks at screen files, so these parts can never trip it.
expected: Each of these parts has a short member article (or a line in the right one), and the help check also covers the shared parts the screens are built from.
how_often: whenever a member asks about these parts
fix_line: Add the missing member articles and extend the help check to the shared parts

title: Moving to a new phone silently leaves workout photos, the profile photo and own exercise pictures behind
what: The backup help says your workouts, routines and body weight are saved and come back on a new phone. The backup page warns only that progress photos stay on this phone. Photos on a workout, the profile photo and the photo or video on an exercise the member made are also never carried to a new phone, and nothing tells the member before they switch. After the move those pictures are simply missing, which reads as lost data and ends up as a support question.
expected: The backup help and the backup page say plainly that all photos and videos (workout photos, progress photos, profile photo, own exercise pictures) stay on the old phone, so a member saves them before switching.
who: members moving to a new phone
how_often: every phone change by a member with photos
fix_line: Add one line to the backup help and the backup page naming every kind of picture that stays on the old phone

title: Exercise demo clips are downloaded from the founder's personal GitHub account, fixed inside every installed copy
what: The demo films are not in the app. Each phone fetches them, the first time an exercise is opened, from a public release on one personal GitHub account under the old ForgeAI name. That address is written into every installed copy. If the account is renamed, locked or lost, the repository is made private, or the release is deleted, every phone that has not yet opened a clip shows no clip at all, with no message, and only a new app version can point elsewhere. A failed download is only written to the phone's own log, so nobody at MettleUp would notice. Nothing in this part of the app says who holds that account or how to get back in. Checked today: the address answers (redirect to the file).
expected: The clips sit on a MettleUp-owned address (or are bundled), the account holding them is written down with its way back in, and a clip that cannot be fetched is noticed by MettleUp.
how_often: only if that GitHub account or release is lost, but then on every phone
fix_line: Host the clips on a MettleUp-owned address and write down who holds that account

title: The outage alarm reaches only you, and nothing says so if the alarm itself stops
what: Every 10 minutes a cloud check opens an outage note that emails and names one person only, the owner. If the check itself breaks, it just fails quietly in the cloud. GitHub also pauses timed checks in a public code store after 60 days with no new change, and can start them late. No second person, phone alert or heartbeat exists.
expected: An outage reaches at least a second way (phone alert or a second person), and a missed or broken check is itself noticed.
fix_line: Send the outage note to a second channel and add a daily 'the watch is alive' check from outside GitHub.

title: Outage notes, including a failed backup or a refused logs key, are posted where anyone can read them
what: The outage notes are opened in the public code store. Crash notes were moved to a private store on 10 Nov for this reason, but outage notes were not. They say when the gym server, sign-in, the nightly backup or the record of direct looks at gym data is failing, and why.
expected: Outage and key notes live in the private store, like crash notes.
fix_line: Open the outage and key-reminder notes in the private crashes store instead.

title: One personal code-store account holds every release, store upload, WhatsApp and alarm path, with no written way back if it is lost
what: The phone app signing key, the Apple key, the Play upload access, the WhatsApp token and PIN, the Cloudflare key and the outage alarm all sit in one personal GitHub account. Losing the laptop breaks nothing, since all of it is in the cloud. Losing that account, or the phone that confirms its sign-in, stops releases, store updates, new WhatsApp tokens and alarms at once. The signing note covers a lost signing key only. Saved secrets can never be read back from GitHub.
expected: A written, tested way back into the GitHub account (recovery codes kept offline, a second admin), and a list of every key with where its spare copy lives.
fix_line: Write a one-page way back in for the GitHub account and every key, keep recovery codes offline, and add a second admin.

title: Deleting a gym also deletes its proof that it accepted the terms and the data agreement
what: The record of who accepted the terms, when and which version is described as kept for ever, but when MettleUp deletes a gym at its request, that record is deleted with it. HQ's own records survive the delete; this one does not. In a business with several branches, the acceptance is stored on one branch only, so deleting that branch also leaves the other branches with no acceptance, and their owners are asked again.
expected: The acceptance record outlives the gym, like HQ's own legal records, so MettleUp can still show what the gym agreed to after it leaves; and a branch delete never removes the business's acceptance.
who: MettleUp (legal record), owners of branch businesses
fix_line: Keep the acceptance rows when a gym is deleted, as HQ's own records are kept, and count a deleted branch's acceptance for the rest of the business

title: Records taken back by Undo this import stay on our server in full, for ever
what: When an owner undoes a wrong data import, the members, plans, memberships and receipts it made are only marked as removed: every name, mobile and amount stays on the server. Taken-back check-ins and expenses are the same. The nightly clean-up never clears them, so a wrong file (even another gym's list) stays stored with no end date.
expected: Records taken back are emptied of personal details after a short time, and the nightly clean-up clears them.
who: members of gyms that undo an import
fix_line: Have the nightly clean-up empty the details of records removed more than a set time ago

title: If the nightly clean-up stops, nobody is told, and the log-deletion promises quietly break
what: The nightly clean-up deletes the sign-in log after 7 days and creator addresses after a year, as the privacy notice says. If it fails, the only trace is a hidden server log line. The HQ system page shows no 'last clean-up' time, so a broken key or job could leave logs kept far longer than promised without anyone noticing.
expected: HQ shows when the clean-up last ran, and warns you when it has not run for a day or more.
who: you (MettleUp), and every gym's staff whose sign-in log is kept
fix_line: Show the last clean-up time in HQ and warn when it is more than a day old

title: After every branch of a business is deleted, the business's name stays on our server
what: A business with branches has its own row holding the business name. Deleting a gym removes the branch but leaves that row; when the last branch goes, the name stays with nothing pointing to it, and the delete's own check that nothing was left behind does not look at it.
expected: Deleting the last branch also deletes the business row.
who: owners of branch businesses that leave
how_often: every full offboarding of a branch business
fix_line: Remove the business row when its last branch is deleted

title: A gym that pays MettleUp during its free trial loses its unused trial days, and a plan change carries the old paid days onto the new plan
what: When HQ confirms a payment, the paid month or year is counted from today or the current paid-until date; the free trial's end is ignored. A gym paying on day 3 of its trial loses the rest of the trial, while HQ's own confirm line says the paid time starts when the trial ends. A change of plan also moves all the days already paid onto the new plan: a gym with months of Starter left that pays one Pro month gets Pro for all of them, and a Pro gym that pays one Starter month drops to Starter at once for the rest of its paid Pro time. The later billing step that fixes both is not live.
expected: Paid time starts when the trial ends, and a plan change is priced or timed so neither MettleUp nor the gym loses paid days, with HQ's line showing the same date the server sets.
how_often: every gym that pays during its trial or switches plan
fix_line: Count paid time from the trial's end and handle a plan switch as its own case, as the next billing step already does, then make that step live

title: A gym that has paid but is still waiting for MettleUp to confirm is cut down to basic and then read-only like a gym that never paid
what: The gym's state comes only from its paid-until and trial dates. A payment the owner has sent and MettleUp has not yet confirmed counts for nothing, so once the plan limits are switched on, a gym whose confirmation waits more than 7 days on the one person who confirms loses new members and Pro extras, and after 37 days goes read-only.
expected: A gym with a payment waiting to be checked keeps everything on until MettleUp confirms or rejects it, and a payment left waiting raises an alarm that does not depend on one person looking.
how_often: whenever MettleUp is slow to confirm a payment, once plan limits are on
fix_line: Treat a waiting payment as paid for the state check, and remind MettleUp when one waits over a day

title: The nightly backup never copies member photos, workout report files or gym logos
what: The nightly copy holds every table but none of the stored files. If the database project were lost, every member photo taken at the desk and every workout report file would be gone for good; the restore guide says so, but nothing else copies them.
expected: Every file a gym or member relies on has a second copy somewhere else, or the gym is told plainly that photos are not backed up.
how_often: only if the database project is lost
fix_line: Add a weekly copy of stored files to a second store, or tell owners that photos have no backup

title: Every backup sits in the same Cloudflare account that runs the service, for 7 days, and only one person can open it
what: The nightly copy is kept only in Cloudflare, in the same account as the live service, and each copy is deleted after 7 days. Getting it back needs someone signed in to that account on a computer. If that one account is lost, locked or hacked, the live service and every backup go together, and a fault noticed after a week has no copy left from before it.
expected: At least one copy lives outside the main accounts, a second trusted person can reach it, and the way back in is written down.
how_often: only if that account is lost or a fault is found late
fix_line: Keep a weekly copy in a second, separate place and write down who else can reach it

title: If the Firebase key stops working, every phone pop-up is lost quietly and MettleUp is never told
what: Each pop-up job is marked as sent before it goes out. When the Firebase key is missing, wrong or refused, the sender only writes a line to the server log and the pop-ups of that batch are gone. Nothing in HQ shows that pop-ups have stopped; members only see the message later when the app checks by itself.
expected: A broken or refused pop-up key shows as a red line in HQ and sends MettleUp an alert the same day.
how_often: whenever the Firebase key breaks or expires
fix_line: Record each pop-up run's result where HQ's health check can see it and alert when runs fail

title: Help on sending messages never says there is a limit of 10 a day, no pop-up from the 3rd, and one offer a day
what: The server refuses an 11th message in a day, sends the 3rd and later messages with no phone pop-up, and allows one offer or event a day and three a week. The help article on sending messages and offers mentions none of these, so an owner who hits a limit has no help answer.
expected: The help article states the daily and weekly limits and the quiet rule in plain words.
how_often: every owner who sends many messages
fix_line: Add two lines on the limits to the message help article

title: A member's question to one trainer who never answers quietly closes after 14 days, and the owner never sees it
what: A question picked for one trainer is seen only by that trainer while they are still ticked. If that trainer ignores it, it stops being open after 14 days and the owner is never shown it, so the member's question reaches nobody.
expected: A question nobody has answered after a day or two is also shown to the owner, or the member is told and can ask someone else.
how_often: whenever a picked trainer does not reply
fix_line: Show questions unanswered for two days to the owner too

title: A gym that stops paying and never asks to leave keeps all its members' details on our server for ever
what: After the grace and basic days a gym goes read-only and stays that way with no end. Its members' names, phone numbers and payments are kept with no date for removal and no reminder to the owner or to MettleUp.
expected: A gym that stays read-only for a set time is warned, then removed or archived on a date the terms state.
how_often: every gym that leaves without asking
fix_line: Set and publish a time after which a read-only gym is warned and then deleted

title: Reports from 'Report this page' are saved where nobody can read them, and HQ has no button to take a page down
what: A visitor who reports a gym web page as a scam, offensive or closed gets a thank-you, and the report is stored. But nothing in HQ, the HQ server or any other part of the product ever reads those reports, and HQ has no way to take a page down: it can only show whether a page was taken down. A scam or offensive page stays up and nobody at MettleUp ever hears of the report.
expected: Each report shows in HQ (and in Needs you), and HQ can take the page down or put it back from there.
who: visitors who report a page, the owner, gyms
fix_line: Add a reports list and a take-down button to HQ, and count new reports in Needs you

title: A member's question sent to one trainer rings only that trainer, so it can wait unseen if the trainer is away or removed
what: When a member sends a question to a named trainer, only that trainer gets the bell and browser alert; the owner gets no alert. If the trainer is on leave, never signs in, or is removed from staff, the question rings nobody. The owner can only find it by opening Member messages and looking.
expected: A question to a trainer still reaches someone: the owner is alerted when the trainer is removed, or when it has had no reply for a day or two.
how_often: whenever the chosen trainer is away or removed
fix_line: Alert the owner when a trainer question has no reply after a set time or its trainer is gone

title: A plan payment whose confirmation from the payment company is lost is checked again for only 48 hours, then forgotten
what: If the payment company's message saying a gym paid never arrives, the nightly check asks the company only about pay links opened in the last 48 hours. A pay link lasts 24 hours, so a payment gets one or two nightly checks. If those runs fail or are missed, the money is taken, the gym gets no plan, and the payment never appears in Payments to check, because it is still marked open.
expected: Pay links still open after the check window show up in Payments to check (or Needs you) so no paid link is ever silently dropped.
who: gym owners who pay online, the owner
how_often: rare: only when the payment message and the nightly checks both fail
fix_line: List pay links still open after 48 hours in Payments to check

title: One secret signs phone checks, AI credit spending, join payments and web page chats, with no way to change it without breaking all of them
what: The same single secret, kept in one database row and copied into the web server, proves phone numbers, lets AI answers spend a gym's credits, ties join payments to the right gym and signs web page chats. The database accepts only one value. Changing it (for example if the laptop or a copy leaks) breaks all four at once until both places are changed, and no change file says how to change it safely.
expected: Each job has its own secret, or the database accepts an old and a new secret during a change-over, and the written steps for changing it are kept where someone other than Claude can find them.
how_often: whenever the secret must be changed
fix_line: Let the database accept a second secret during a change and write down the change steps

title: Plan receipts can go out with no business name, and nothing warns that the setting is empty
what: The legal business name on every MettleUp plan receipt comes only from a setting that starts empty and must be filled by hand on the live server. If it was never filled, receipts are still numbered and issued with no legal name, and neither HQ nor the receipt says anything is missing.
expected: HQ warns while the receipt business name is empty, before any online payment is taken.
who: gym owners who pay MettleUp, the owner
how_often: every receipt while the setting is empty
fix_line: Show a warning in HQ while the receipt business name is not set

title: A gym that pays for Starter while on Pro never moves to Starter while online buying is off
what: When HQ confirms a Starter payment for a gym still on Pro or in its trial, the gym is told Starter starts on the day Pro ends. Only the nightly billing job makes that switch, and that job runs only when online buying is switched on, which it is not. So the gym stays on Pro for ever at the Starter price, and its admin app keeps showing a Starter start date that has passed.
expected: The planned switch to Starter happens on its day whether or not online buying is on.
who: gym owners who choose Starter, and MettleUp
how_often: every Starter payment confirmed for a gym on Pro or trial
fix_line: Run the planned plan switch every night on its own, not only when online buying is on.

title: Leads, help questions and replies, AI limits and the online-payment settings have no backup and no restore steps
what: The nightly backup copies only the gym server. The second, smaller database holds the website leads, every feedback and help message with your replies, each gym's AI limits, the online-payment records and switches, and HQ's messages to gyms. It is in no copy, and the written restore steps never mention it. If that database or the Cloudflare account were lost, all of it would be gone.
expected: Every database MettleUp keeps is in the nightly copy, or the written restore steps say how to bring it back.
how_often: only if that database or account is lost
fix_line: Add the second database to the nightly copy, or write down how to bring it back from Cloudflare's own history.

title: HQ opens for one Google account only, and there is no written way back in if it is lost
what: HQ lets in only the one Google address kept as a secret on Cloudflare. If that Google account, or the laptop holding its passkey, is lost, the only way back is to change that secret and send HQ out again from a computer signed in to Cloudflare. HQ is never sent out by GitHub, only by hand, and nothing in HQ's setup names a second person or the steps to follow.
expected: A written, tested way back into HQ and Cloudflare that does not depend on one laptop or one Google account.
how_often: only if the Google account or laptop is lost
fix_line: Write the way back in (who, which accounts, which steps) and keep a second trusted sign-in or recovery set.

title: If the nightly clean-up or billing job fails, nobody is told
what: The nightly backup and the direct-read record each have a status the watch reads and turns into an alert. The nightly clean-up (old feedback, old leads, old AI requests, test gyms) and the nightly billing job only write a hidden log line when they fail. The deletions the privacy notice promises could stop for weeks without you knowing.
expected: A failed nightly clean-up or billing run shows up the same way a failed backup does.
who: you, and members whose old data should be deleted
fix_line: Save the result of each nightly job and let the watch alert on a failure, like the backup.

title: The key behind staff browser alerts is kept in one place only, and HQ says it must never change
what: The key that sends gym alerts to staff browsers is made once, never shown, and stored only as a Cloudflare secret. The setup note says never change it, because every browser's alerts are tied to it. There is no copy, so if HQ is ever made again or moved to another account, every staff browser stops getting alerts until each one signs up again.
expected: A safe copy of the key is kept with the other recovery items, or the admin app signs browsers up again by itself when the key changes.
how_often: only if HQ is re-made or moved
fix_line: Keep a sealed copy of the alert key, or make browsers sign up again when the key changes.

title: Deleting a gym leaves its payment company keys and payment records on our web server
what: When HQ deletes a gym, only the gym server and its files are cleared. Our separate small web database still keeps that gym's sealed payment company keys or sign-in tokens, every payment link record with member ids and amounts, and its AI limits. The keys are only wiped after a desk presses Disconnect, which a leaving gym may never do. Nothing removes the payment records at all.
expected: Deleting a gym also clears everything about it in the small web database, within the 30 days the data agreement promises, and the delete step says so.
fix_line: Make the gym delete also clear that gym's rows in the small web database, and log it

title: Nobody can tell from the code which changes to the small web database are live
what: The first line of several change files for the small web database still says not applied, although the features that need them are live: Verify with WhatsApp, AI help answers and the AI usage counts. Some files were applied one by one, so the database's own list of applied changes is not complete either. Running the standard apply step those files suggest could try to add a column that already exists and stop half way.
expected: Each change file says truthfully whether it is live, and one written list matches the database, so the next change is applied safely.
fix_line: Check the live list once, fix each file's first line, and write the apply rule in one place

title: The nightly clean-up, the 10-minute payment check and the help AI's monthly limit fail with only a hidden log line
what: If the nightly clean-up of crash reports, sign-in codes and friend form counts fails, or the payment check that marks links paid fails, the server only writes a log line nobody is sent. When the help box reaches its monthly AI spending limit, every person quietly gets no answer for the rest of the month, again with only a log line.
expected: Each of these shows up in HQ or the outage alarm: last good run time, failures, and when the monthly AI limit is reached.
how_often: whenever a job or key fails
fix_line: Write each job's last good run where HQ already reads, and warn on a miss

title: The small web database is left out of the written backup plan
what: The backup note covers only the gym server. The small web database holds demo requests, every help question and team reply, payment links and each gym's sealed payment keys. Nothing written says how it is backed up or how to bring it back after a bad change or a lost account. Cloudflare keeps its own restore points, but no note says so, for how long, or how to use them.
expected: The backup note lists this database too, with how long restore points last and the steps to restore it.
fix_line: Add the small web database to the backup note, with its restore steps

title: No written list of the about 17 secret keys this server needs, what each breaks, or how to replace one
what: This server uses about 17 secret keys: the help AI key, three other AI keys, the WhatsApp token and app secret, the sign-in code secret, the payment master key, six payment partner keys and a salt. Each is named only inside the code. The sign-in code secret must match a copy kept in the gym server, and nothing says how to change both together. No note says who holds each key, when it runs out, or what stops if it goes.
expected: One short note lists every key: what uses it, what breaks without it, when it expires and how to replace it safely.
how_often: when a key is lost or expires
fix_line: Write one key list for this server with replace steps

title: When the watch app fails or crashes on a member's wrist, MettleUp never hears of it
what: The watch app has no crash report of its own and no internet access. Every failure it catches (a set not sent to the phone, the phone refusing a set, a phone message it could not read, a rest card button that did nothing) is written only to the watch's own log, which nobody at MettleUp can see. The only thing that ever reaches MettleUp is the screen diary, and only when the member ticks 'Add my watch's screen log' in the phone's Help and feedback, and that diary holds screen and battery events, not these failures. So a watch model where logging from the watch keeps failing, or where the app crashes, stays invisible unless a member writes in.
expected: The watch keeps a short list of its own failures and crashes and passes it to the phone, which sends it with the phone's crash reports; the owner sees watch problems in the same place as phone problems.
who: members with a watch, and the owner
fix_line: Have the watch hand its failures and crashes to the phone so they go out with the phone's crash reports

title: The gym-owner site offers to come to any gym and set it up in person, with no area or limit
what: The gym-owner site says twice that if a gym leaves its number, MettleUp calls and sets it up with them at their gym. The About page also promises free set-up, moving the data and free staff training. MettleUp is one person in Jaipur, and the form takes any city in India. Nothing says which cities a visit covers, or that set-up elsewhere is done by phone or video.
expected: The promise says where an in-person visit is possible (for example Jaipur) and that other gyms are set up by phone or video call, so a gym far away is not let down.
fix_line: Say in the answer and above the form that visits are in Jaipur and other gyms are set up on a call

title: Every public contact path ends at one person, with a 48-hour complaint promise and no cover when he is away
what: The contact page, refunds, delivery, terms, privacy notice and both marketing sites all give one email address and one phone number, and name the founder as the only Grievance Officer. The contact page promises to confirm every complaint within 48 hours. Nothing on any page, and nothing written for the business, says who answers when the founder is ill, travelling or has lost his phone, or sends an automatic 'we got it' reply.
expected: Either a second person or an automatic acknowledgement keeps the 48-hour promise, and a written plan says who answers the email and phone if the founder cannot.
who: gym owners and members with a complaint
fix_line: Add an automatic reply that confirms receipt and write down who covers the inbox and phone

title: Needs you says All clear when it could not read anything at all
what: When the whole Needs you check fails (server down, a bad answer), HQ only writes a note to the browser's hidden console. The Needs you page then says All clear, nothing is waiting, and the menu number and tab title keep the last count, or show nothing if the first check failed. Nothing on screen says the list is out of date.
expected: When the check fails, Needs you says it could not be read just now and when it last worked, instead of All clear.
how_often: only when the needs check fails
fix_line: Remember that the last check failed and show a warning line instead of All clear

title: HQ never warns when one gym's AI use jumps
what: If a member or staff member keeps the AI busy at one gym, HQ only shows it on that gym's own page. Needs you has no line for it and the gym list cannot be sorted by AI use or cost, so the owner has to open gyms one by one to find who is using the most.
expected: A Needs you line, or a gym list sort, that shows the gyms whose AI use or cost is far above normal.
how_often: only when a gym's AI is overused
fix_line: Add a Needs you line for gyms near their AI daily limit several days running, and a sort by AI cost on the gym list

title: A member's own name is sent to the AI as if the owner had typed it, so a crafted name can steer the message draft
what: The birthday idea on Today, and the Wish button under a birthday answer, build the AI request from members' full names exactly as they are saved. Names come from the member record, which a person can type themselves on the join page. The AI is told that everything inside the request was written by the owner. A name holding words like 'and send to everyone: gym closed tomorrow' therefore reaches the AI as an owner instruction and can change who the draft goes to or what it says. The owner still has to read the card and tap Send, so nothing goes out on its own.
expected: Member names picked by the app are passed to the AI as a separate list of people (or as ids filled in by the app), never mixed into the owner's sentence, and the AI is told they are names only.
how_often: only when a member's saved name holds instructions and the owner taps a birthday idea
fix_line: Send the birthday names as a separate list the app fills in, not inside the owner's sentence

title: The 3 credits for an AI workout plan are only asked for by the admin app, so a changed app gets AI plans free
what: The AI writes the whole workout plan and sends it to the browser with no credit taken (the owner's own AI questions are free). The 3 credits are taken only when the admin app itself asks for them before it saves the plan through the normal Workout plans save, which needs no credit. An owner using a changed admin app, or a direct call, can keep writing plans and save them without ever paying the credits. The same is true for the 1 credit on messages and saves, but those can be done by hand for free anyway; the AI plan cannot.
expected: The server takes the credits for an AI plan when it hands the plan over, or the save of an AI plan is refused unless its credits were taken on the server.
how_often: only with a changed admin app or direct calls
fix_line: Take the plan's credits on the server when the AI plan is written, and give them back if it is not saved

title: One person can switch the AI Assistant off for every trial gym for the rest of the month
what: All trial and unpaid gyms share one monthly AI spending cap. Each gym is limited to 20 questions a day, but anyone can create a free trial gym. A person who makes several trial gyms and asks the daily maximum in each fills the shared cap, and then every trial gym is told the AI Assistant is resting till next month.
expected: Each trial gym has its own small monthly cap, so no single gym or person can use up the AI for the other trial gyms.
how_often: only when someone sets out to do it
fix_line: Give each trial gym its own monthly AI cap, inside the shared one

title: Anyone can get another 3-month free trial by making a new gym with the same mobile
what: Create my gym gives every new gym 3 free months unless a WhatsApp-checked number is sent. The number check is behind a switch that is off, and the panel falls back to making the gym without it. So an owner whose trial ended can make a fresh gym with the same number, import his members again, and use Pro free for another 3 months, as often as he likes (5 gyms an hour from one internet address).
expected: One free trial per mobile number: a number that already owns a gym or already had a trial gets no new free months, whether or not the WhatsApp check is on.
how_often: every time an owner makes another gym
fix_line: Give the free months only to a number that has never owned a gym or had a trial, even without the WhatsApp check

title: The front desk can add or remove check-ins for any day with no name kept, and check-ins now win challenge prizes
what: The gym server takes any check-in the panel sends from a front-desk login: any member, any day (past or future), and it lets the desk delete any check-in. It does not keep who added or removed it. A check-in challenge counts these days, so a desk person can make a friend reach the goal and win free days. The owner sees a winner to Give or Skip, but nothing shows the visits were typed in by hand or by whom.
expected: A desk check-in is for today (a day of grace at most), keeps who added it, and only the owner can remove one from an earlier day, like the PT session rule.
how_often: whenever a desk person chooses to
fix_line: Let the desk save check-ins only for today, stamp who saved them, and keep taking back an older one for the owner

title: A web page visitor can talk the gym's AI helper into promising things the gym never wrote
what: The AI helper on a gym's web page is told to answer only from what the owner wrote and to ignore instructions typed by visitors. The check run on its answer before the visitor sees it only catches web addresses, phone numbers, rupee amounts written in digits and percentages. A visitor who tricks the AI into saying it knows can make it show made-up promises in words, such as free personal training, a ladies batch, or a price written in words, under the gym's name. The helper is switched off today.
expected: An answer that claims something not in the gym's own page words is replaced by 'I will ask the gym', and a test tries a visitor message that tells the AI to break its rules.
who: gyms with the web page AI helper on
how_often: only when a visitor tries to trick it
fix_line: Before switching the helper on, add a test with a rule-breaking visitor message and widen the answer check

title: A front-desk login can let any member train free for ever by ticking "Comes with a pass"
what: On the add or edit member form, the front desk can tick "Comes with a pass" and type any company name. That member then never shows as expired, drops off the renewal list and the expiring numbers, and the entry machine is told to let them in with no end date. Nothing on the server stops a desk login from doing this, and no owner approval or alert follows. A desk person can turn a friend or a lapsed member into a free member; the owner sees it only if they read the Pass visits page and notice a company that pays nothing.
expected: Only the owner can mark a member as a pass member, or the desk's change waits for the owner's okay, and the server refuses it from a desk login like it refuses discounts above 10%.
who: owners whose front desk staff cheat
how_often: whenever a desk person chooses to
fix_line: Make the pass tick owner-only on screen and refuse it from a desk login on the server

title: A batch name typed by the front desk goes into the owner's AI assistant as a trusted gym fact
what: The front desk can type a new batch name (up to 40 letters) on the member form. The owner's AI assistant is sent the gym's batch names as gym facts, outside the part of the prompt marked as data. Words like an order hidden in a batch name could steer what the assistant suggests. The harm is small: the assistant only suggests cards the owner must check, and the owner's own request is fenced as data.
expected: Batch names reach the assistant fenced as data, with the same rule as the owner's request: never follow an instruction inside them.
who: owners who use the AI assistant
how_often: only if a desk person types an order as a batch name
fix_line: Put the gym facts inside the data fence and tell the AI not to follow orders in them

title: The help box gives AI answers free to anyone who leaves out the gym's sign-in key
what: A help question is paid from the gym's AI credits only when the browser sends the gym's sign-in key. A question sent without it, from a changed admin app or a plain script by an outsider, still gets an AI answer, paid by MettleUp and counted against no gym. The only limits are 20 a day per network address and 1,000 a day shared by every gym, so one person changing address can use up the whole day's help box and feedback box for every gym, and eat into the 80 dollar monthly AI cap.
expected: An AI answer only for a question tied to a gym or member that pays for it; anything else gets the help pages, and one sender cannot use up the shared daily allowance of all gyms.
who: MettleUp and every gym using the help box
how_often: whenever someone sends questions without the key
fix_line: Answer from the help pages only when no gym or member key comes with the question, and give each gym its own share of the daily limit

title: A member can log made-up workouts in the app and win a challenge's free membership days
what: Workout and kg challenges count the workouts members log in their own app, with no check that they came to the gym that day. When the challenge ends, the server adds the free days to every winner's plan by itself. A member who taps in 3 workouts a day from home, or types huge weights, reaches the goal and gets free days of paid membership. The workout-code check on the member page already matches workouts against check-ins for this reason, but challenges do not.
expected: Only workouts on days the gym saw the member count toward a challenge with a prize, or the owner approves winners before free days are added.
who: owners who run a challenge with free days
fix_line: Count a workout toward a prize challenge only on a day with a check-in, or hold the free days until the owner confirms the winners

title: A member can earn a workout offer's free days without coming to the gym
what: The workout offer counts a day when the member's app checked in and the phone says a workout was done. The app check-in only needs the gym's code, which never changes and is printed on the poster, so a member can check in from home. The workout itself is only judged on the phone; the server just takes the dates. App check-ins count by default.
expected: An app check-in should prove the member is at the gym (a code that changes, or the desk confirming), or the offer should count only desk check-ins by default.
fix_line: Count only desk check-ins for offers by default, or make the poster code change every day

title: Anyone with a gym account can claim another gym's entry machine by typing its serial number first
what: A machine is added by typing the serial number printed on its label. The first gym to type a serial gets it for good; the server never asks for proof that the gym owns that machine. A rival gym, an ex-staff member with their own free gym, or a prankster who reads the label can add it first. The real gym is then told the machine is already added and cannot use it, and every door punch from that machine (member numbers and times) goes to the other gym. The 'already added' answer also tells anyone whether a serial is in use. Not live today: the entry machine service is written but not switched on.
