expected: A stated keep time for receipt history and ended sign-ins, cleared by the nightly clean-up, or a size cap per gym.
fix_line: Add receipt history and ended sign-ins to the nightly clean-up with a keep time

title: Seven full uncompressed backup copies will fill the free Cloudflare store, and the backup then stops
what: Every night the whole database, every row of every table, is copied as plain text and kept for 7 days in the Cloudflare key store, with no squeezing. Member photos are written as long text that is about twice their real size. The free Cloudflare plan gives 1 GB in that store for the whole account. Once one copy is about 140 MB, seven copies fill it, new copies cannot be saved, and the nightly backup fails. Nothing warns before that point. The outage watch only notices after a night's backup is already missing. Each copy also leaves the gym server as download traffic every night, and that traffic is not watched either.
expected: Backup copies are made smaller before they are stored, their total size is checked against the store's limit, and MettleUp is warned well before the store is full.
who: MettleUp, and every gym if a restore is ever needed
how_often: every night, getting worse as data grows
fix_line: Squeeze each copy before storing it, keep fewer full copies, and warn when the store passes a set share of its limit

title: Every door-machine punch is kept on the gym server for ever
what: When the entry machines are switched on, every punch at the gym door is saved as one row. Other lists in this part (leaderboard days, gym mate workouts, busy times, push jobs) delete old rows after 30 to 90 days, but door punches are never deleted. A gym with 300 visits a day adds about 15 MB a year. Thirty such gyms add about 450 MB a year, close to the free 500 MB that all gyms share. When the database is full, saving members and payments stops for every gym.
expected: Old door punches are deleted after a set time (for example 90 days), since each visit is already kept in the gym's own records.
who: every gym once entry machines are on
how_often: grows every day a machine is used
fix_line: Delete door punches older than a set number of days, the way other lists already do

title: On a busy day gym-message pop-ups over 6 hours late are quietly dropped, and nobody is told
what: The free Cloudflare plan lets the sender make about 45 outside calls a minute, so about 2,700 phone pop-ups go out an hour across all gyms. A message to everyone at a large gym can be sent to up to 5,000 people. When many gyms send in the same morning, the line of pop-ups grows. Any message still waiting after 6 hours is marked late and skipped. Nothing reads those late marks, so MettleUp never learns that members missed pop-ups. Members still see the message inside the app later.
expected: MettleUp is warned when pop-ups start to back up or are skipped as late, before the 6-hour cut-off is reached.
who: gym members and owners on busy days
how_often: only when many gyms send at once
fix_line: Count pop-ups waiting and skipped as late, and warn MettleUp when either passes a set number

title: AI questions from the owner and staff cost the gym nothing and have no total limit per gym
what: AI questions asked by the gym owner or any staff person take no credit and are paid by MettleUp. The only limit is 60 a day for each person. There is no total for the whole gym, and no check that the gym is paying: a trial gym or a free demo gym gets the same. A gym with many staff logins, or many demo gyms, can run up MettleUp's AI bill or use up the shared daily ceiling for everyone, and nothing warns MettleUp as this spend grows.
expected: A daily total of free owner and staff questions for each gym (lower for trial and demo gyms), and a warning to MettleUp when free AI spend passes a set amount in a day or a month.
how_often: every day, growing with staff and gyms
fix_line: Add a whole-gym daily total for free owner and staff AI questions and warn MettleUp past a set spend

title: Gym web page photos have a daily upload limit but no total per gym, and removed photos are never deleted
what: An owner may upload up to 60 web page photos of up to 1 MB each every day. There is no limit on how many a gym keeps in total, and files of photos taken off the page stay in storage for ever because the clean-up job was left for later. A single gym, or a stream of free demo gyms, can add about 60 MB a day each to the 1 GB of free picture storage that all gyms share. When that store is full, every gym's photo uploads stop, and nothing warns MettleUp first.
expected: A total number of page photos per gym, a job that deletes files no page uses, and a storage-size warning to MettleUp well before the free limit.
how_often: once the web page part is turned on
fix_line: Cap page photos per gym, delete unused photo files, and warn on storage size

title: The nightly backup will stop fitting in its free store long before the gym database is full
what: Each night a full copy of the gym database is saved, and the last 7 copies are kept, in a free store that holds 1 GB in total. So once one copy passes about 140 MB, the night's save is refused and no new backup is made. The database itself may grow to 500 MB, so this happens at less than a third of the limit HQ watches. Nothing compares the copy size with the store's space, and the public backup check hides the size, so the first sign is a failed backup.
expected: HQ shows how full the backup store is and warns on Needs you well before 7 copies stop fitting, with a plan (fewer copies, packing, or a paid store) ready.
how_often: once the data grows to about 140 MB, then every night
fix_line: Track the copy size against the store space and warn at 60% and 80%; pack the copy or keep fewer copies before it is full

title: Anyone can make the pop-up sender run over and over, each time calling the gym server
what: The address that says "something was just sent, send pop-ups now" needs no sign-in. Its "once every 3 seconds" brake is kept only inside one running copy of the service, and the service runs many copies, so a script can start many runs a second. Each run asks the gym server for waiting pop-ups even when none wait, using free requests and server traffic that all gyms share.
expected: The early send is limited for the whole service (or needs a sign-in), so outsiders cannot burn the shared free allowances.
fix_line: Keep the 3-second brake in a shared place, or check that the caller is one of our own services

title: The English helper's monthly cost leaves out tries that Google still charges for
what: When a rewrite times out or comes back empty, the helper tries the next model, up to the most expensive one. Only the last, good answer is added to "this month's cost". The tries before it may still be billed by Google, and there is no monthly ceiling, so the cost shown can be lower than the bill.
expected: Every billed try is counted in the month's cost, and the helper stops or warns past a monthly amount.
how_often: when Google is slow or a model is retired
fix_line: Add the token use of every answered try to the month, and add a monthly cap with a Needs you line

title: Every admin app page load uses the shared free daily request limit, and at the limit the admin app may not open at all
what: Our web server is set to run its own code first for every address except the hashed picture and script files. So each opening or refresh of the admin app, its icons, its offline helper file and every gym invite, check-in and join page counts against the free plan's 100,000 requests a day for all of MettleUp. Plain files served without our code would not count. When the limit is passed, Cloudflare shows its own error page: the apps' fallback to the gym server's direct address only helps an app that is already open, so a desk that opens the admin app fresh (with no saved copy in the browser), and every person opening a gym link, sees an error until 05:30 India time.
expected: Only the addresses that need our code (the gym server pass-through, the /api calls and the gym link pages) run it; the admin app's own files are served as plain files that do not use up the daily limit, and what a desk sees at the limit is written down.
who: every gym desk and anyone opening a gym link
how_often: every day the shared limit is passed; every page load adds to the count
fix_line: Run our code only for the addresses that need it and let the admin app's plain files be served without it

title: The gym web page chat's AI cost is written only to a passing log line
what: Each AI answer in the chat on a gym's web page works out its cost but only prints it in a log line, which Cloudflare keeps for a few days. It is not added to any usage count, so HQ cannot see what the page chat costs per gym or per month, and it has no money ceiling of its own; only the gym's AI credits and the 30-a-day limit hold it back. It uses the same paid AI key as the owner's AI Assistant. Not live today: the chat is switched off.
expected: Page chat calls and tokens are counted like the help answers and the AI Assistant, shown on HQ's AI cost, and covered by a monthly ceiling with a warning before it.
how_often: every page chat answer once the chat is switched on
fix_line: Count page chat tokens in the small web database and add them to HQ's AI cost and a monthly ceiling

title: The AI helper on gym web pages spends MettleUp's AI money without counting it anywhere
what: Each answer from the AI helper on a gym's web page is a paid AI call. Its cost is only written to a passing log line. It is not added to the AI usage tally that the other AI features use, so no month total, no all-gyms ceiling and no warning can include it. The gym's own credits limit each gym, but MettleUp cannot see what the helper costs in total.
expected: Every web-page helper answer is added to the same AI usage tally as the other AI features, so HQ shows its cost and warns before a monthly amount is passed.
how_often: every AI helper answer, once the helper is switched on
fix_line: Record each helper answer and its cost in the shared AI usage tally and include it in HQ's month total

title: The per-visitor limits on gym web page forms switch off quietly when the small web store fails or is full
what: Ask the gym, Report this page and the AI helper count sends per network address in Cloudflare's small free web store. When that store is missing, broken or over its free daily write limit, the count is skipped and every send goes through. Only a log line says so; nobody at MettleUp is warned, and the only brake left is each gym's own daily limit, which one visitor can then use up.
expected: MettleUp is warned before the web store nears its free daily limit, and is told at once when the per-visitor count stops working.
how_often: whenever the web store is down or over its free limit
fix_line: Raise an HQ alert when the per-visitor count cannot be used, and watch the web store's daily writes

title: In the light look, the orange words and buttons are too faint to read easily
what: When the computer or phone is set to light mode, every ordinary orange button has orange words on a pale orange patch, about 3.5 to 1 against the background. Orange links and the solid orange buttons with white words reach about 4.3 to 1. Plain text needs at least 4.5 to 1. In bright light or with weaker eyesight the button words blur.
expected: Every word on every button and link reads at 4.5 to 1 or better in both the dark and the light look.
fix_line: Use a darker orange for words in the light look.

title: In the dark look, the red count on the menu is hard to read
what: The red bubble that counts what needs you is a light red with white numbers in the dark look, about 2.8 to 1. The numbers are small and bold, so they can be misread at a glance.
expected: The count reads at 4.5 to 1 or better.
fix_line: Use a deeper red behind the count, or dark numbers.

title: Many boxes have only a grey hint inside, no name, and the hint vanishes once you type
what: The why box for pausing a gym, the why box for signing a gym out everywhere, the note boxes on feedback and leads, the member box on a delete request, the gym-code box for deleting a gym for ever, the cancel reason, and the boxes for refusing or noting a payment have no name above them. The only words are a grey hint inside the box, which disappears as soon as you type, so you cannot check what the box was for. In the light look that grey hint is about 3.2 to 1, below the readable level.
expected: Every box has a name that stays visible above it, as the other forms in HQ already do.
fix_line: Wrap each of these boxes in the same named field the other forms use.

title: The gym list rows open a gym but do not show or say that they can be opened
what: Each gym row opens the gym when clicked or when Enter is pressed. A screen reader announces it only as a table row, not as something to open. The keyboard highlight is a background shade almost the same as the row, so you cannot see which gym is selected. Space does nothing. On a phone each gym is a plain card with no arrow, unlike the Needs you lines and the number tiles, which carry an arrow.
expected: Each gym is a real link with a clear highlight, and an arrow on the phone card.
fix_line: Make the gym name a link to the gym page, give rows a visible focus ring and an arrow on phones.

title: The Needs you page redraws itself every minute and loses your place
what: While the Needs you page is open, HQ rebuilds the whole page every minute unless you are typing in a box. If you have moved with the keyboard to a line, or a screen reader is reading the page, the selection jumps back to the top of the page and reading starts again.
expected: The page updates only the parts that changed and keeps the selected item where it was.
fix_line: Skip the redraw when nothing changed, and keep focus when it does.

title: A screen reader reads the read-log warning out again every minute
what: The red read-log warning on top of every page is rebuilt every minute as a fresh urgent message, so a screen reader breaks in and reads the same warning again each minute on every page.
expected: The warning is read once when it first appears or changes.
how_often: every minute while the warning shows
fix_line: Rebuild the warning only when its words change.

title: Moving to another page is silent for a screen reader, and the current page is shown by colour only
what: The current page in the side menu and bottom bar is marked only by colour. Nothing tells a screen reader which page is open. When you pick a page, the content changes, but the reading position does not move to the new heading and the tab title stays the same, so a screen reader user does not know the page changed.
expected: The current menu item is marked as current for screen readers. A new page moves the reading position to its heading.
fix_line: Mark the current menu item as current and move focus to the new page heading.

title: On a phone, the More sheet opens but the keyboard and screen reader stay on the page behind it
what: Tapping More slides up the menu sheet over a dark cover, but the selection stays on the More button. With a keyboard or screen reader you keep moving through the page hidden behind the cover before reaching the sheet. Escape and tapping the cover do close it.
expected: Opening More moves the selection into the sheet and keeps it there until the sheet closes.
how_often: every time More is opened with a keyboard or screen reader
fix_line: Move focus into the sheet when it opens and back to More when it closes.

title: Two things on the phone are small to tap: the back link on a gym page and Install app
what: On a phone, the All gyms back link on a gym page is only about one line of small text tall, about 22 pixels, because the rule that enlarges links skips it. The Install app button in the top bar is 36 pixels. Other buttons on the phone are 44 to 46 pixels.
expected: Every tappable thing on the phone is at least 44 pixels tall.
fix_line: Give the back link and Install app a 44 pixel tap height on phones.

title: HQ ignores the bigger text setting in the computer browser
what: All HQ text sizes are fixed. If the browser text size on a computer is set to large, HQ stays the same size. Zooming the page and the phone text size settings still work.
expected: HQ grows with the browser text size setting.
how_often: only for someone who set bigger text
fix_line: Size text relative to the browser setting instead of fixed pixels.

title: If you close the install pop-up, the Install app button disappears with no hint how to install later
what: Tapping Install app opens the browser install pop-up. If you close it, HQ hides the button and does not tell you that you can still install from the browser menu. The button may come back only on a later visit, if the browser offers it again.
expected: After the pop-up is closed, HQ keeps the button or a short line saying how to install from the browser menu.
how_often: once, after closing the install pop-up
fix_line: After a closed install pop-up, show a line saying to use the browser menu to install.

title: No automatic accessibility check ever runs on HQ
what: The automatic accessibility check in the build looks only at the gym admin app. HQ is never checked, so faint colours, missing names and keyboard traps on HQ are found only by hand.
expected: The same automatic check runs over every HQ page in the build.
fix_line: Add HQ pages to the cloud accessibility check.

title: On a computer, the AI side panel cannot be reached or closed well with the keyboard
what: Pressing the AI Assistant button opens the side panel, but the keyboard focus does not move into it: the button disappears and the focus drops to the top of the page, so a keyboard or screen-reader user has to hunt for the panel. Escape does not close it, and after closing it the focus is lost again instead of going back to the button.
expected: Opening the panel puts the focus in its ask box, Escape closes it, and closing it returns the focus to the AI Assistant button.
who: owners who use a keyboard or screen reader on a computer
how_often: every time the panel opens or closes
fix_line: Move the focus into the panel when it opens, close it on Escape, and give the focus back to the button on close

title: A screen reader hears 'Thinking' but never hears that the answer has come
what: While the assistant works, a 'Thinking' line is announced. When the answer card arrives that line just vanishes and the card is not announced, and the focus stays in the ask box. A blind owner does not know the answer is there or where it is.
expected: When the answer arrives, a short line such as 'Answer ready' is announced, or the card's heading is announced.
fix_line: Announce the answer's arrival in a polite live line when the Thinking line goes away

title: Member names in an answer and past tasks in History can be tapped but look like plain text
what: In an answer card, each member's name opens that member, and in History each past task puts its words back in the box. Both are drawn as plain text with no border, arrow or colour, so a first-time owner does not know they can tap them. The picture of the member list shows two plain names.
expected: Rows that open something show a small arrow (as other lists in the panel do) or a clear row look, and History says 'Tap to ask again'.
how_often: every member list answer and every History visit
fix_line: Add the panel's usual arrow to these rows and a short hint on History

title: When today's questions are used up, the only reason shown is faint grey text inside a locked box
what: At the daily limit the ask box, the microphone and the send button all turn off. The only words saying why are the box's greyed placeholder; no line above the box says it (the 'questions left' line stops at 1). A screen reader reads only 'Ask or give a task, dimmed', and greyed placeholder text in a locked box is hard to read in both colour schemes.
expected: A plain line above the box says that today's free questions are used up and when they come back, read out by a screen reader.
who: owners who hit the daily limit, worst for screen-reader users
how_often: every time the limit is reached
fix_line: Show the limit line as real text above the box when it is locked

title: Closing the voice sheet after speaking throws away what was heard
what: After the owner speaks, the sheet shows the words it heard to fix. Cancel, Escape or a tap outside closes it and the words are gone. Opening it again starts the microphone afresh, so the owner must speak again, which uses more of the day's voice minutes.
expected: Closing after the words are heard keeps them, for example by putting them in the ask box, so nothing spoken is lost.
how_often: whenever the voice sheet is closed after speaking
fix_line: On close, put the heard words in the ask box instead of dropping them

title: A changed member AI switch or monthly limit is lost without a word if the credits sheet is closed
what: In AI credits, the owner can turn members' AI answers on or off and change the monthly limit, then must press Save changes. Closing the sheet with the cross, Escape or a tap outside throws the change away with no warning, so the owner may think members' AI is off when it is still on.
expected: Closing with an unsaved change asks 'Save your change?' or keeps the change until saved.
how_often: whenever the sheet is closed before saving
fix_line: Ask before closing when the switch or limit changed and was not saved

title: Several AI Assistant buttons are smaller than the panel's own finger-size rule
what: The panel's rule is 44 points for anything tapped. In the assistant the credits pill and the Ask/History tabs are 36, the 'Open Members' style links 32, the language and Now/Later choices 34, member rows in an answer 36, the small rewrite chips 36 and the panel's close cross 40.
expected: Every tap target is at least 44 points high, like the rest of the panel.
fix_line: Raise these controls to the panel's 44-point minimum

title: The ask box shows no focus ring when reached with the keyboard
what: The ask box turns off the browser's focus outline and its frame does not change when it has the focus, so a keyboard user cannot see that the box is selected until typing starts.
expected: The ask box's frame lights up in the accent colour when it has the keyboard focus, like other focus rings in the panel.
fix_line: Show an accent frame on the ask box while it has the focus

title: No automatic accessibility check ever looks at the AI Assistant
what: The panel's automatic accessibility crawl visits the assistant's address, but the demo gym has the assistant off, so it only sees the Today page it falls back to. The assistant's own test takes pictures in dark and light but runs no accessibility check. Contrast, labels and roles in the assistant are never measured.
expected: The accessibility check runs on the assistant's main screen, its cards and its sheets in dark and light.
fix_line: Run the accessibility check inside the assistant's existing picture test

title: Closing the side panel throws away a half-typed request
what: Words typed in the ask box live only while the panel is open. Closing the panel with the cross, or leaving the full-screen assistant on a phone, empties the box; the chat itself is kept.
expected: A half-typed request is still in the box when the owner opens the assistant again.
how_often: whenever the panel is closed mid-typing
fix_line: Keep the box's words with the chat so they survive closing

title: On Staff & sign-in, a screen reader hears the same button names on every person, with no name
what: Each person on the Staff & sign-in list has the buttons Make sign-in code, Sign out everywhere and Remove, and a Trainer tick. A screen reader reads them only by those words, so moving through the buttons gives 'Remove, Remove, Remove' and 'Trainer, Trainer' with no sign of whose they are. Remove and Sign out everywhere cannot be undone.
expected: Each button and tick says whose it is to a screen reader, for example 'Remove Suresh' or 'Suresh is a trainer'.
who: owners who use a screen reader
fix_line: Give each person's buttons and tick a spoken name that includes the person's name; the shared button already allows this

title: Forgot your PIN, Other ways back in and Sign out look like grey words, not buttons
what: On the sign-in card, 'Forgot your PIN?' is grey bold words with no outline, no fill and no underline. The same plain look is used for 'Can't use WhatsApp? Other ways back in', for Sign out on the terms screen, and for the red Remove word on the staff list. A first-time owner who is locked out may not see that the words can be tapped, and these are the ways back in.
expected: Every tappable thing has an outline, a fill or an underline, so it plainly looks tappable, most of all the ways back in after a forgotten PIN.
fix_line: Give the plain button style an outline or an underline, or use the outlined style for these ways back in

title: While waiting for the WhatsApp message, a screen reader reads the waiting line out again every minute
what: The 'Waiting for your message. The code works for N more minutes.' line is marked as a live message, and its minutes go down every minute and its words change when the check starts. Each change makes a screen reader read the whole line out again while the person is busy in WhatsApp or scanning the code.
expected: The waiting line is read out once; the minutes left stay on screen without being read out each time.
who: owners who use a screen reader
fix_line: Keep the minutes-left words outside the live message, or read out only the change from waiting to checked

title: The 'Other ways back in' button does not tell a screen reader whether the list is open
what: Tapping 'Can't use WhatsApp? Other ways back in' shows or hides a box under it, but the button never says if the box is open or shut, and the shared button has no way to say so. A screen reader user hears nothing change after the tap.
expected: The button says open or closed, and the box that appears is announced or reached next.
who: owners who use a screen reader
fix_line: Let the shared button say expanded or collapsed, and use it on this toggle

title: No automatic accessibility check ever looks at sign-in, new gym, Forgot PIN, WhatsApp check or the terms screen
what: The panel's automatic accessibility crawl visits only signed-in pages of the demo gym, in the dark look only. The sign-in card, Create my gym, Forgot your PIN, the WhatsApp number check and the terms screen are never visited, and the light look is never checked by it. Staff & sign-in is visited only in the demo gym, where the people list is not shown.
expected: The crawl also opens the signed-out screens and Staff & sign-in with people listed, in both looks.
fix_line: Add the signed-out screens and a light-look pass to the accessibility crawl

title: The colour code boxes on Branding show no focus ring when reached with the keyboard
what: The boxes where the owner types the brand colour code and the background tone code turn off the browser's focus outline, and their frame does not change when they have the focus. A keyboard user cannot see which box is selected until they start typing.
expected: Every box shows a clear ring or frame change when it gets the keyboard focus, in the dark and the light look.
how_often: every time a keyboard is used
fix_line: Show the accent ring on the colour code boxes when they have the focus.

title: The admin app ignores the bigger text setting in the computer browser
what: Every text size in the admin app is a fixed number of screen dots, set on each piece of text. If an owner sets the browser's text size to large, the admin app stays the same size. Page zoom still works. The smallest notes on Branding are 11 and 12 dots.
expected: Text grows when the browser's text size setting is raised, and stays readable at the largest setting.
how_often: every time, for anyone using bigger browser text
fix_line: Size text from the browser's base size instead of fixed dots.

title: In the light look, the 'No logo yet' words are hard to read
what: The logo box is always painted in the member app's dark background, but the 'No logo yet' words inside it use the admin app's grey for quiet words. In the light look that grey is dark, so it sits at about 3.4 to 1 on the near-black box. Small words need at least 4.5 to 1.
expected: The words inside the logo box read at 4.5 to 1 or better in both the dark and the light look.
how_often: every time in light mode before a logo is added
fix_line: Use a light word colour inside the dark logo box.

title: Which of the other logo colours is picked is shown only by a slightly different frame
what: Under the suggested colour, the other colours from the logo are plain coloured squares. The one in use gets a frame of a different shade, the same thickness, with no tick. A screen reader hears only a colour code, such as 'Use this colour: #3A7BD5', not a colour name.
expected: The picked square is clearly marked by more than colour (a tick or a thicker frame), and each square says something a person can picture.
how_often: every time a logo has more than one colour
fix_line: Add a tick to the picked square and a plain colour name to each.

title: The two logo choices behave like a pick-one list for a screen reader, but the arrow keys do nothing
what: After the background is taken off a logo, the 'Without the background' and 'Keep my logo as it is' cards tell a screen reader they are a pick-one list. In such a list people expect the arrow keys to move between choices. Here the arrow keys do nothing, and each card is a separate Tab stop.
expected: Either the arrow keys move between the two choices, or the cards are announced as plain buttons.
who: owners using a keyboard or screen reader
how_often: every time a plain logo background is taken off
fix_line: Add arrow key movement to the two logo choices.

title: Closing a half-filled form with the cross or Escape throws away everything typed, with no question
what: Add member, Sell membership and Collect payment close at once on the cross in the corner or the Escape key, the same as Cancel. Everything typed (name, mobile, birthday, address, emergency contact, price, amount, notes) is gone, and the next open starts empty. On a phone the cross sits at the top right where a thumb can hit it by mistake while scrolling a long form.
expected: When something has been typed, closing asks 'Throw away what you typed?' or keeps the typing for the next open.
how_often: whenever a filled form is closed by mistake
fix_line: Ask before closing a form that has typing in it

title: On a phone, '+ New batch' can sit hidden off the right edge of the batch row
what: On Add member the batch choices are one row that scrolls sideways on a phone, with the scroll bar hidden. The gym's batches come first and 'None' and '+ New batch' come last, so a gym with three or four batches has '+ New batch' off the screen and nothing shows the row can be swiped. A first-time desk person does not find how to add a new batch. The pass company row ends with '+ Other company' in the same way.
expected: '+ New batch' is always in view (first, or the row wraps), or the row shows it continues past the edge.
who: owners and front desk on a phone
how_often: every member added in a gym with several batches
fix_line: Let the batch and pass chip rows wrap, or put the add-new chip first

title: On Add member, the 'already has this number' and 'could not save' messages appear at the top, out of sight
what: Add member is a long form with the button at the bottom. When the number belongs to an archived member, or the save fails, the red message (with its Bring them back and Open their page buttons) appears at the very top of the form. The form is not scrolled up and the keyboard focus stays on the button, so on a phone the desk sees nothing happen after pressing Add member. Only a screen reader hears it.
expected: The message is brought into view (and focused) like the wrong-box messages are, so the desk sees it and its buttons at once.
who: owners and front desk on a phone
how_often: each clashing number or failed save on Add member
fix_line: Scroll the form to the top message and move the focus to it when it appears

title: A screen reader does not read the explanation under 'Comes with a pass' or 'Can train at every branch'
what: The tick boxes on the member form have a grey line under them saying what the tick means: for a pass, no plan, no dues and never on the renewal list. That line is not tied to the tick box, so a screen reader reads only the tick box's name and skips what it does to the member's money.
expected: The screen reader reads the explanation together with the tick box.
who: owners and desk staff using a screen reader
how_often: every time these boxes are reached
fix_line: Link the shared tick box's hint to the box so it is read out

title: 'Cancel receipt' stays greyed out with no word saying a reason of 3 letters is needed
what: On Cancel this receipt, the red button is greyed until 3 letters are typed in Reason. Nothing says so: the hint only says the reason is saved with the receipt. The message 'Write a short reason' can never show, because the greyed button cannot be pressed. An owner who opens the sheet sees a dead button.
expected: The hint says a short reason is needed to cancel, or the button stays pressable and shows the message.
fix_line: Say in the hint that a reason is needed before the receipt can be cancelled

title: On Collect payment, a wrong amount or date is shown only in a banner, not at the box
what: When the amount or the date received is wrong, Collect payment shows the reason in a red banner at the top. The wrong box itself is not marked red and not marked wrong for a screen reader, unlike the sell sheet and the member form, so the desk has to work out which box the banner means.
expected: The wrong box turns red with its message under it, as on the other forms.
how_often: each wrong amount or date on Collect payment
fix_line: Show the amount and date messages on their own boxes

title: When a payment link cannot be made, the message says show the UPI QR or try again, but neither button is there
what: On Collect payment or Sell membership, tapping Make a payment link when the link cannot be made (for example the member has no mobile number) shows 'Show the UPI QR instead, or try again'. The box has now switched to the link view, so the Show UPI QR and Make a payment link buttons are hidden and nothing replaces them. Once any link is on screen there is also no way back to the UPI QR.
expected: After a failed or open link, the desk still sees Show UPI QR and Try again (or a Back), so the money can still be taken on the same sheet.
how_often: every time a payment link fails
fix_line: Keep the UPI QR and try-again buttons showing when a link fails, and add a Back from the link view

title: Moving through the branch list with the arrow keys opens each branch in turn
what: The branch picker at the top switches branch the moment its choice changes. With the keyboard, in common Windows browsers each arrow press on the closed list changes the choice, so the owner is thrown into the first branch passed and sent to the home page, before reaching the one wanted.
expected: A keyboard user can move through the branches and only opens one on Enter, or the picker is a list of buttons.
how_often: every keyboard use of the picker
fix_line: Open the branch only on a confirmed pick, not on every change of the list

title: Open payments, the move notice buttons and the branch picker are smaller than the panel's finger-size rule
what: The panel's own rule is 44 points for anything tapped. The Open payments link under the Pay online box has no padding, so it is only as tall as its 13-point words. The OK and Open now buttons on the moving-address notice are about 31 points tall, and the branch picker is 40.
expected: Every one of these is at least 44 points tall.
who: owners and front desk on phones
fix_line: Give these three controls the same 44-point height as the panel's buttons

title: A screen reader is not told the result of a branch member search
what: After Find on 'Member from another branch', and while typing in 'Find a member in any branch', the result or the 'No member ... has this number' line appears on screen but is not announced, so a screen-reader user hears nothing after the search.
expected: The result line, or how many were found, is read out when it appears.
who: owners and front desk using a screen reader
fix_line: Mark the search result line so it is read out when it changes

title: The day-by-day visit charts tell their details only by colour, bar height and a mouse-hover note
what: The 30-day check-in bars on Visits and the training squares on a member page show each day's count or 'trained' only through bar height, a brighter colour for today, or an orange square. The words for each day sit in a hover note that a phone tap and a screen reader do not get, so those users only hear the short summary line.
expected: Each chart has a short spoken summary (or a hidden list of days) and today or a trained day is marked by more than colour.
who: owners and desk staff using a screen reader or a phone
how_often: every time the chart is read
fix_line: Give each chart a spoken summary and mark today or trained days with a shape or word, not only colour

title: No automatic accessibility check ever looks at Diet plans, Challenges, Gym timings, Busy machines or Entry machines
what: The automatic page check visits Visits, Enquiries, Expenses, Import, Help and a member page, but never opens Diet plans, Challenges, Gym timings, Busy machines or Entry machines, never opens any pop-up, and only looks in the dark look. Faults on those pages can ship unseen.
expected: Every page of the panel, its main pop-ups and the light look are checked automatically.
who: owners who rely on a screen reader or keyboard
fix_line: Add these pages, a few pop-ups and the light look to the automatic page check

title: On Trainers, the keyboard ring vanishes on the booking grid, member picks, bookings and working days
what: The free and booked times in the trainers' week grid, the member list in Book a session, a trainer's bookings and the working-day buttons are made with all their look wiped, which also wipes the ring that shows where the keyboard is. A keyboard user tabbing through cannot see which time or day they are on.
expected: Every button shows a clear ring when reached with the keyboard, like the rest of the panel's buttons and tap rows.
who: owners and desk staff using a keyboard on a computer
fix_line: Give these buttons the panel's own focus ring class, or stop wiping the browser's ring

title: Some things on these pages are smaller to tap than the panel's own finger-size rule
what: The Free and booked times in the trainers' week grid are 36 points tall, the working-day buttons on a trainer's profile are 40, and the member name links on Member messages, Member questions and Training progress are only as tall as the text. The panel's rule is 44.
expected: Every tappable thing is at least 44 points tall so a thumb hits it first time.
who: owners, desk staff and trainers on a phone
fix_line: Raise these to the 44-point size the rest of the panel uses

title: On Today, a screen reader hears 'Message' on every person row with no name
what: Each person row on Today has a 'Message' link that opens WhatsApp. Its spoken name is only 'Message', so a screen reader user going through the links hears 'Message, Message, Message' and cannot tell who each one is for. The renew list's own Message button on the same page does say the member's name.
expected: Each link says who it messages, for example 'Message Riya Sharma on WhatsApp'.
who: owners and desk staff using a screen reader
fix_line: Add the member's name to each Message link's spoken label

title: On Today, a person's name opens their page but looks like plain text
what: In Today's lists, the member's picture, name and status line open the member's page, but they carry no underline, arrow or frame. A first-time owner sees only the orange 'Message' as something to tap and may not know the name opens the member.
expected: A row that opens something shows it, for example with the arrow or the firm-up frame other panel rows use.
fix_line: Give the name part of each row the panel's tap-row look with an arrow

title: A screen reader hears only 'Edit' or 'Open' on product and app member cards, not the price, stock or orders
what: On Shop products, the top of each card (picture, name, price, stock, Hidden) is one button that a screen reader names only 'Edit <product>'. On Joined in the app, each member card is one button named only 'Open <name>'. The given name replaces everything inside, so a blind owner never hears the price, how many are left, that a product is hidden, or a member's orders and money paid.
expected: The card's button name, or text next to it, includes the facts shown on the card (price, stock, hidden; orders and paid), so a screen reader user gets the same facts as a sighted one.
who: owners and desk staff who use a screen reader
how_often: every time the product list or app members list is read aloud
fix_line: Let the card read out its own words, or add the price, stock and order facts to its spoken name

title: Three product card buttons have a spoken name that does not match the words on them
what: The buttons read '+10 stock', 'Hide from app' and 'Add photo' on screen, but their spoken names are 'Add 10 to stock, <product>', 'Hide <product>' and 'Add a photo of <product>'. A person using voice control who says 'click Hide from app' or 'click +10 stock' gets nothing, because the spoken name does not contain the words they see.
expected: Each spoken name starts with the words shown on the button, then adds the product name.
fix_line: Make each spoken name begin with the button's visible words

title: On a workout offer, member names open the member's page but look like plain text
what: In the list of members in a workout offer, each name is a link to that member's page, but it is drawn in the normal text colour with no underline and no arrow. Nothing tells a first-time user the name can be tapped.
expected: The name looks tappable: link colour or underline, or an arrow at the end of the row.
how_often: every time the offer list is shown
fix_line: Show the member name as a link or add an arrow to the row

title: The colour dots on each product choice are smaller than the panel's own finger-size rule
what: When a product comes in flavours or sizes, each choice row has a row of colour dots to tap. They are 32 dots across, while the panel's own rule for anything tappable is 44. On a phone they sit close together and are easy to miss.
expected: Each colour dot has a tap area of at least 44 by 44, as the bigger colour dots higher in the same form already do.
who: owners editing products on a phone
how_often: every time a choice colour is picked
fix_line: Give the small colour dots the same 44 tap area as the big ones

title: The number tiles on Today open a list, but look like plain number cards
what: Each tile in Your numbers (fees collected, new members, busiest hours and so on) opens the list behind that number when tapped. On screen a tile is a flat card with a big number, a small heading, a grey line and a little picture. There is no arrow, no 'See list' and no underline, so a first-time owner reads them as a report and may never find the lists behind them. A screen reader does hear 'Open the list'.
expected: A tile that opens a list shows it, for example with the arrow other tappable rows in the panel use, or a 'See who' line.
fix_line: Add an arrow or a 'See the list' line to each number tile

title: With the keyboard, the bell panel does not take the focus, and closing it loses your place
what: Pressing the bell opens the Notifications panel, but the keyboard focus stays on the bell. When the panel is closed with Escape while the focus is inside it, the focus is not put back on the bell, so a keyboard or screen reader user starts again from the top of the page. The panel's spoken name is always the English word 'Notifications', also in Hinglish.
expected: Opening the panel moves the focus into it, closing it puts the focus back on the bell, and the panel's spoken name follows the chosen language.
who: owners and staff using a keyboard or screen reader
how_often: every time the bell is used with the keyboard
fix_line: Move the focus into the bell panel when it opens and back to the bell when it closes, and translate its name

title: Dark | Light and English | Hinglish are announced as pick-one lists, but the arrow keys do nothing
what: Both switches tell a screen reader they are a pick-one list. In such a list people expect the arrow keys to move between choices. Here the arrow keys do nothing, and each choice is a separate Tab stop. This is on the first screen, in the top bar and in Settings.
expected: Either the arrow keys move between the two choices, or the choices are announced as plain buttons with on or off.
who: owners and staff using a keyboard or screen reader
fix_line: Add arrow key movement to the two switches, or make them plain on/off buttons

title: The side menu's group headings, 'More below' and the 'Pay now' link are smaller than the panel's finger-size rule
what: The panel's own rule is 44 points for anything tapped. The side menu's group headings, which fold a group, are 20 to 22 points tall, and 'More below' is 28. The 'Pay now' words on the stopped-paying line on Today, and on the MettleUp billing card, are a plain text link one line tall, also on a phone.
expected: Every tappable thing is at least the panel's finger size, most of all 'Pay now', which an owner whose gym is about to be locked will need.
fix_line: Give 'Pay now' the button look and the group headings and 'More below' more height

title: 'Not now' on the put-on-your-phone card hides it for good and never says where to find it again
what: On a phone, Today shows a card to put the admin app on the home screen. Its button says 'Not now', which sounds like it will come back, but tapping it hides the card on that device for good. The card does not say the same help is in Settings.
expected: Either the card comes back later, or the card says it can still be found in Settings.
who: owners and staff on a phone
fix_line: Add a line saying the install help stays in Settings, or call the button 'Hide'

title: The 'Your gym is ready' card shows once and never says where the gym code and join link live after
what: Right after a gym is made, a card shows the gym code, the join link, its QR and Share. It is shown only once: closing it with Done, the cross or Escape ends it. The card does not say that the same code and link stay under Settings, Invite members. Only the 'Open the QR poster' button hints at it.
expected: The card says where the code and link can be found again, for example 'You can find this any time in Settings, Invite members'.
fix_line: Add one line saying the code and link stay in Settings, Invite members

title: A screen reader user cannot speak to the coach: the mic only works while held
what: The coach chat mic records only while a finger stays on it and stops the moment it lifts. With a screen reader on, a double-tap presses and lets go at once, so nothing is heard. There is no tap-to-start, tap-to-stop way. The coach chat is hidden today.
expected: The mic can also be started and stopped with single taps, or offers a screen reader action, so people using a screen reader can talk to the coach.
how_often: every time, once the coach chat is switched on
fix_line: Let a tap start and a second tap stop the recording.

title: In the coach chat a screen reader cannot tell who said what, and new replies are not read out
what: The member's messages sit on the right in orange and the coach's on the left in grey, with no spoken 'You' or 'Coach'. A new reply or the typing dots are not announced, so a screen reader user does not know the answer has come. The coach chat is hidden today.
expected: Each message is read with who sent it, and a new coach reply is announced.
how_often: every message, once the coach chat is switched on
fix_line: Add who sent it to each message and announce new replies.

title: In an exercise's history, the best set is marked only by colour, and drop and failure sets only by a letter
what: On the History tab of an exercise, the best set of each workout is shown only with an orange wash and bold orange text. Drop sets and sets to failure show just 'D' or 'F'. A screen reader says nothing about the best set and reads the bare letter, and a colour-blind member may miss the highlight.
expected: The best set also says it in words (for example 'best set'), and D and F are read as 'drop set' and 'to failure'.
fix_line: Add spoken words for the best set and the D and F marks.

title: Each record row on the Charts page opens the exercise but shows no arrow
what: In the records list on the Charts page, every row opens that exercise when tapped, but it has no arrow or other sign. The 'See all records' line and the other lists on the same page do show an arrow, so these rows look like plain text.
expected: Record rows show the same small arrow as the other rows that open something.
fix_line: Add the arrow to each record row.

title: A screen reader is not told when a Balance check choice fails to save
what: When 'Keep it', 'Go back' or 'Not now' on the Balance check card fails, a red line appears in the card, but it is not announced. A screen reader user hears nothing and may think it worked.
expected: The failure line is announced when it appears.
fix_line: Make the failure line announce itself.

title: No automatic accessibility check ever runs on the phone app
what: The automatic accessibility check in the build looks only at the gym admin app. The phone app's screens are never checked by a tool, so missing spoken names and small tap areas are found only by reading the code.
expected: An automatic check of spoken names and tap sizes runs over the phone app's screens in the build.
fix_line: Add an accessibility check to the phone app's cloud tests.

title: Only half of the round help button is on screen, so the part you can tap is about half the finger size
what: The floating Help and feedback button is 48 points wide but sits half behind the screen edge, so only about 24 points of it can be touched, right on the edge where Android's back swipe lives. Moving it needs a drag, which a screen-reader user cannot do.
expected: The part of the button you can touch is at least the app's own 48-point finger size, away from the back-swipe edge, and it can be moved without dragging (or hidden from Settings, which exists).
how_often: every time they tap the help button
fix_line: Let more of the tab show, or give it a touch area that reaches into the screen

title: The Undo bar runs out after 6 seconds even for a member using a screen reader
what: After a delete the Undo bar stays 6 seconds and only stops its clock while a finger rests on it. A screen-reader user has to swipe to reach it, and the clock keeps running; the phone's own 'time to take action' setting is not used. On iPhone the bar is not even read out, since the announcement used works on Android only.
expected: With a screen reader on, the Undo stays until it is reached (or for the phone's chosen time), and it is read out on both phones.
who: members who use a screen reader
fix_line: Make the Undo wait longer or stay while a screen reader is on, and announce it

title: The gym sync sign-in form cannot be filled in reliably with a screen reader
what: The Email, Password, Gym code and Name boxes have no spoken name, so once typed in a screen reader reads only what is in them. The 'Create account / Sign in' choice is not said to be a choice and does not say which one is picked, and is smaller than finger size. The agreement tick box is not said to be a tick box and never says if it is ticked.
expected: Every box says what it is for, the choice says which one is picked, and the tick box says ticked or not ticked.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time (feature is behind a switch)
fix_line: Give each box a spoken name and give the choice and tick box their proper roles and states

title: When a backup, restore, gym connect or erase fails, a screen reader says nothing
what: Several Settings cards show their failure only as small red words placed under the buttons, with no spoken announcement, although the app's own rule is that error lines are read out. A screen-reader user taps the button and hears no result.
expected: Every failure line in these cards is read out when it appears, like the app's shared error line.
who: members who use a screen reader
fix_line: Use the shared error line that is read out in these cards

title: Closing the feedback sheet while speaking throws away what was said
what: If the sheet is closed (a tap outside, the back button) while recording or while the voice is being turned into text, the recording is deleted and the words never reach the box. Typed words are kept when the sheet opens again, spoken ones are not.
expected: Words already spoken are still turned into text and waiting in the box when the sheet opens again, or the member is asked before they are thrown away.
fix_line: Finish turning the clip into text and keep it with the unsent message

title: The AI key box and its Edit button do not say what they are for
what: The box for typing your own AI key has no spoken name, and its button only says 'Edit', so a screen-reader user does not know what is being edited.
expected: The box and button say 'AI key' in their spoken names.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time (feature is behind a switch)
fix_line: Give the box and the Edit button spoken names that mention the AI key

title: Home-screen widget buttons can be hard to read when the app is in light mode
what: The widgets always have a dark background, but their label and action words (Start, Resume, Check in, Open) take the app's current accent colour. In light mode that accent is made darker so it reads on white, so on the dark widget it reads poorly: about 3 to 1 for MettleUp's own orange, and worse for a gym with a dark brand colour. The words are small (11 and 13 points), which need 4.5 to 1.
expected: Words on the widget are easy to read whatever the phone's theme and the gym's colour.
who: members who use light mode and add a widget
fix_line: Always give the widgets the dark-mode accent colour, or check its contrast against the widget's dark background

title: The Stop control on the Health Connect rows does not look like a button
what: When sending workouts, weight or steps with Health Connect is on, the way to stop it is the word Stop in small grey text at the side of the row, with no outline, fill or icon. A first-time user can read it as a status word and not know it can be tapped. The tap area itself is big enough and the screen reader calls it a button.
expected: Stop looks tappable, like the other buttons on this card.
fix_line: Draw Stop as a small outlined button or in the accent colour

title: After the WhatsApp check, a screen reader is not told whether the gym was found
what: When a member comes back from WhatsApp, the screen changes on its own to Checking, then to either the gym that was found or Not found. None of these changes is read out, so a blind member hears nothing and must hunt around the screen to learn the result.
expected: The result (found at this gym, or not found) is read out as soon as it shows.
fix_line: Read out the found or not-found line when the check finishes

title: On the start-up error screen, a failed Save my data file is not read out
what: If saving the data file fails (the phone cannot share, no file, or the save broke), the reason appears as small grey text under the buttons. A screen reader does not say it, so a blind member thinks the file was saved.
expected: The save result is read out when it appears.
who: members using a screen reader whose app cannot open
fix_line: Make the save result line one that is read out when it appears

title: Got it, Open Profile and Skip look like plain words, not buttons
what: On the one-time Workout-tab note, Got it is plain grey words and Open Profile plain orange words, with no outline or underline. On the intro screens, Skip is plain grey words in the corner. Elsewhere on the welcome, text buttons are underlined, so these read as labels to a first-time user.
expected: Every text button shows it can be tapped, as the underlined links on the welcome do.
fix_line: Give these text buttons the same underline or outline as the other welcome links

title: On the Body page, your own entries can be tapped to fix or delete but look exactly like the trainer's entries, which cannot
what: In the list under the graph, each of the member's own weigh-ins and measurements opens a fix-or-delete sheet when tapped, but the row has no arrow, pencil or other sign. The trainer's rows look the same and do nothing. A first-time member has no way to see that a wrong weigh-in can be fixed from here.
expected: Rows that open something show a clear sign (for example an arrow or pencil), and rows that do nothing look different.
fix_line: Add a small arrow or pencil to the member's own rows

title: The note about a wrong link on the Workout tab can only be closed by tapping it, with nothing showing that
what: When a broken app link lands on the Workout tab, a plain grey card explains it. Tapping the card closes it, but there is no close mark, so sighted members do not know how to get rid of it (a screen reader does hear Dismiss).
expected: The note shows a visible close mark or button.
fix_line: Add a small close mark to the note

title: When importing from Hevy or Strong, a screen reader does not say which choice (add to or replace) is picked
what: The two import choices are large cards. The picked one turns orange with a tick, but the screen reader is not told they are buttons or which one is selected, so a blind member may start a replace without knowing it.
expected: Each choice is read out as a choice, with selected or not selected.
fix_line: Tell the screen reader each card is a choice and which is picked

title: The Got it button on the Profile tab note looks like plain grey text
what: The note saying progress now lives in Profile has a Got it control drawn in the same grey as normal text, with no button shape or orange colour, so it does not look like something to tap.
expected: Got it looks like a button or link (the app's orange link colour or a button shape).
fix_line: Draw Got it in the link colour or as a small button

title: Undo for a deleted set in a live workout is hidden from screen readers and vanishes after 4 seconds
what: When a member removes a set during a workout, a small 'Set removed  Undo' bar shows for 4 seconds and then goes away for good. The Undo word is not marked as a button and has no spoken name, the bar is not read out when it appears, and its tap area is small. A screen reader user, or anyone slow to react, loses the only way to get the set back. The app's own undo bar used elsewhere does all of this right (read out, 48 point button).
expected: The removed-set bar is read out, Undo is a named button of full finger size, and it stays long enough to reach (or uses the app's shared undo bar).
how_often: every time a set is removed
fix_line: Show the removed-set message with the app's shared undo bar instead of the hand-made one

title: A few buttons on these screens are smaller than a finger
what: The previous and next month (or year) buttons on the monthly report are only about 28 points tall. The Cancel word while picking two photos to compare has no minimum size. The minus and plus buttons for sets and reps in the routine editor reach about 46 points. The app's own rule elsewhere is 48.
expected: Every one of these is at least 48 points to the finger, like the other buttons on the same screens.
fix_line: Give these buttons a 48 point minimum height and width

title: In the routine editor, a screen reader is not told when Move up, Move down, minus or plus cannot be used, or what the number is
what: At the top or bottom of the list, or at the lowest or highest sets and reps, these buttons only turn grey. A screen reader still announces them as normal buttons, and tapping does nothing. The minus and plus buttons say 'Decrease sets' or 'Increase sets' but not the current number, so the member cannot hear the result of a tap.
expected: Buttons that cannot be used are announced as unavailable, and the current number is spoken with the minus and plus buttons.
fix_line: Mark these buttons unavailable when greyed and add the current number to what they say

title: 'Take back' on a waiting pause or renew request is small faint grey text that does not look like a button
what: Under a request still waiting for the desk, the only way to take it back is a short line of the smallest, faintest grey text. It has no button shape, no colour and no underline, and its finger area is well under the usual size.
expected: Take back looks like a button (a ghost button like 'Pause my plan') and is at least a finger wide and tall.
how_often: every time a request is waiting
fix_line: Show Take back as a normal small button with the usual finger size

title: In the pause calendar a screen reader reads each day as a computer date, and the day circles are small
what: Each day in the pause calendar is announced as a raw code like '2026-12-04' instead of 'Friday 4 December', and today is marked only by a thin ring. The day circles are 40 points, under the 48 the rest of the app uses.
expected: Days are read as spoken dates with 'today' said, and each day is a full finger size.
fix_line: Read each day as a spoken date, say today, and make the circles a bit larger

title: The 'Your plan ends on Friday' card on the Workout tab opens the Gym tab, but nothing shows it can be tapped
what: The whole card is tappable and takes you to your gym page, but it looks like a plain notice: no arrow, no button and no words like 'See my plan'. Only a screen reader is told it opens something.
expected: The card shows it can be tapped, for example with an arrow on the right or a 'See my plan' line.
how_often: when the plan is near its end
fix_line: Add an arrow or a short 'See my plan' line to the card

title: A screen reader user cannot move through the points on an exercise chart
what: On an exercise's progress chart, a past point can only be picked by touching and sliding a finger over the line. A screen reader user hears only the one number shown above the chart and cannot step to other dates or open the workout behind a point.
expected: Each point (or a step left / step right control) can be reached and read by a screen reader, and opening that point's workout works the same way.
who: members who use a screen reader
how_often: every time they open an exercise chart
fix_line: Make the chart a slider a screen reader can swipe through, saying each date and value, with open-workout on the picked point

title: On the month report calendar, the days trained are shown by colour only
what: The month calendar fills in the days trained with the orange colour. A screen reader reads each day as a plain number, so it cannot tell which days were trained, and someone who cannot see the colour well has only a slightly bolder number to go on.
expected: Each trained day says 'trained' to a screen reader, and has a mark besides colour (a tick or dot) on screen.
who: members who use a screen reader or see colour poorly
fix_line: Give each day a spoken name like '12, trained' and add a small mark to trained days

title: The minus 5 s, Stopwatch and plus 5 s buttons on the hold timer are small to tap
what: On the hold timer, the three buttons that set the countdown are 38 points tall with no extra touch room, below the app's own rule of at least 48 for every tap target. Mid-plank with sweaty hands they are easy to miss.
expected: Every button on the hold timer is at least 48 points to the finger, as the app's rule says.
how_often: every time they set a countdown
fix_line: Add extra touch room around these three buttons or make them 48 tall

title: The locked suggested-weight line can be tapped but looks like a grey note
what: For a free member, the line 'Suggested weight and reps: MettleUp Plus' under an exercise opens the MettleUp Plus explanation, but it is faint grey words with a small target icon and no arrow or lock, so it reads as a plain note.
expected: A line that opens something shows it can be tapped, for example with an arrow or a lock and a stronger colour.
who: free members once the Plus switch is on
fix_line: Add an arrow or lock to the line and give it the tappable colour

title: Tapping Not now a second time on a muscle tip stops it for good without saying so on screen
what: A muscle tip's Not now button always just says 'Not now'. The second time, it puts that tip away for good. Only a screen reader hears 'Don't suggest it again'; a sighted member is not told, and nothing on the card says where to get the tip back.
expected: The button's visible words change to say it will not ask again (as the spoken name already does), or the member is told where to turn the tip back on.
how_often: the second time they put off the same tip
fix_line: Show 'Not now, don't ask again' on the last Not now, matching the spoken words

title: The small "i" on a set that explains its target is hard to hit
what: When a set has a reason behind its target, a tiny round "i" is drawn on the corner of the set number. It is 14 points wide and its touch area reaches only about 30 points, and it sits on top of the set number, which opens the set type choices. A finger often opens the wrong thing.
expected: The "why" mark can be tapped on its own with a normal finger, at least 48 points, without landing on the set number.
how_often: every set that shows the mark
fix_line: Make the why mark larger or move it beside the set number so its touch area is full finger size

title: A screen reader skips the explaining line under some workout settings
what: In workout settings, rows such as Default rest, Rest-over sound, Weight step and Reps to aim for read out only their name and value. The small line under each one is never read, including "Workout sounds are off: Rest is over only buzzes" and "Change it per exercise from the exercise's menu".
expected: A screen reader user hears the same explanation a sighted member reads under each setting.
fix_line: Add the explaining line to what the screen reader says for these rows, or as a hint

title: The minimised workout bar does not say the rest time left or the workout time
what: The bar above the tabs shows the rest countdown or the time trained in large numbers. A screen reader only hears "Rest, 3 sets done, tap to open the workout", never how many seconds of rest are left or how long the workout has run.
expected: The bar reads out the same time it shows, for example "Rest, 45 seconds left".
how_often: every time a workout is minimised
fix_line: Put the shown time into what the screen reader says for the bar

title: "Not now" on the watch install card looks like plain grey words
what: On the one-time "Install MettleUp on your watch" card at the start of a workout, "Not now" is grey text with no outline or underline, next to the orange "Install on watch". It does not look like something to tap.
expected: Every choice on the card looks tappable.
how_often: once, the first workout with a watch
fix_line: Give Not now a button look, such as an outline or the same colour style as the other choice

title: The "older names" fold in the routine import does not say if it is open
what: When bringing routines in after a Hevy or Strong import, the row "N older names (not used for a year)" opens a hidden list. A screen reader is not told whether it is open or closed, and its arrow always points right, even when open.
expected: The screen reader says open or closed, and the arrow turns when the list is open.
who: members switching from Hevy or Strong
fix_line: Mark the row as open or closed for the screen reader and turn the arrow

title: A screen reader says nothing about the share picture before it is shared
what: The share sheet shows a preview of the workout, report or before/after picture, but the drawn picture carries no spoken description. A blind or low-vision member hears nothing about what is on the picture (title, kilos, records, gym name) before sending it to friends.
expected: The preview reads out a short summary of what the picture shows, for example the workout name, day, kilos lifted and records.
fix_line: Give the preview a spoken summary built from the same words drawn on the picture

title: Closing the Update routine question loses the change for good
what: After a workout that changed its routine, the summary asks once whether to update the routine. If the member taps Keep original, presses back or taps outside by mistake, the question is gone and never comes back, and the saved workout offers no Update routine action. The only way left is Save as routine, which makes a second copy instead of updating the routine they follow.
expected: After closing the question there is still a way to update the original routine from that workout, for example an Update routine action on the saved workout page or a line on the summary.
how_often: each time a routine workout changed
fix_line: Keep an Update routine action on the summary and the saved workout page after the question is closed

title: A screen reader cannot name the watch's big Done and Go buttons, and a greyed Done is not read at all
what: The big round Done button (a tick) and Go button (an arrow) show only a picture with no spoken name, so a screen reader user hears a button with no word. While Done cannot be used yet, it is not a button at all for the screen reader, and only its grey colour tells a sighted member it is off.
expected: Done and Go are read as 'Done, log this set' and 'Next exercise', and a Done that cannot be used yet is read as 'Done, not available'.
how_often: every set logged on the watch with a screen reader on
fix_line: Give the tick and arrow buttons a spoken name and keep the greyed Done as a button marked not available

title: Several watch buttons are much smaller than a finger
what: The screen is drawn on a 456-point plan scaled to the watch (about 0.42 to 0.5 finger units per point). 'Not now' is 46 points tall (about 21 units), 'Allow' and 'Open on phone' 52 points (about 24), the effort number tiles 64 points tall (about 29) and the effort Skip 80 points (about 36). Wear OS asks for at least 48.
expected: Every button on the watch is at least 48 finger units tall and wide, or has a touch area that big around it.
how_often: first launch, and every effort rating
fix_line: Make the touch area of these buttons at least 48 finger units, even where the drawn shape stays small

title: Most watch screens ignore the member's larger text setting
what: Words on the permission, no workout, workout saved, get the phone app, phone not connected and rest screens are drawn at one fixed size whatever text size the member chose. Only some words on the logging screens grow, and those stop at 1.24 times.
expected: Words grow with the member's text size (the big numbers may stay fixed), with the layout made to fit at the largest setting.
how_often: every time, for members with large text on
fix_line: Let the words on every watch screen grow with the text size setting, keeping only the big numbers fixed

title: 'Not now' on the watch's first screens looks like plain words
what: Under the filled Allow button, 'Not now' is white text with no outline or fill, so a first-time member cannot tell it is a button.
expected: 'Not now' has a visible outline or fill so it reads as a button.
fix_line: Draw 'Not now' as an outlined button

title: After 'Not now', the watch never offers heart rate or rest alerts again
what: Tapping 'Not now' on the heart rate or rest alerts screen hides it for good. The watch app has no other place to turn these on, and the heart rate line simply disappears, so the member is never told why or where to switch it on.
expected: A way back stays: for example a small 'Heart rate off, tap to turn on' line or a later reminder, so the member can still get what 'Not now' put off.
how_often: every member who taps Not now once
fix_line: Show a small tap-to-turn-on line where the heart rate would be, and offer rest alerts again later

title: The bottom quick bar on a gym's page and on the member site can be reached with the Tab key while it is hidden off screen
what: On a phone-width screen, the gym's web page and the member website have a bar at the bottom ('Become a member', 'Ask', 'Get the app'). When it is not wanted it is only slid below the screen. Its buttons stay in the Tab order and stay readable by a screen reader, so a keyboard or screen reader user lands on buttons that cannot be seen.
expected: While the bar is hidden, its buttons are skipped by the Tab key and by screen readers, as the gym-owner site already does with its own bar.
who: visitors who use a keyboard or a screen reader
how_often: every visit, before scrolling past the top
fix_line: Take the bar's buttons out of the Tab order and hide them from screen readers while the bar is off screen

title: On a gym's web page the keyboard focus ring is drawn in the gym's own colour, so it disappears on the gym-coloured signboard and bottom bar
what: The ring that shows which button the keyboard is on always uses the gym's chosen colour. The top signboard, the board headings and the bottom bar are painted in that same colour, so on 'Become a member', 'Ask' and the other signboard buttons the ring is the same colour as the background and cannot be seen.
expected: The focus ring always stands out from what is behind it, for example in the text colour on gym-coloured parts.
how_often: every time on the signboard and bottom bar
fix_line: Draw the focus ring in the signboard's text colour where the background is the gym's colour

title: On the gym-owner website the colour dots and the source numbers are too small to tap easily
what: The six round colour choices next to 'Type your gym's name' are 30 by 30 pixels, and the small source numbers after the big figures are 11-pixel links. Both are well under the usual 44-pixel finger size, so on a phone it is easy to hit the wrong one.
expected: Every tappable thing is at least about 44 pixels in each direction, or has that much tappable space around it.
how_often: every time they pick a colour or open a source
fix_line: Give the colour dots and the source numbers a bigger tappable area without changing how they look

title: On a tablet or small laptop, the gym's photos scroll sideways with no scroll bar or arrows, so most photos look missing
what: Between phone and full computer width, the gym's photos sit in one sideways row with the scroll bar hidden and no arrows. The only hint, 'N photos, swipe', means nothing with a mouse and is hidden from screen readers. A visitor with a mouse sees two photos and no sign that there are more.
expected: When photos scroll sideways, there is a visible way to move through them with a mouse or keyboard, such as arrows or a scroll bar.
who: visitors on a tablet or small laptop with a mouse
how_often: every visit at that screen width
fix_line: Show arrows or a thin scroll bar on the photo row when the screen is not a touch phone
